items.title: [E12-T5] Migration: deletion queue, steps, receipts and ledger tables
items.body:
## Summary
Create deletion_requests, erasure_steps, erasure_receipts and erasure_ledger with RLS, partial poll index and grants.

## Description
Implement deep-dive/05-1 5.11 and 5.13 in one Alembic migration (four tables). `deletion_requests (tenant_id, id)`: `scope` in (document, source, advisor, tenant), `subject_ref`, `reason` in (erasure, takedown, source_withdrawal, offboarding, source_kill), `requested_by`, `requested_at`, `status` in (pending, running, executed, windows_open, closed, failed), `claimed_at`, `attempts`, `parent_request_id` (reserved, nullable), a partial index `WHERE status = 'pending'`, and a unique index `(tenant_id, subject_ref) WHERE scope = 'source'` so the purge pull is idempotent on `(tenant_id, purge_id)`. `erasure_steps (tenant_id, request_id, store)`: `status`, `executed_at`, `rows_affected`, `probe_result`, `window_closes_at`, `swept_at`. `erasure_receipts (tenant_id, request_id, phase)`: phase 1 or 2, `receipt jsonb`, `hmac`, `gcs_uri`, `issued_at`. All three: ENABLE and FORCE RLS, policies use `current_setting('app.x')` without missing_ok. Grants per 5.13: INSERT on deletion_requests to `fa_app` only when `app.role = 'tenant_admin'` and tenant matches; `fa_worker` SELECT and UPDATE (status, claimed_at, attempts) on its own non-PUBLIC tenant; no INSERT for `fa_etl_public`; `erasure_steps` and `erasure_receipts` `fa_worker` SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE. Also grant `fa_worker` DELETE on the child tables listed in 4.19 (Postgres step order) and on `pseudonym_map`. Also create `erasure_ledger` (5.11): key `(tenant_id, doc_key, sha256)`, append-only, hashes only, columns `request_id`, `scope_type`, `requested_at`, `released_at`, `released_by`; for advisor and tenant scopes `doc_key` holds `subject:<salted hash>` and `sha256` is the empty string; ENABLE and FORCE RLS; `fa_worker` SELECT and INSERT, SELECT also to `fa_etl_public` and to the sink roles (outbox relay, bq-sink, ETL writers) because ingest and the sinks check tombstones with uncached point reads (E5-T15 helper), no DELETE for anyone, UPDATE of `released_at` and `released_by` only for the operator release command role, no `fa_app` grant (5.13). The `lineage_edges` table is not created here (E11); the uncached sink-guard helper is E5. Out of scope: any worker code.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the migration is applied to an empty database, when `alembic downgrade -1` then `upgrade head` run, then both succeed and `information_schema` shows the four tables with RLS forced.
- [ ] Given the leak matrix (L0), when role `fa_app` as tenant A inserts a `deletion_requests` row for tenant B, then it fails; as non-admin role for tenant A it also fails.
- [ ] Given `fa_etl_public`, when it tries INSERT on `deletion_requests`, then permission is denied (privilege test via role_table_grants).
- [ ] Given two inserts of scope `source` with the same `(tenant_id, subject_ref)`, then the second violates the unique index.
- [ ] Given `erasure_ledger`, when any role tries DELETE, or the release role UPDATEs a column other than `released_at` and `released_by`, then permission is denied; an INSERT of a duplicate `(tenant_id, doc_key, sha256)` fails, and the same key for another tenant succeeds (tenant-scoped); and `fa_etl_public`, the outbox relay, bq-sink and ETL writer roles can SELECT it but not INSERT/UPDATE (test `test_erasure_ledger_grants_for_sink_roles`).
- [ ] EXPLAIN of the poll query (status = 'pending' ORDER BY requested_at LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) uses the partial index on a 10k-row table.

## Architecture

items.title: [E1-T8] RLS v2 policies and grants for content tables
items.body:
## Summary
documents, chunks, suitability_rules and ingest_rejects have the own-or-PUBLIC read policies, own-tenant-only write policies, column grants and the fa_etl_public-only PUBLIC write.

## Description
Add an Alembic revision implementing overview 5.4 and the 5.3 grants for the content tables. `<PUBLIC>` is the `PUBLIC_TENANT_ID` uuid literal substituted by the migration; `fa_eval` policies use the `EVAL_TENANT_ID` literal. Policies call `current_setting('app.x')` without `missing_ok`, so an unset setting raises (fail closed).

Policies (policy text for `chunks` is the arch text; `documents` and `suitability_rules` are identical in shape, `suitability_rules` uses `min_tier_required`):
- `*_select_app TO fa_app FOR SELECT`: `(tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid OR tenant_id = '<PUBLIC>'::uuid) AND tier_required <= current_setting('app.tier')::int AND jurisdiction = ANY (string_to_array(current_setting('app.jurisdictions'), ','))`.
- `*_select_pipe TO fa_worker, fa_etl, fa_etl_public, fa_dbt FOR SELECT`: own tenant only.
- `*_ins_tenant`, `*_upd_tenant`, `*_del_tenant TO fa_worker`: own tenant and `tenant_id <> '<PUBLIC>'` (USING and WITH CHECK on UPDATE). `fa_etl` gets INSERT and UPDATE on `documents` with the same own non-PUBLIC clause, and SELECT on `chunks`.
- `*_all_public TO fa_etl_public FOR ALL`: USING and WITH CHECK `tenant_id = '<PUBLIC>'::uuid`.
- `fa_eval`: the `fa_app` policies with the tenant literal of the `eval` tenant plus PUBLIC reads.
- `ingest_rejects`: tenant match for the roles holding grants, no PUBLIC clause.
`fa_app` has no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE policy or grant on `chunks`, `documents`, `suitability_rules` ("document ACL changes and deletes are applied by the `acl-applier` worker (ADR-022)").

Grants per 5.3: `fa_app` SELECT only; `fa_worker` on `chunks` SELECT, INSERT, DELETE and UPDATE (`tier_required`, `jurisdiction`) only, on `documents` SELECT, INSERT, DELETE and UPDATE (`tier_required`, `jurisdiction`, `status`, `parser_version`), on `suitability_rules` SELECT, INSERT, DELETE, on `ingest_rejects` SELECT, INSERT; `fa_etl` SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE (`status`, `parser_version`, `bronze_uri`) on `documents` and SELECT on `chunks`; `fa_etl_public` write on the content tables; `fa_dbt` SELECT; `fa_eval` the `fa_app` grants. Never `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES` (partitions get no grants).

Out of scope: tenants/advisors (E1-T9), other tables (E1-T10), the full leak matrix (E1-T19, E1-T20).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a principal for tenant A (tier 2, jurisdictions US), when `fa_app` selects from `chunks` after `set_config(..., true)`, then it sees tenant A and PUBLIC rows only, never tenant B rows, never rows with `tier_required = 3`, never rows with `jurisdiction = 'EU'` (`tests/db/test_rls_content.py`, parametrised over `chunks`, `documents`, `suitability_rules`).
- [ ] Given `fa_app`, when it runs INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on `chunks`, `documents` or `suitability_rules`, then each fails with permission denied (no grant).
- [ ] Given `fa_worker` bound to tenant A, when it inserts a chunk with `tenant_id` = B, or with `tenant_id` = PUBLIC, then each raises a row-level-security violation; and when it updates `documents.title`, then it fails with permission denied (column grant).
- [ ] Given `fa_etl_public`, when it inserts a chunk into the PUBLIC tenant, then it succeeds; when it inserts into tenant A, then it raises a row-level-security violation.
- [ ] Given `fa_eval` with `app.tenant_id` set to tenant A, when it selects from `documents`, then it sees only `EVAL_TENANT_ID` and PUBLIC rows.
- [ ] Given no `app.tenant_id` set in the transaction, when `fa_app` selects from `chunks`, then it raises `unrecognized configuration parameter` (fail closed) and returns no rows.

## Architecture

- overview.md#5.3

- decisions.md#adr-004

None

## Size

items.title: [E6] ETL and data engineering
items.body:
## Summary
ETL and data engineering (phase 2: Product). Scope, ADRs and exit criteria are in the plan section below.

## Plan
- **Goal.** A replayable, idempotent pipeline from raw documents to tenant-scoped, redacted, embedded chunks and analytics.
- **Scope.**
  - Bronze (GCS by sha256); silver (Docling, Presidio, structure-aware chunking with Voyage token counts, Pandera, rejects; Parquet partitioned tenant / dt); contextual headers (Haiku batch, flag); suitability-rule extraction and validation; embed-indexer publishes (chunk identity is the unique 8-column key of deep-dive 05-1 §5.10 including `valid_from`, `parser_version` and `embed_model`; `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)` is a non-unique reuse index) and bumps `corpus_version` last.
  - Dagster assets / partitions run daemon-less as Cloud Run jobs from Scheduler, with Postgres run storage (`dagster` database, `fa_dagster`); `dagster dev` locally. Tenant stages run as worker consumers; PUBLIC (EDGAR 497K) runs all stages in-process in `etl-public` and publishes only analytics events. Synthetic per-tenant corpus.
  - dbt gold as `fa_dbt` (`security_invoker` views or incremental models, never full rebuilds); `dbt-bigquery` marts; BigQuery sink with per-tenant authorized views (primary) and row access policies (second layer).
  - ACL change as metadata UPDATE (applier from E5).
- **Arch sections.** deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md#4.7 to #4.11, deep-dive/04-1-key-flows.md#4.14 (flow 2), deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md#5.2, deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.8; ADR-014, ADR-016.
- **Dependencies.** E5.
- **Spikes first.** Docling on the 497K HTML and inline-XBRL tables (chunk sizes measured with Voyage `count_tokens`).
- **Done when.**
  - Re-running the same partition re-embeds zero unchanged chunks (count asserted); an ACL change updates metadata with zero embed calls.
  - Every Pandera failure appears in `ingest_rejects`; no raw document text exists outside GCS bronze (scan test of `documents`, `chunks`, events, BigQuery).
  - `suitability_rules` is populated and validated for the synthetic corpus; `lookup_suitability_rule` returns rows on a real DB.
  - dbt gold models pass the CI assertion that every tenant-schema table has RLS enabled, forced, with policies, and no dbt run does a full-table rebuild of a tenant table; only `fa_tenant_lookup` is `SECURITY DEFINER`.
  - The PUBLIC corpus is written only by `fa_etl_public` (test: a worker attempt is denied by policy and a PUBLIC event on a pipeline topic is sent to `dlq.v1`).
  - BigQuery tables are day-partitioned, clustered by `tenant_id`, with `maximum_bytes_billed` set; a tenant's authorized view returns only that tenant's rows.
  - Fixes G-07, G-39, G-62.

- **Round 4 changes (2026-11-02).**
  - Silver path is `silver/tenant_id=/doc_id=/version=` (was tenant / dt), so erasure deletes by prefix and a parser bump re-parses; chunk identity includes `valid_from` and `parser_version` (ADR-014 amended, ADR-027). Supersedes the "partitioned tenant / dt" wording and the "re-running the same partition re-embeds zero unchanged chunks" bullet: replay after a parser bump re-parses, and unchanged chunk hashes extend `valid_to` with no embed call.
  - Atomic publish: the indexer is the only writer of `chunks`; it embeds outside any transaction, then one transaction per document: advisory lock first, tombstone check, `contract_passed AND scan_passed`, insert or extend chunks, version `active`, cache purge, `processed_events`, `corpus_version` row last (ADR-028, R4-D5; one transaction per document). Every sink (`bq-sink`, silver, contextualizer, indexer) guards with the E5 ledger helper; the silver worker checks before and after writing Parquet.
  - Ingest scan stage in the silver worker: parse-time sanitiser (script and style, comments, hidden or off-screen text, zero-width and bidi characters), deterministic pattern list, then quarantine (`status=quarantined`, bytes under `quarantine/`, never silver or chunks). Model Armor document screening is added by E11 (ADR-036).
  - Quality: Pandera with `PANDERA_VALIDATION_DEPTH=SCHEMA_AND_DATA`; dbt `contract: enforced` on gold tables; Dagster blocking checks are advisory only (the atomic gate is the control; cross-run behaviour UNVERIFIED, tested here); BigQuery `max_time_travel_hours=48` on every dataset including dbt-created ones (idempotent repo-managed DDL plus an assertion); OpenLineage dropped (ADR-014 amended, ADR-034).
  - Validation (2026-11-07, ADR-039): BigQuery time travel is set by the project default `default_max_time_travel_hours = 48` (dbt sets no dataset options), with the per-dataset setting as an assertion (ADR-029 amended). Chunk identity and embedding generations follow ADR-035 as amended (R4-D19 M1).
  - Contextual headers are an ablation arm, default OFF; the baseline B0 is the free structural prefix (title plus section path) written by the chunker (ADR-016 amended). Presidio runs English only.
  - Real connectors move to E11; `source_observations` is E11's table.
  - Added to Done when: #1 with a test double that commits a tombstone immediately before the sink write (N interleavings: zero rows or objects; E12 repeats it with the real worker); #5 on synthetic poison (malformed HTML and PDF, a zip-bomb-like size, injection payloads: none indexed, all in quarantine or the DLQ, consumers continue); #8 (replay a fixture corpus twice after a parser bump: the hash equals a single run, zero resurrection); a planted bad row fails Pandera; the BigQuery `max_time_travel_hours` assertion.

## Architecture

- deep-dive/04-1-key-flows.md#4.14 (flow 2)
- deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md#5.2
- deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.8

- [ ] E6-T2 Scaffold the ETL package and daemon-less Dagster

- [ ] E6-T5 Silver transform: Docling parse, Presidio scrub, chunking
- [ ] E6-T6 Pandera validation, ingest_rejects and versioned silver Parquet
- [ ] E6-T7 silver worker role: consume bronze, emit silver, guard writes
- [ ] E6-T8 contextualizer: Haiku headers (default off), guarded sink
- [ ] E6-T9 Suitability-rule extraction, validation and lookup
- [ ] E6-T10 indexer: atomic per-document publish and lock order
- [ ] E6-T11 Replay, parser-bump and ACL-change tests with zero embed calls
- [ ] E6-T12 Dagster partitions and the etl job entrypoint
- [ ] E6-T13 etl-public: in-process EDGAR 497K pipeline as fa_etl_public
- [ ] E6-T14 Raw-text scan test across documents, chunks, events, BigQuery
- [ ] E6-T15 dbt project and Postgres gold models as fa_dbt
- [ ] E6-T16 CI assertions: tenant tables RLS and no dbt full rebuild
- [ ] E6-T17 BigQuery dataset: partitioned tables, views, 48 h time travel
- [ ] E6-T18 dbt-bigquery marts and the ingest_events feed

items.title: [E12-T6] Migration: source_purges and reconciliation tables
items.body:
## Summary
Create the PUBLIC source_purges table and the reconciliation manifest and findings tables with their grants.

## Description
Implement deep-dive/05-1 5.11 `source_purges (tenant_id = PUBLIC, purge_id)` with `source_id`, `reason`, `requested_at`; INSERT granted to `fa_etl_public` on the PUBLIC tenant only, SELECT to every runtime role under own-or-PUBLIC, no UPDATE or DELETE for anyone. Implement 5.12 `reconciliation_manifests (tenant_id, version_id, hop, parser_version)` with `hop` in (bronze, silver, chunks, bigquery), `n_chunks`, `chunk_set_hash`, `computed_at`, and `reconciliation_findings (tenant_id, id, pair, detail, status, opened_at)`. Both reconciliation tables: ENABLE and FORCE RLS, pipeline roles own tenant, `fa_etl_public` for PUBLIC, no `fa_app` grant (5.13). Out of scope: the reconcile job and the purge command.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the migration, when role `fa_etl_public` inserts a `source_purges` row for tenant PUBLIC, then it succeeds; for a firm tenant id it fails.
- [ ] Given tenant A under `fa_worker`, when it SELECTs `source_purges`, then it sees PUBLIC rows only, and an UPDATE or DELETE fails for every role (grants test).
- [ ] Given `fa_app`, when it SELECTs `reconciliation_manifests` or `reconciliation_findings`, then permission is denied.
- [ ] Given a manifest key `(tenant, version, hop, parser_version)` inserted twice, then the second violates the primary key; the same version with a new `parser_version` is accepted (parser bump re-baseline).

items.title: [E6-T4] Bronze asset: GCS by sha256, register documents, publish
items.body:
## Summary
Fetch source documents into immutable GCS bronze, register a documents row and publish docs.bronze.v1.

## Description
Arch (4.8 `etl`; 4.10; Flow 2): 'Dagster run of tenant bronze assets (fetch, GCS by sha256, register `documents`, publish `docs.bronze.v1`)'. Bucket `GCS_DATA_BUCKET`, object `bronze/{tenant_id}/{sha256}` holding raw immutable bytes plus source URL and fetch time (object metadata); skip upload if the object exists. Register `documents` (5.2): `title, doc_type, jurisdiction, tier_required, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, product_category, risk_level, source ('synthetic'|'edgar'), source_uri, bronze_uri, bronze_sha256, parser_version NULL, status 'active'`; unique `(tenant_id, bronze_sha256)` so re-registering is a no-op (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). No `raw_content` anywhere. Publish `docs.bronze.v1` keyed by tenant_id with the E5 envelope via the E5 idempotent producer; payload carries ids and bronze_uri only, never text. Runs as DB role `fa_etl` with `app.tenant_id` set. Asset is partitioned tenant x dt. Source adapter for synthetic corpus from E6-T3. Out of scope: EDGAR source (E6-T13).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a doc already in bronze, when the asset reruns, then no GCS write occurs and no new `documents` row (asserted by counting GCS puts and rows, integration with fake-gcs)
- [ ] Given a new doc, when materialized, then exactly one `docs.bronze.v1` message with key == envelope.tenant_id and no content field is produced (test on payload schema)
- [ ] Given `fa_etl` and tenant A context, when inserting a documents row for tenant B, then RLS denies it (test)
- [ ] `documents` has no column named raw_content/content (reuse E1-T17 assertion passes)

items.title: [E11-T4] Migration: source_registry and source_observations
items.body:
## Summary
Create the source registry and the append-only observations table with RLS and grants.

## Description
Alembic migration for two tables, owned by E11 (planning note: E11 to E13 tables are created by their owning epic).

Arch (deep-dive/05-1 section 5.9): `source_registry` key `(tenant_id, source_id)`; `connector` (`ecfr`, `sec`, `eurlex`, `legislation_gov_uk`, `fca_api`, `publisher`), `source_class` (`law`, `qa`, `fca_api`, `publisher`), `on_withdraw` (`retire`, `erase`), `cursor jsonb`, `overlap_s` default 172800, `last_listing_at`, `frozen boolean`, `frozen_reason`, `rate_limit_rps`, `enabled`. `source_observations` key `(tenant_id, id)`: append-only; `source_id` composite FK, `external_id`, `version_key`, `content_sha256`, `source_ts`, `observed_at` (DB clock, `clock_timestamp()`), `state` in (`present`, `revoked`, `withdrawn`, `pending`), `listing_run_id`; unique on `(source_id, external_id, version_key, content_sha256)`; index `(tenant_id, source_id, external_id, observed_at DESC)`; "No UPDATE or DELETE grant except the erasure of an erased source".

Add ENABLE + FORCE RLS with tenant-match policies in the pattern of E1-T8 (PUBLIC rows readable by every tenant per the "own-or-PUBLIC SELECT" rule only where the arch says so; `source_registry` for a firm source is that tenant's). Writers are the ETL roles only; `fa_app` gets no write.

Out of scope: `document_versions` (E11-T5), connector code.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the migration applied then `source_registry` and `source_observations` exist with the columns, check constraints on the enumerated values and the unique index of 5.9 (test `backend/tests/test_source_tables_schema.py::test_columns_and_unique_index`).
- [ ] Given `fa_etl` role when it tries UPDATE or DELETE on `source_observations` then it is denied; INSERT is allowed (test `test_observations_append_only_grants`, `integration`).
- [ ] Given a row of tenant A when tenant B's role selects `source_registry` then zero rows are returned; `relforcerowsecurity` is true for both tables (test `test_source_tables_rls_leak`, part of the L0 leak matrix).
- [ ] Given `alembic upgrade head` then `downgrade -1` then `upgrade head` the schema is identical (migration round-trip test).

items.title: [E1-T19] L0 leak matrix part 1: cross-tenant reads, writes, FK probes
items.body:
## Summary
A pytest leak-matrix harness proves cross-tenant read, insert, update, delete into PUBLIC, FK existence probes and fail-closed on every table, and reports leaks = 0.

## Description
Build the L0 leak matrix (deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md §5.4: "The write split and the PUBLIC rule are tested by the L0 leak matrix"; 8.5 leak-path controls). `tests/leak/` with a harness: seed tenants A, B and PUBLIC (plus advisors with different tiers and roles) through `fa_owner`; helper `as_role(role, principal_settings)` opening a connection as that role's login and running statements inside a transaction with `set_config(..., true)`. A result collector counts a *leak* whenever a forbidden statement succeeds or returns a foreign row; the suite fails if `leaks != 0` and prints `LEAKS=<n>` in the output.

Matrix cases in this ticket, over every tenant table (parametrised from `pg_class` so a new table without a case fails):
1. Cross-tenant read: for each role holding SELECT (`fa_app`, `fa_worker`, `fa_etl`, `fa_dbt`, `fa_eval`) bound to tenant A, selecting from each table returns no tenant B row.
2. Cross-tenant insert: for each role holding INSERT, inserting a row with tenant B's `tenant_id` while bound to A raises a row-level-security violation or permission denied.
3. Update and delete into PUBLIC: `fa_worker`, `fa_etl`, `fa_app` (where granted) cannot INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE rows with the PUBLIC `tenant_id`; only `fa_etl_public` can, and only for PUBLIC.
4. FK existence probes: as tenant A, inserting `chunks`, `conversations`, `escalations`, `acl_change_requests` rows referencing ids of tenant B's `documents` / `advisors` fails with a foreign-key violation whose message is the same as for a nonexistent id (no oracle) or a permission error; cross-tenant composite pairs `(A, id_of_B)` fail.
5. Fail-closed: with `app.tenant_id` unset (new transaction on a fresh connection), every SELECT on a tenant table by a policy-bound role raises an error and returns zero rows.

Out of scope: direct partition access, self-escalation, pooled reuse, EXPLAIN pruning and CI gate wiring (E1-T20).

Round 4 (ADR-039 M6, ADR-002 D13a): the matrix stays parametrised from `pg_class`, so tables added by later epics (`document_versions`, `source_registry`, `deletion_requests`, `pseudonym_map`, ...) enter it automatically and need a case. Case 3 is extended: `fa_etl_public` has NO INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on any firm tenant's table (including `deletion_requests`); the FCA purge is a pull model, so it writes only the PUBLIC `source_purges` rows. Tables not yet created by their epic are skipped by the parametrisation and covered when that epic's migration lands.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the matrix runs against the migrated schema, then `pytest tests/leak -k 'read or insert or public or fk or failclosed'` passes and its output contains `LEAKS=0`.
- [ ] Given a deliberately weakened policy in a negative test (e.g. `chunks_select_pipe` USING (true) in a scratch database), then the matrix reports `LEAKS` greater than 0 and the test asserting detection passes.
- [ ] Given a new table is added to the schema without a matrix case, then `tests/leak/test_coverage.py` fails (table list from `pg_class` must equal the set of tables covered).
- [ ] Given case 4 for a nonexistent id and for an id of tenant B, then the error class and SQLSTATE are identical for both (no existence oracle) or both permission denied.
- [ ] Given case 3, then `fa_etl_public` inserting into tenant A raises a row-level-security violation (the only PUBLIC writer cannot write tenants).
- [ ] Given every tenant table present in the schema, when `fa_etl_public` bound to PUBLIC attempts INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE of a row carrying a firm tenant's `tenant_id`, then each raises a row-level-security violation or permission denied, and the output still contains `LEAKS=0` (`tests/leak/test_public_writer.py::test_fa_etl_public_writes_no_firm_table`).

## Architecture
- deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.4
- deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.13

items.title: [E1-T5] Migration: content tables with LIST-partitioned chunks
items.body:
## Summary
documents, chunks (LIST by tenant), suitability_rules and ingest_rejects exist in the target shape with composite FKs, raw_content dropped, and the PUBLIC and DEFAULT partitions.

## Description
Add an Alembic revision (0002 or later; baseline 0001 is immutable) as `fa_owner` that replaces the MVP content tables with the target shape of deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md §5.2 and 5.5. The MVP `documents.raw_content` column is dropped (G-03: "No `raw_content` column"). The service has never been deployed, so the revision drops and recreates the MVP content tables without a data migration.

Tables, all `FORCE` + `ENABLE` RLS at creation, all with `tenant_id uuid NOT NULL`:
- `documents (tenant_id, id)`: columns per 5.2 (`title, doc_type, jurisdiction, tier_required CHECK 1..4, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, product_category, risk_level, source CHECK in (edgar, synthetic), source_uri, bronze_uri, bronze_sha256, parser_version, status CHECK in (active, superseded, deleted), created_at`); unique `(tenant_id, bronze_sha256)`; index `(tenant_id, doc_type, jurisdiction)`.
- `chunks (tenant_id, id)` `PARTITION BY LIST (tenant_id)`; columns per 5.2 including `embedding halfvec(1024)` and `tsv tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(context_header,'') || ' ' || content)) STORED`; composite FKs `(tenant_id, document_id)` to documents and `(tenant_id, parent_id)` self; identity unique `(tenant_id, document_id, provision_path, chunk_index, chunk_hash, valid_from, parser_version, embed_model)` (round 4, below). Indexes declared on the parent so each partition gets its own: HNSW on `embedding halfvec_cosine_ops` `m=16, ef_construction=64` partial `WHERE kind = 'child'`; GIN on `tsv`; btree `(tenant_id, document_id)`, `(tenant_id, parent_id)`, `(tenant_id, tier_required, jurisdiction)`.
- `suitability_rules (tenant_id, id)`: per 5.2, composite FK `(tenant_id, source_document_id)`, `client_risk_profile` CHECK 3 values (use the values already in the MVP schema).
- `ingest_rejects (tenant_id, id)`: per 5.2.
Partitions: one for the PUBLIC tenant (`chunks_public`) and a DEFAULT partition (`chunks_default`); rows in DEFAULT are a bug. Write a reusable function `src/db/partitions.create_chunks_partition(conn, tenant_id)` (partition name from the uuid, no `GRANT`) that E1-T11 reuses. The partitions are created without any grants.

If E1-T2's ADR changed the partition design, follow the ADR.

Out of scope: policies and grants (E1-T8), tenant partitions (E1-T11), changing the retrieval code that reads these tables (E3).

Round 4 (ADR-027, ADR-035, R4-D3, R4-D19 M1; deep-dive/05-1 section 5.10): (1) `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist` first, as `fa_owner`. Availability on Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 16 is UNVERIFIED: the migration fails with a clear message if the extension cannot be created, and the PR records the check on a Cloud SQL instance (or marks it open for E10). (2) `chunks` also carries `provision_path`, `chunk_index`, `kind`, `valid_from date NOT NULL`, `parser_version`, `embed_model`, `valid_range daterange NOT NULL`, `system_range tstzrange NOT NULL`, `is_current boolean GENERATED ALWAYS AS (upper_inf(valid_range)) STORED`, with CHECK `valid_from = lower(valid_range)`. The identity above is UNIQUE (it includes `embed_model`, so generations coexist); the old `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)` becomes a plain, non-unique index used to reuse vectors. (3) `create_chunks_partition(conn, tenant_id)` also executes, for the leaf it creates (the PUBLIC partition migration does the same for `chunks_public`), `ALTER TABLE chunks_<tenant> ADD CONSTRAINT chunks_<tenant>_no_overlap EXCLUDE USING gist (tenant_id WITH =, document_id WITH =, provision_path WITH =, chunk_index WITH =, kind WITH =, embed_model WITH =, valid_range WITH &&) WHERE (upper_inf(system_range))`. PostgreSQL 16 cannot declare an exclusion constraint on a partitioned parent, hence per leaf. The composite FKs to `document_versions` and the `documents` column changes of section 5.2 belong to E11-T4/E11-T5 (that epic owns `document_versions`); not here.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given `alembic upgrade head` on an empty database, then `tests/db/test_schema_content.py` passes: `chunks` has `relkind='p'` and `partstrat='l'`, partitions `chunks_public` and `chunks_default` exist, and `documents` has no column named `raw_content`.
- [ ] Given a chunk row whose `(tenant_id, document_id)` points to a document of another tenant, when inserted as `fa_owner`, then it raises a ForeignKeyViolation (composite FK; test).
- [ ] Given `create_chunks_partition(conn, <uuid>)` is called, then a partition bound to that uuid exists and `has_table_privilege` for `fa_app`, `fa_worker`, `fa_etl`, `fa_etl_public` and `fa_dbt` on it is false for every privilege (test).
- [ ] Given two rows with the same full 8-column identity, then the second insert raises a UniqueViolation; given text A (valid 2020-01-01 to 2021-01-01), text B, then text A again with `valid_from` 2022-01-01, the three rows insert with disjoint ranges and no violation (A-B-A test `tests/db/test_chunk_identity.py::test_aba_is_three_rows`).
- [ ] Given the PUBLIC partition, then `pg_indexes` shows an HNSW index with `halfvec_cosine_ops`, `m='16'`, `ef_construction='64'` and predicate `kind = 'child'`, a GIN index on `tsv`, and a NON-unique index on `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)` (`test_public_partition_indexes`).
- [ ] Given two current rows with the same `(tenant_id, document_id, provision_path, chunk_index, kind, embed_model)` and overlapping `valid_range`, when inserted into a leaf created by `create_chunks_partition`, then Postgres raises an exclusion violation (SQLSTATE 23P01); the same overlap with `system_range` closed (not `upper_inf`) is accepted; the same overlap with a different `embed_model` is accepted (`test_exclude_per_leaf`).

items.title: [E1-T9] RLS for tenants and advisors, and fa_tenant_lookup
items.body:
## Summary
tenants and advisors policies and grants are in place, advisors cannot self-escalate, and the single SECURITY DEFINER function fa_tenant_lookup exists.

## Description
Add an Alembic revision implementing the `tenants` and `advisors` items of overview 5.4 and the 5.3 grants.

`tenants`: `tenants_select_app TO fa_app FOR SELECT USING (id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid OR id = '<PUBLIC>'::uuid)`; `tenants_lookup TO fa_lookup FOR SELECT USING (true)`; `tenants_owner TO fa_owner` for SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE; `tenants_upd_worker TO fa_worker FOR UPDATE USING / WITH CHECK (id = app.tenant_id AND id <> <PUBLIC>)`; `tenants_upd_public TO fa_etl_public FOR UPDATE USING / WITH CHECK (id = <PUBLIC>)`. Column grants: `fa_app` SELECT on (`id`, `slug`, `corpus_version`, `acl_version`, `budgets`) only; `fa_lookup` SELECT on the columns the function returns plus `slug`; UPDATE limited to `corpus_version` and `acl_version` for `fa_worker` and to `corpus_version` for `fa_etl_public`.

`advisors`: SELECT `TO fa_app` when `tenant_id = app.tenant_id AND (id = app.user_id OR idp_uid = app.idp_uid OR app.role = 'tenant_admin')`; UPDATE `TO fa_app` only when `tenant_id = app.tenant_id AND app.role = 'tenant_admin'`, `WITH CHECK (tenant_id = app.tenant_id)`. Column grants: UPDATE on `tier, jurisdictions, licenses, role, status, entitlement_version` only (`tenant_id` immutable). No self-escalation: "an advisor cannot raise their own tier or role".

`fa_tenant_lookup(p_slug text DEFAULT NULL, p_idp_tenant_id text DEFAULT NULL)`: `SECURITY DEFINER`, owned by `fa_lookup` (not `fa_owner`), explicit `SET search_path`, returns `(id, display_name, idp_tenant_id)`, serves both slug discovery and the `idp_tenant_id` to `tenants.id` mapping (D14.4); `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC; GRANT EXECUTE ... TO fa_app;`. It is the only `SECURITY DEFINER` function allowed in the database. With both arguments NULL it returns no rows.

Out of scope: the HTTP endpoint (E1-T16), the principal that calls the function (E1-T14).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a principal of tenant A, when `fa_app` selects from `tenants`, then it sees exactly the tenant A row and the PUBLIC row; selecting a column outside the grant (e.g. `idp_tenant_id`) fails with permission denied; any UPDATE on `tenants` by `fa_app` fails with permission denied (`tests/db/test_rls_identity.py`).
- [ ] Given an advisor with `app.role = 'advisor'`, when it runs `UPDATE advisors SET tier = 4, role = 'tenant_admin' WHERE id = app.user_id`, then rowcount is 0 and the stored tier and role are unchanged.
- [ ] Given `app.role = 'tenant_admin'` of tenant A, when it updates the tier of an advisor of tenant A then it succeeds; of an advisor of tenant B then rowcount is 0; `UPDATE advisors SET tenant_id = ...` fails with permission denied.
- [ ] Given `fa_tenant_lookup(p_slug => 'acme')` called as `fa_app`, then it returns exactly the columns `id, display_name, idp_tenant_id`; called as `fa_worker` it fails with permission denied; `has_function_privilege('public', ...)` is false.
- [ ] Given `pg_proc`, then exactly one function with `prosecdef = true` exists in the app schemas, it is `fa_tenant_lookup`, and its owner is `fa_lookup` (test).
- [ ] Given `fa_tenant_lookup(NULL, NULL)` called as `fa_app`, then it returns zero rows (test).

items.title: [E11-T5] Migration: bitemporal document_versions with EXCLUDE
items.body:
## Summary
Create document_versions with the valid-time EXCLUDE constraint and the idempotency index.

## Description
Alembic migration for `document_versions`, created here by E11. Enable `btree_gist` (available on Cloud SQL).

Arch (5.9): key `(tenant_id, version_id)`; `doc_id` (composite FK to `documents`), `version_key`, `valid_range daterange NOT NULL` (half-open, UTC days), `valid_from_basis` (`source` or `observed`), `system_range tstzrange NOT NULL DEFAULT tstzrange(clock_timestamp(), NULL)`, `bronze_sha256`, `bronze_uri`, `content_hash`, `parser_version`, `attribution_text`, `scan_passed`, `contract_passed`, `quarantine_reason`, `released_by`, `status` in (`ingesting`, `active`, `superseded`, `revoked`, `withdrawn`, `quarantined`, `known_pending`, `erased`), `created_at`. Unpartitioned. Exactly:

```sql
ALTER TABLE document_versions ADD CONSTRAINT document_versions_no_overlap
  EXCLUDE USING gist (tenant_id WITH =, doc_id WITH =, valid_range WITH &&)
  WHERE (upper_inf(system_range) AND status NOT IN ('ingesting', 'quarantined', 'erased'));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX document_versions_idem ON document_versions
  (tenant_id, doc_id, version_key, bronze_sha256) WHERE upper_inf(system_range);
```

RLS and grants in the E1-T8 pattern; the indexer and `etl-public` roles write. Dates are UTC days; system time only via `clock_timestamp()`.

Out of scope: `reconcile_lineage` (E11-T9), the per-leaf EXCLUDE on `chunks` (partition-creation migration).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given two current rows of one document with overlapping `valid_range` and status `active` when the second is inserted then the EXCLUDE raises; the same overlap with status `quarantined` is allowed (test `test_no_overlap_constraint.py::test_overlap_rejected_for_active_only`).
- [ ] Given a row whose `system_range` is closed when a row with an overlapping `valid_range` is inserted then it succeeds, since only the current belief is constrained (test `test_historical_rows_unconstrained`).
- [ ] Given the same `(tenant, doc, version_key, bronze_sha256)` inserted twice with an open `system_range` then the unique index rejects the second (test `test_idempotency_index`).
- [ ] Given tenant A's row when tenant B's role queries then zero rows; `relforcerowsecurity` true (L0 leak matrix test).

items.title: [E6-T17] BigQuery dataset: partitioned tables, views, 48 h time travel
items.body:
## Summary
Create fa_analytics tables with partitioning, tenant clustering, authorized views, row policies and the project-default 48 h max time travel.

## Description
Arch (4.11, 5.8): dataset `fa_analytics`, tables `chat_audit`, `chat_usage`, `eval_events`, `gateway_audit`, `acl_changes`, `ingest_events`; 'day-partitioned, clustered by `tenant_id`; per-tenant authorized views (primary isolation) plus row access policies (second layer); `maximum_bytes_billed` on every query'. DDL as code in the repo (`etl/bq/schema.py` or `bigquery/` SQL, applied by an idempotent `jobs`-callable command) with BQ_DATASET and BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED; partition by `DATE(event_time)` with `require_partition_filter`; cluster by `tenant_id`; `ensure_tenant_view(tenant_id)` in a separate views dataset authorized on the base dataset; a row access policy per tenant; all query helpers pass `maximum_bytes_billed`. Subject-bearing tables (`chat_audit`, `chat_usage`, `eval_events`, `acl_changes`) have a `pseudonym_id` column and no text columns; no table holds FCA content or answer text (ADR-013 amended, ADR-026).

Round 4 (ADR-029 amended 2026-11-07, R4-D18 V2, ADR-039): BigQuery time travel is set by the PROJECT default: the DDL command runs `ALTER PROJECT ... SET OPTIONS (default_max_time_travel_hours = 48)` for the dataset region (idempotent), so every new dataset, including dbt-created ones, inherits it; dbt-bigquery sets NO dataset options (not documented). The per-dataset `max_time_travel_hours = 48` is kept only as a CHECK: the same command reads `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA_OPTIONS` for every dataset in the project and exits non-zero if any value differs. Out of scope: the bq-sink writer (E5-T14), onboarding hook wiring.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the applied DDL, when table metadata is read, then each of the 6 tables has `time_partitioning.type=DAY` and `clustering_fields[0]=='tenant_id'`; no column named answer, excerpt, question or text exists in any table (test).
- [ ] Given the DDL command run on a project whose default is unset, when finished, then the project default is 48 h and a dataset created afterwards (by a plain CREATE SCHEMA) reads `max_time_travel_hours = 48` (test_project_default_time_travel_48h; gated job on a real test project, since an emulator may not model it).
- [ ] Given a dataset whose time travel is 168 h, when the check runs, then it exits non-zero naming the dataset (negative control).
- [ ] Given rows for tenants A and B, when a query runs through tenant A's authorized view, then only tenant A rows return; a query without `maximum_bytes_billed` is rejected by the wrapper; running the DDL twice is a no-op.

items.title: [E6-T20] Ingest scan stage and quarantine in the silver worker
items.body:
## Summary
Add the parse-time sanitiser and deterministic pattern list to the silver worker and quarantine a failing version before anything reaches silver.

## Description
Implement the scan stage of 4.25 as a hook in the E6-T7 handler (in-process in `etl-public` for PUBLIC, E6-T13). Quote 4.25: 'Parse-time sanitiser: drop script and style, comments, hidden or off-screen text, zero-width and bidi characters, long base64 runs; keep a per-document diff count. Deterministic pattern list: instruction-override phrases, role markers, tool-call syntax, URLs outside an allow-list. ... Any failure: version `status = quarantined`, bytes under `quarantine/`, never silver, never chunks.' Sanitiser output replaces the parsed text; a diff count is stored. The pattern list is a versioned data file `etl/silver/scan_patterns.yaml`; the URL allow-list is a setting. A pattern hit or a sanitiser hard failure sets the `document_versions` row `status='quarantined'` and `scan_passed=false`, copies the bronze bytes to `quarantine/tenant_id=/doc_id=/version=/` in the data bucket, writes NOTHING to silver and creates no chunks, emits no `docs.silver.v1`, and the consumer continues with the next message. A pass sets `scan_passed=true`. Model Armor document screening (fail closed) is added to this stage by E11-T13; operator `release` and `reject` are E11-T12; the contract checks are E11-T11. Out of scope: classifier arms (ablation only).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a document with hidden text, zero-width characters and a script block, when scanned, then the sanitised text contains none of them and the diff count equals the number removed (unit test).
- [ ] Given a document containing an instruction-override phrase from the pattern list, when consumed by the silver worker, then the version is `quarantined` with scan_passed=false, the bytes exist under `quarantine/`, no silver object and no chunk exist, and the next message in the partition is processed (test_injected_document_quarantined).
- [ ] Given a clean document, when consumed, then scan_passed=true and processing continues unchanged.
- [ ] Given a URL outside the allow-list in the text, when scanned, then it is a pattern hit; given an allow-listed URL, it passes (parametrised test).

items.title: [E11-T9] reconcile_lineage: idempotent version and chunk reconcile
items.body:
## Summary
Implement the one function that reconciles late, out-of-order, withdrawn and replayed versions.

## Description
Implement `reconcile_lineage(document_id)` in `backend/src/lineage/reconcile.py`, called by the indexer (tenant path) and `etl-public` (PUBLIC path) so the two paths cannot drift.

Arch (4.16): input = every non-withdrawn, non-quarantined `document_versions` row of the document in `valid_range` order plus its silver Parquet. Output = the target chunk set keyed by chunk identity `(tenant_id, document_id, provision_path, chunk_index, chunk_hash, valid_from, parser_version, embed_model)`. Applied as a diff in ONE transaction under the document's advisory lock (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(tenant_id, doc_id))`, lock order of 4.17: advisory lock first, tenant `corpus_version` row last): insert missing rows (embed only hashes with no vector for the active `embed_model`), extend `valid_range` where the same chunk hash continues into the next version (no embed call), close superseded rows (`valid_range` upper and `system_range` upper set, never overwritten), delete extras. Swap order: close old rows' `system_range`, then insert new ones. `valid_from` and `parser_version` are in the identity so a replay after a parser fix re-parses and A-B-A text is two rows with disjoint ranges. `valid_from_basis='observed'` for UK sources (observed date as `valid_from`).

Out of scope: the indexer's publish transaction steps around it (E6-T10), erasure (E12).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given versions v3, v1, v2 fed in all 6 permutations then the final valid-time line and chunk set hash are identical (#11; test `backend/tests/lineage/test_reconcile.py::test_all_permutations_identical`, PR).
- [ ] Given text A, then B, then A again then two A rows exist with disjoint `valid_range` and no unique violation (#8; test `test_aba_reversion_representable`, PR).
- [ ] Given `reconcile_lineage` run twice then the chunk-set hash equals a single run and zero embed calls are made on the second run (test `test_replay_twice_idempotent`).
- [ ] Given a parser bump then replay then no chunk of the old parse is retrievable by `search` and the old parse is closed in the same transaction as the new one is opened (#8; test `test_parser_bump_replay_no_old_chunks`, PR).
- [ ] Given an unchanged chunk hash across two versions then `valid_range` is extended and the embed client mock is not called (test `test_unchanged_chunk_extends_range_without_embed`).

items.title: [E1] Identity and tenancy
items.body:
## Summary
Identity and tenancy (phase 1: Platform core). Scope, ADRs and exit criteria are in the plan section below.

## Plan
- **Goal.** A caller is a verified person in a tenant, and the database refuses every cross-tenant read and write.
- **Scope.**
  - First ticket: verify the `firebase.tenant` claim name against a real Identity Platform tenant (D14.17).
  - `tenants` and `advisors`; Identity Platform multi-tenancy (one IdP tenant per firm); project-level ID-token verification with firebase-admin and the `firebase.tenant` check (`auth`, ADR-032); `principal` with the 60 s entitlements cache and `entitlement_version`; IdP tenant provisioning script (Terraform comes in E10).
  - Schema for the whole target model in the baseline migration: `documents.raw_content` is dropped here (G-03 early); `acl_change_requests`, `eval_scores`, `turn_events`, `outbox` and `processed_events` tables are created (the outbox is written in E4 and relayed in E5).
  - RLS v2 on all tables: ENABLE + FORCE, SELECT own-or-PUBLIC, writes own-tenant only, PUBLIC writable only by `fa_etl_public`; roles `fa_app` (SELECT only on content), `fa_worker`, `fa_etl`, `fa_etl_public`, `fa_dbt`, `fa_owner`, `fa_lookup`, `fa_maint`, `fa_eval`, `fa_dagster`; `tenants` policies; `advisors` admin-only UPDATE; `advisor_id` owner clauses; `set_config(..., true)` in short transactions; composite FKs.
  - LIST partitions of `chunks` and monthly partitions of `messages` with no partition grants; tenant onboarding in the `migrate` job; `maintenance` job schema and role (scheduling in E10); startup / readiness role and RLS assertions.

items.body:
### Self Checks

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Language Policy](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/issues/1542).
- [x] This is only for bug report, if you would like to ask a question, please head to [Discussions](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/discussions/categories/general).
- [x] I have searched for existing issues [search for existing issues](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/issues), including closed ones.
- [x] I confirm that I am using English to submit this report, otherwise it will be closed.
- [x] 【中文用户 & Non English User】请使用英语提交，否则会被关闭 ：）
- [x] Please do not modify this template :) and fill in all the required fields.

### Dify version

Source main `f73b1807c0a455e8d04bac61651f8f6071079047` (1.19.0).

### Cloud or Self Hosted

Self Hosted (Source). Reproduced through the production extractor on Windows, Python 3.13.9 and python-docx 1.2.0, with a real local DOCX and an unbound SQLAlchemy Session. No deployed service or model call.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a DOCX with a BEFORE paragraph, a paragraph wrapped in `w:sdt/w:sdtContent` containing CONTROL_VALUE, and an AFTER paragraph. Run `WordExtractor(path, tenant_id, user_id, session=session).extract()`.

A small fixture can be created with python-docx:

```python
doc = Document()
doc.add_paragraph("BEFORE")
paragraph = doc.add_paragraph("CONTROL_VALUE")
parent = paragraph._p.getparent()
control = OxmlElement("w:sdt")
display = OxmlElement("w:sdtContent")
parent.replace(paragraph._p, control)
display.append(paragraph._p)
control.append(display)
doc.add_paragraph("AFTER")
doc.save(path)
```

Import Document from docx and OxmlElement from docx. Reopening the saved file confirms CONTROL_VALUE remains in its document XML.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The visible control value is extracted between BEFORE and AFTER. The same applies to inline controls and controls around cell paragraphs.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Actual production-entry outputs:

```text
block:  'BEFORE\nAFTER'
inline: 'BEFORE\n\n\nAFTER'
cell:   'BEFORE\n|  |\n| --- |\nAFTER'
```

The block traversal skips wrapped paragraphs/tables; inline and cell parsing also skip wrapped content.

Proposed scope: expand only content-control display containers in the loaded main-document body, then reuse existing paragraph, table, image and hyperlink parsing. Keep the source file intact and omit control properties, dropdown alternatives and data-binding evaluation.

This is separate from #42832 (run whitespace), #42808 (nested-table images), and #43439 (repeated cell paragraphs); their patches have been checked. Regression fixtures cover block, inline, cell, nested, empty and rich-content controls.

items.title: [E12-T19] purge_source pull model: tenant erasure-worker polls source_purges
items.body:
## Summary
Each firm tenant's erasure-worker enqueues its own source request from a PUBLIC purge row and erases quoted FCA text.

## Description
The command and the PUBLIC-side purge (bump `source_epoch`, write `source_purges`, suspend the connector) are E11; this ticket owns the pull. In every erasure-worker run, under THAT tenant's `fa_worker` role, SELECT `source_purges` rows not yet handled and INSERT its own `deletion_requests` row (scope `source`, source `fca_api`, `subject_ref` = `purge_id`), idempotent on `(tenant_id, purge_id)` (unique index of E12-T5; use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). Then execute it like any request: delete the messages and cached answers that quote FCA text (found via `retrieval_chunk_ids` and `source_document_ids` against the purged documents), with the usual steps and receipt. There is no cross-tenant write and no cross-tenant role (ADR-002 D13a, ADR-039). FCA content never entered Kafka or BigQuery, so those stores need no step. A stopped tenant catches up at its next run (`demo-up` runs the erasure job first). Out of scope: PUBLIC erasure, the drill schedule (quarterly, ops).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given fixtures with 2 firm tenants and a `source_purges` row, when each tenant's worker runs once, then each has exactly one `deletion_requests` row for that `purge_id`, and re-running adds no row (#15; idempotency).
- [ ] Given messages and cached answers quoting FCA text in firm A, when the request executes, then they are gone and a receipt is issued; messages not citing FCA are untouched (#15).
- [ ] Given the L0 leak matrix, then `fa_etl_public` has no INSERT on any firm `deletion_requests` and no cross-tenant role exists (grants test).
- [ ] Given a tenant worker that was stopped during the purge, when it starts later, then it enqueues and executes the pending purge (catch-up test).
- [ ] Given the Kafka and BigQuery fixtures, then they contain no FCA text or chat answer text after the purge (absence scan, #15).

items.title: [E6-T5] Silver transform: Docling parse, Presidio scrub, chunking
items.body:
## Summary
Implement the pure silver transform that turns a bronze document into redacted, structure-aware chunks carrying the fields of the chunk identity.

## Description
Arch (4.7 `silver`): 'Docling parse, Presidio scrub, structure-aware chunking (256-512-token children, ~1k-token parents, token counts from Voyage `count_tokens`)'. Build `etl/silver/transform.py`: `transform(doc_bytes, doc_meta) -> list[Chunk]` where Chunk has `kind` (child|parent), `chunk_index`, `parent_ref`, `content` (redacted), `provision_path` (the structural path: section path of the document), `token_count`, `chunk_hash` (sha256 of the redacted content plus provision_path, stable across runs), `context_header`, plus ACL fields copied from the document (`tier_required, jurisdiction, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, source_title`).

Round 4 (ADR-027, ADR-016 amended, deep-dive 05-1 §5.10): (1) The chunk identity is the unique 8-column key `(tenant_id, document_id, provision_path, chunk_index, chunk_hash, valid_from, parser_version, embed_model)`; the transform therefore takes `valid_from` (from `doc_meta`, the version's start of validity) and `parser_version` (a constant bumped when the parser or chunker changes) and stamps both on every Chunk; `chunk_hash` does NOT include them (so unchanged text keeps its hash across versions and parser bumps and vectors can be reused). (2) Baseline B0 (ADR-016 amended): the chunker writes the free structural prefix, 'title plus section path', into `context_header` for every child chunk; contextual headers from Haiku are an ablation arm and OFF by default. (3) Presidio runs English only; no DE/FR PII claim is made (the E4-T2 spike measures it). Scrub before anything is written. Use the chunk-size findings and Docling version from docs/adr/docling-497k.md. Voyage `count_tokens` is called through an injectable client. Out of scope: Pandera, Parquet, Kafka (E6-T6/T7), Haiku headers (E6-T8).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the planted-PII manifest from E6-T3, when a document is transformed, then no planted PII string appears in any chunk content (test).
- [ ] Given a doc, when transformed twice, then the chunk_hash list is identical; given the same doc with a bumped `parser_version`, the chunk_hash list is still identical but every Chunk carries the new parser_version and the given `valid_from` (test_chunk_identity_fields).
- [ ] Given a child chunk, when its `context_header` is read, then it equals 'title > section path' of its provision (B0 structural prefix) and contains no LLM-generated text (test).
- [ ] Child chunks have token_count in 256..512 except a final short chunk per section; parents <= 1100 (property test over the synthetic corpus); each child references a parent present in the output.

items.title: eval: consider ClickHouse as primary store for billing analytics
items.body:
## Background

The current stack stores FOCUS 1.2 billing line items in PostgreSQL (`billing_line_items` table, 40+ columns, indexed on `billingPeriodStart/End`). This works for early development but PostgreSQL is an OLTP row-store — as billing data volumes grow into hundreds of millions or billions of rows, full-period aggregation queries will become the dominant performance bottleneck.

ClickHouse is a purpose-built columnar OLAP database with an Apache 2.0 licence that has become the de-facto standard for real-time billing and cost analytics at scale. Its design maps naturally to FOCUS billing data.

## Why ClickHouse fits FOCUS billing data

FOCUS 1.2 uses an **append-only correction model**: when a cloud provider discovers a billing error, it emits a new row with `ChargeClass = 'Correction'` — the original row is never mutated. This means billing data is structurally immutable from ingestion onward, which is a perfect fit for ClickHouse's MergeTree engine (which is designed for immutable sorted parts). ClickHouse's known weakness — expensive async mutations — is irrelevant for correction-model data.

Query patterns (aggregating `EffectiveCost` over time ranges, grouped by `ServiceName`, `ResourceId`, `Provider`, filtered by `BillingPeriod`) are exactly the columnar scan patterns ClickHouse is vectorised to execute.

Published benchmarks and real-world migrations show:
- 10–100x query latency reduction vs PostgreSQL on large billing datasets
- 10–30x storage compression (LZ4/ZSTD per-column codecs)
- Sub-second aggregations over billions of rows on modest hardware

## ClickHouse limitations to evaluate

- **Mutations are expensive and async.** `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE/DELETE` rewrites entire data parts in the background. No transactional consistency during mutation. This is a non-issue for billing data (append-only), but matters for any metadata co-located in ClickHouse.
- **Not suitable for OLTP.** User accounts, tenant configs, cost allocation rules, and workflow state require frequent updates and transactional guarantees — these must remain in PostgreSQL.
- **Operational complexity.** Self-hosting ClickHouse on Kubernetes (via the Altinity operator) requires managing ClickHouse Keeper (the ZooKeeper replacement), replication topology, and shard configuration. ClickHouse Cloud eliminates this at a cost premium.

## Recommended architecture: PostgreSQL + ClickHouse hybrid

| Data type | Store | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Billing line items (FOCUS) | ClickHouse | Columnar, analytical, append-only model, 10–100x query performance |
| App data (users, tenants, rules) | PostgreSQL (managed) | OLTP, full TypeORM/NestJS compatibility, CRUD/ACID |

The split is clean: the billing ingestion service writes directly to ClickHouse (dual-write, not routed through PostgreSQL). NestJS queries PostgreSQL for app state and ClickHouse for cost analytics via separate connection pools. No CDC or cross-system sync required for the core use case.

## Multi-tenancy in ClickHouse

Three patterns are supported; the recommended progression:

1. **Shared table with `tenant_id` in partition and primary key + ClickHouse row policies** — simplest to operate, good for early scale. Row policies transparently append `WHERE tenant_id = ...` at the database layer.
2. **Separate database per tenant** (`billing_acme`, `billing_globocorp`) — per-tenant TTL, partitioning, and data retention policies; clean GDPR deletion story (drop database). Suitable for large or regulated tenants.
3. **Separate cluster per tenant** — only for strict data residency requirements.

## Deployment options

- **ClickHouse Cloud** (recommended for early stage): managed, separated compute+storage, auto-pausing, no ZooKeeper/Keeper management. Note: 2025 pricing revision introduced egress fees — factor this into long-term cost modelling.
- **Altinity Kubernetes Operator** (v0.26, Apache 2.0): production-proven self-hosted K8s deployment, manages `ClickHouseInstallation` CRDs, rolling upgrades, replica management. Appropriate once the team has K8s DevOps capacity.

## Application integration

ClickHouse exposes an HTTP interface and a native TCP protocol. The `@clickhouse/client` Node.js SDK (official, maintained by ClickHouse Inc.) provides a typed query API. Billing queries are analytical SQL — TypeORM is not needed (and not appropriate) for ClickHouse; use the SDK directly in a `ClickHouseBillingRepository` service.

## Alternatives considered

- **TimescaleDB** (PostgreSQL extension with columnar compression and hypertables): viable up to ~100M rows with 10–100x query speedup over vanilla PostgreSQL. Simpler stack (one database). Does not close the performance gap for multi-billion-row datasets or sub-second interactive dashboards. Consider as a fallback if a single-database constraint is hard.
- **PostgreSQL with pg_partman + indexing**: reasonable for the current dataset; will not scale to the analytical query patterns expected in a production FinOps platform.

## Tasks

- [ ] Benchmark current PostgreSQL query performance on a representative billing dataset (1M, 100M rows)
- [ ] Evaluate ClickHouse Cloud vs self-hosted (Altinity operator) based on team capacity and cost
- [ ] Design ClickHouse schema for `billing_line_items` (partition by `toYYYYMM(billingPeriodStart)`, primary key `(tenant_id, billingPeriodStart, provider, serviceCategory)`)
- [ ] Implement `@clickhouse/client` adapter in billing ingestion service (replace/parallel to TypeORM insert)
- [ ] Implement ClickHouse row policies for tenant isolation (or per-database isolation if required)
- [ ] Migrate existing billing ingestion endpoint to write directly to ClickHouse
- [ ] Evaluate whether TimescaleDB is an acceptable interim step before committing to the hybrid stack
- [ ] Decide on multi-tenancy isolation level (shared table vs per-database) and document the decision

---
## Deutsche Fassung

## Hintergrund

Der aktuelle Stack speichert FOCUS-1.2-Abrechnungspositionen in PostgreSQL – Tabelle `billing_line_items` mit mehr als 40 Spalten und Indizes auf `billingPeriodStart/End`. Das funktioniert in der frühen Entwicklung, PostgreSQL ist jedoch ein zeilenorientierter OLTP-Speicher. Wenn das Abrechnungsvolumen auf Hunderte Millionen oder Milliarden Zeilen anwächst, werden Aggregationsabfragen über vollständige Perioden zum dominierenden Leistungsengpass.

ClickHouse ist eine speziell entwickelte spaltenorientierte OLAP-Datenbank unter Apache 2.0 und hat sich als De-facto-Standard für Echtzeit-Abrechnungs- und Kostenanalysen im großen Maßstab etabliert. Ihr Design passt natürlich zu FOCUS-Abrechnungsdaten.

## Warum ClickHouse zu FOCUS-Abrechnungsdaten passt

FOCUS 1.2 verwendet ein **Append-only-Korrekturmodell**: Entdeckt ein Cloud-Provider einen Abrechnungsfehler, erzeugt er eine neue Zeile mit `ChargeClass = 'Correction'`; die ursprüngliche Zeile wird nie verändert. Abrechnungsdaten sind damit ab der Datenübernahme strukturell unveränderlich – ideal für die MergeTree Engine von ClickHouse, die auf unveränderliche sortierte Teile ausgelegt ist. Die bekannte ClickHouse-Schwäche teurer asynchroner Mutationen spielt für dieses Korrekturmodell keine Rolle.

Abfragemuster wie die Aggregation von `EffectiveCost` über Zeiträume, gruppiert nach `ServiceName`, `ResourceId` oder `Provider` und gefiltert nach `BillingPeriod`, entsprechen genau den spaltenorientierten Scans, die ClickHouse vektorisiert ausführt.

Veröffentlichte Benchmarks und reale Migrationen zeigen:
- 10- bis 100-fach niedrigere Abfragelatenzen als PostgreSQL bei großen Abrechnungsdatensätzen,
- 10- bis 30-fache Speicherkompression durch spaltenspezifische LZ4-/ZSTD-Codecs,
- Aggregationen über Milliarden Zeilen in weniger als einer Sekunde auf moderater Hardware.

## Zu bewertende Einschränkungen von ClickHouse

- **Mutationen sind teuer und asynchron.** `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE/DELETE` schreibt ganze Datenteile im Hintergrund neu; währenddessen besteht keine transaktionale Konsistenz. Für Append-only-Abrechnungsdaten unproblematisch, aber relevant für gemeinsam gespeicherte Metadaten.
- **Nicht für OLTP geeignet.** Benutzerkonten, Mandantenkonfigurationen, Kostenverteilungsregeln und Workflow-Zustand benötigen häufige Updates und Transaktionsgarantien; sie müssen in PostgreSQL verbleiben.
- **Betriebliche Komplexität.** Selbst gehostetes ClickHouse auf Kubernetes mit Altinity Operator erfordert Verwaltung von ClickHouse Keeper, Replikationstopologie und Sharding. ClickHouse Cloud vermeidet dies gegen einen Preisaufschlag.

## Empfohlene Architektur: Hybrid aus PostgreSQL und ClickHouse

| Datentyp | Speicher | Begründung |
|---|---|---|
| Abrechnungspositionen – FOCUS | ClickHouse | spaltenorientiertes analytisches Append-only-Modell und 10- bis 100-fache Abfrageleistung |
| App-Daten – Benutzer, Mandanten, Regeln | verwaltetes PostgreSQL | OLTP, vollständige TypeORM-/NestJS-Kompatibilität und CRUD/ACID |

Die Trennung ist klar: Der Ingestion Service schreibt direkt nach ClickHouse – Dual Write, nicht über PostgreSQL. NestJS fragt PostgreSQL für App-Zustand und ClickHouse über getrennte Connection Pools für Kostenanalysen ab. Für den Kernanwendungsfall sind weder CDC noch systemübergreifende Synchronisierung erforderlich.

## Multi-Tenancy in ClickHouse

Drei unterstützte Muster mit empfohlener Entwicklung:

1. **Gemeinsame Tabelle mit `tenant_id` in Partition und Primärschlüssel sowie ClickHouse Row Policies:** einfachster Betrieb, gut für frühe Skalierung. Row Policies ergänzen auf Datenbankebene transparent `WHERE tenant_id = ...`.
2. **Eigene Datenbank pro Mandant** wie `billing_acme` oder `billing_globocorp`: mandantenspezifische TTL, Partitionierung und Aufbewahrung; saubere DSGVO-Löschung durch Löschen der Datenbank. Geeignet für große oder regulierte Mandanten.
3. **Eigener Cluster pro Mandant:** nur bei strikten Anforderungen an Datenresidenz.

## Deployment-Optionen

- **ClickHouse Cloud – für die Frühphase empfohlen:** verwaltet, getrennte Compute- und Storage-Ressourcen, Auto-Pause, keine Verwaltung von ZooKeeper oder Keeper. Die Preisänderung 2025 führte Egress-Gebühren ein; diese in langfristige Kostenmodelle einbeziehen.
- **Altinity Kubernetes Operator – Version 0.26, Apache 2.0:** produktionserprobtes selbst gehostetes K8s-Deployment mit Verwaltung von `ClickHouseInstallation`-CRDs, Rolling Upgrades und Replikaten. Sinnvoll, sobald das Team ausreichende K8s-DevOps-Kapazität besitzt.

## Anwendungsintegration

ClickHouse bietet HTTP und ein natives TCP-Protokoll. Das offizielle Node.js SDK `@clickhouse/client` stellt eine typisierte Query-API bereit. Abrechnungsabfragen sind analytisches SQL; TypeORM wird für ClickHouse weder benötigt noch empfohlen. Das SDK direkt in einem Service `ClickHouseBillingRepository` verwenden.

## Bewertete Alternativen

- **TimescaleDB:** PostgreSQL-Erweiterung mit spaltenorientierter Kompression und Hypertables; bis etwa 100 Millionen Zeilen tragfähig, mit 10- bis 100-facher Beschleunigung gegenüber einfachem PostgreSQL. Einfacherer Stack, aber bei Milliarden Zeilen oder interaktiven Dashboards unter einer Sekunde bleibt eine Leistungslücke. Als Rückfalloption bei harter Ein-Datenbank-Vorgabe erwägen.
- **PostgreSQL mit pg_partman und Indizes:** für den aktuellen Datensatz vernünftig, skaliert aber nicht auf die analytischen Abfragemuster einer produktiven FinOps-Plattform.

## Aufgaben

- [ ] Aktuelle PostgreSQL-Abfrageleistung mit repräsentativen Datensätzen von einer Million und 100 Millionen Zeilen benchmarken.
- [ ] ClickHouse Cloud und selbst gehosteten Altinity Operator anhand Teamkapazität und Kosten vergleichen.
- [ ] ClickHouse-Schema für `billing_line_items` entwerfen: Partition nach `toYYYYMM(billingPeriodStart)`, Primärschlüssel `(tenant_id, billingPeriodStart, provider, serviceCategory)`.
- [ ] Adapter mit `@clickhouse/client` im Ingestion Service implementieren – als Ersatz oder parallel zu TypeORM Insert.
- [ ] ClickHouse Row Policies für Mandantenisolation implementieren oder bei Bedarf Datenbanken trennen.
- [ ] Bestehenden Ingestion-Endpunkt auf direktes Schreiben nach ClickHouse migrieren.
- [ ] Bewerten, ob TimescaleDB als Zwischenschritt vor dem hybriden Stack akzeptabel ist.
- [ ] Isolationsniveau für Multi-Tenancy festlegen – gemeinsame Tabelle oder eigene Datenbank – und Entscheidung dokumentieren.

items.title: ETL fase 3 — fornecedor, profissional e produto: o indice de preco nao tem onde pousar
items.body:
## O que foi pedido, e o que a régua achou

O prompt pede a **"fase 1 do ETL"**: clientes, fornecedores, profissionais, produtos + variantes +
preço de tabela + índice, com script no repo, idempotente, dry-run primeiro, e relatório para o
user **antes** de qualquer carga real. Banco de produção virgem; popular é decisão do user.

Três coisas mudaram de figura ao medir:

1. **A numeração colide com a que o repo já usa.** `scripts/etl/LEIA-ME.md` chama de *fase 1* o
   RBAC (api#137, PR #142) e de *fase 2* o cadastro de cliente (PR #168, mergeada). O bloco de
   cadastros que o prompt chama de "fase 1" é, aqui, **a fase 3**. Esta issue usa a numeração do
   repositório e registra a equivalência para que os dois nomes não virem dois trilhos.
2. **Cliente já está entregue** — 9.322 linhas, com dry-run, idempotência e 42 casos de bateria.
   O gap é fornecedor, profissional, produto, variante e preço.
3. **O índice de preço não tem onde pousar.** Medido abaixo. Ele sai do escopo desta issue e vira
   nota, não tabela inventada.

**Entrega desta issue: ZERO código.** Nenhuma branch, nenhum commit. O que segue é a medição.

---

## Como foi medido

| | |
|---|---|
| Fonte do legado | `cabinet-erp-web/docs/legado/schema/bdprincipal-{linhas,colunas,fks}.csv` e `dbml/softlux-completo.dbml` |
| Contagens | `bdprincipal-linhas.csv`, medidas na extração — não estimadas |
| Larguras | **`dbml/`**, que conta CARACTERES; `-colunas.csv` conta BYTES e `nvarchar` gasta dois |
| Destino | `origin/main` do api: `src/core/db/schema.gerado.ts` (foto do banco) e as 55 migrações |
| Contrato | via api#114, que já mediu a superfície de preço na `main` do web |

Só `bdprincipal`. `bdprodutos` é staging descartável e não entra.

---

## §1 — O escopo, medido linha a linha

| Tabela do legado | Linhas | Destino no Cabinet | Camada | Situação |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `Clientes` | 9.322 | `partners` + `partner_tenant` | ORG + empresa | **entregue** (PR #168) |
| `fornecedor` | 868 | `partners.is_supplier` + `partner_tenant` | ORG + empresa | falta |
| `Indicacoes` | 1.316 | `partners.is_professional` + `partner_tenant` | ORG + empresa | falta |
| `produtos` | 108.992 | `products` | **ORG** | falta |
| `Preco_Produto` | 169.764 | `product_variants` + `product_tenant` | ORG + empresa | falta |
| `Acabamento` | 248 | `finishes` | ORG | falta |
| `unidades` | 7 | `units_of_measure` | ORG | falta |
| `Indice_preco` | 376 | — | — | **sem destino (§3)** |
| `Indice_precoGrupoUsuario` | 2.059 | — | — | **sem destino (§3)** |

Fora de escopo, declarado: `ProdutosFornecedores` (108.604 → `product_suppliers`), venda/orçamento
(`Venda`, 34.136, discriminada por `Ven_Tipo`), estoque, financeiro.

---

## §2 — O achado que decide a forma: variante não é tabela no legado

`product_variants` é `(product_id, finish, size)` com `uq_product_variants_produto_acabamento_tamanho`.
No Softlux **não existe tabela de variante**: quem carrega o par produto×acabamento é a linha de
`Preco_Produto` — `Pre_Codnosso` + `Pre_Acabamento` + `Tam_codigo`. Daí 169.764 linhas de preço
para 108.992 produtos: **1,56 variante por produto**.

E o preço não mora na variante: mora em `product_tenant (tenant_id, variant_id, price_cents)`.
Consequência mecânica — **uma linha de `Preco_Produto` vira DUAS linhas em camadas diferentes**:

- a **variante**, no ORG, deduplicada entre as empresas;
- o **preço**, por empresa, recortado por `Emp_codigo`.

Ler `Preco_Produto` como "tabela de preço" e carregá-la numa só produziria variante por empresa —
que é exatamente o que a PK `(tenant_id, variant_id)` recusa.

`finishes` confirma a leitura: `code`/`name`/`name_secondary`/`application`/`application_secondary`
caem um a um sobre `CodAcabamento`/`DescAcabamento`/`DescAcabamento2`/`acab_tipo`/`acab_tipo2`. A
tabela foi modelada a partir desta.

---

## §3 — BLOQUEIO: o índice de preço não tem tabela nem contrato

O prompt manda "`Ipr_Indice` migra como está". **Não há onde.** Varredura das 96 tabelas da `main`:
não existe `price_index`, `cost_profile`, `margin`, nem coluna de custo em `products`,
`product_variants` ou `product_tenant`. O que o Cabinet guarda é o **resultado**:
`product_tenant.price_cents`.

A api#114 já mediu o outro lado e continua valendo: **0 rotas, 0 schemas e 0 URNs de preço** no
contrato, e a decisão **D1 (Custo+Índice)** está aberta na memória compartilhada, com
`contador fiscal` anotado como segunda trava do módulo Preço.

Criar tabela de índice aqui seria migração + pacote de RLS completo por uma decisão que ninguém
tomou, e o dado não teria porta de leitura nenhuma. **Fica de fora, anotado.** Quando D1 for
decidida, a fonte está medida: `Indice_preco` é PK `(for_codigo, Ipr_descricao)` — índice **por
fornecedor, sem empresa**, a única tabela do escopo sem `Emp_codigo` —, e
`Preco_Produto.Pre_Codindice` referencia `Ipr_descricao` por TEXTO.

### E há uma pergunta de dinheiro que o script não pode responder sozinho

`Preco_Produto` tem **seis** colunas `money`: `Pre_Tabela`, `Pre_compra`, `Pre_Custo`, `Pre_Venda`,
`Pre_Lucro`, `Pre_PorLucro`. O destino tem **uma**: `price_cents`. O prompt diz "preço de tabela",
que aponta para `Pre_Tabela`; o preço que o cliente paga é `Pre_Venda`. **Escolher no script seria
inventar a decisão.** Vai como pergunta ao user (§7), e o dry-run conta as duas para que a resposta
seja dada com o número na frente.

---

## §4 — Profissional não tem documento, e isso quebra a segunda porta de procura

`Indicacoes` tem 40 colunas e **nenhuma de CPF/CNPJ**. A fase 2 procura o parceiro por duas portas
— o vínculo (`partner_tenant.code`) e o documento (`uq_partners_document`). Para profissional só a
primeira funciona.

Não é impedimento: `uq_partners_document` é **parcial** (`WHERE document IS NOT NULL`), então os
1.316 entram sem colidir entre si. É uma **perda de dedup declarada**: o arquiteto que também é
cliente entra duas vezes, e o dado não permite saber. Contar e nomear no relatório; adivinhar por
nome seria fundir duas pessoas homônimas.

Duas armadilhas do cadastro:

- **`Ind_Dtnacimento` é `nvarchar(5)`** — não cabe uma data. O destino `partners.birth_date` é
  `date`. O dry-run tem de mostrar os valores distintos antes de qualquer conversão; a fase 2 já
  pagou o caso do ano `0000`, que o Postgres recusa e que derrubaria a carga inteira.
- **`Ind_profissao` é texto livre** e `Profissão` tem 149 linhas — lookup existe, o vínculo não.

**Esta fase destrava uma dívida da fase 2.** O LEIA-ME declara que `Ind_codigo` não é resolvido
porque o profissional não existia. `partners.specifier_id` é FK para `partners`, e `Clientes` tem
`Ind_codigo`: com os profissionais carregados, a segunda passada vira entregável — e entra no DoD.

---

## §5 — Produto é do ORG, e o legado o tem por empresa

`products` **não tem `tenant_id`**; `produtos` tem `Emp_codigo` (nullable), e a base tem 4 empresas.
Mesmo `Pro_codnosso` em duas empresas = **um** produto no ORG. O que fazer quando as descrições
divergirem é decisão de dado, não de código: contar e nomear no relatório.

Larguras conferidas no `dbml` (caracteres, não bytes) — **todas cabem**:

| Legado | Destino | |
|---|---|---|
| `Pro_codnosso nvarchar(20)` | `products.code varchar(30)` | cabe |
| `Pro_descricao nvarchar(100)` | `products.description varchar(200)` | cabe |
| `Pre_Acabamento nvarchar(10)` | `product_variants.finish varchar(60)` | cabe |
| `CodAcabamento nvarchar(10)` | `finishes.code varchar(20)` | cabe |
| `For_cnpj_cpf nvarchar(14)` | `partners.document varchar(20)` | cabe |
| `For_Nome nvarchar(45)` | `partners.legal_name varchar(160)` | cabe |

A regra da fase 2 continua: **nada é truncado** — o que não couber não entra e sai nomeado.

Três guardas que só o dado responde, e por isso são casos obrigatórios do dry-run:

1. **`Preco_Produto` não tem FK para `produtos`.** `bdprincipal-fks.csv` traz quatro FKs citando
   `produtos` e nenhuma delas é essa; `Pre_Codnosso` é **nullable**. Linha de preço órfã não pode
   virar variante — contar antes.
2. **`Tam_codigo` aponta para `tamanho`, que tem 0 linhas.** `product_variants.size` é `NOT NULL`.
   Quantas linhas trazem `Tam_codigo` não nulo decide se `size` entra vazio ou com valor.
3. **`Emp_codigo` é nullable em todas as tabelas do escopo.** Linha sem empresa não tem tenant de
   destino. Contar; a regra de fallback é do user (§7).

---

## §6 — O que já existe e NÃO se refaz

`scripts/etl/` na `main` tem os três estágios separados, e a fase 2 provou que a fronteira aguenta
fonte nova sem tocar na anterior:

| Arquivo | Estágio | Reaproveitamento |
|---|---|---|
| `fonte.ts` | extrair | CSV, BOM, `;`, vocabulário de flags — **usar** |
| `sql.ts` | carregar | `texto()`, `INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS` — **usar** |
| `legado-clientes.ts` / `mapa-clientes.ts` / `sql-clientes.ts` | — | **modelo a seguir**, não editar |
| `negocio.ts` | CLI | ganha os novos dumps; o de cliente não muda de comportamento |

O desenho a manter, porque já foi pago: **sem rede** (nada fala com o SQL Server da loja);
**aditivo** (`WHERE NOT EXISTS`, nunca `ON CONFLICT`; quem está no banco vence); **dump fora da
árvore** (`--dump`, nunca descoberta automática — é dado pessoal); e o repositório guarda só a
**consulta que define o formato** mais uma **amostra fabricada**.

`set_config('app.current_tenant', …)` na forma estrita continua obrigatório antes de qualquer
`NOT EXISTS` sobre tabela com `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` — sem ele a segunda execução não enxerga
o que entrou e morre na chave primária.

---

## §7 — Perguntas ao user (bloqueiam a CARGA, não o script)

O script e o dry-run são construídos sem elas; o `--aplicar` não roda antes das respostas.

1. **Qual coluna vira `price_cents`** — `Pre_Tabela` (o "preço de tabela" do prompt) ou `Pre_Venda`
   (o que o cliente paga)? O relatório traz as duas contadas.
2. **As 4 empresas do legado viram 4 `tenants`, ou só a VERTZ?** Muda o recorte de produto, preço,
   fornecedor e profissional.
3. **`Emp_codigo` nulo vai para qual empresa** — a VERTZ, ou fica de fora e sai no relatório?

---

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `--relatorio` (dry-run) para os quatro dumps novos, com **contagem por tabela conferida
      contra `bdprincipal-linhas.csv`**: 868 · 1.316 · 108.992 · 169.764 · 248 · 7.
- [ ] O relatório conta, antes de qualquer carga: preço órfão · `Emp_codigo` nulo · produto
      duplicado entre empresas com descrição divergente · valor que não coube · `Tam_codigo`
      preenchido · `Ind_Dtnacimento` fora de formato · profissional sem documento.
- [ ] Inventário de **colunas sem destino**, nomeadas — o que falta construir no cadastro.
- [ ] `amostra/consulta-*.sql` + amostra **fabricada** por dump novo. Nenhum dado real no repo.
- [ ] Idempotência: `WHERE NOT EXISTS`, três execuções estáveis contra Postgres real com o schema
      das migrações da `main`; a quarta preserva edição feita "pela tela".
- [ ] Bateria em `node:test` (fora do Vitest, sem banco), com **cada guarda provada VERMELHA** —
      guarda de presença é a que falha calada.
- [ ] Segunda passada de `Ind_codigo` → `partners.specifier_id`, agora possível (§4).
- [ ] **Relatório em prosa para o user antes de qualquer `--aplicar`**, com as três perguntas do §7.
- [ ] `pnpm check` (com caminho explícito), `pnpm check-types`, `pnpm test` verdes.

## Fora de escopo

Venda/orçamento (`Ven_Tipo`), estoque, `ProdutosFornecedores`, financeiro, `bdprodutos` inteiro,
e **tabela de índice/custo/margem** (§3 — depende de D1).

## Zona e reservas

Zona: **`scripts/etl/**` exclusivo**. Não toca `migrations/`, `src/`, `contracts/` nem
`package.json`. **Nenhum `NNNN` de migração reservado** — este trilho não cria tabela; se o §3
mudar, a reserva vem antes, em comentário próprio.

## Nota operacional

O CI do `cabinet-erp-api` estava **parado por billing** em 24/08 (quatro jobs vermelhos em 2s, sem
log). Quem pegar este trilho confere antes de ler vermelho como defeito próprio.
