items.title: NiFi: wire the `NIFI_AUTH` switch (localhost-only no-auth default, Keycloak HTTPS for shared deployments)
items.body:
## Summary

`biar-nifi` runs over plain HTTP (`NIFI_WEB_HTTP_PORT=8088` in `biar/env/biar-nifi.env`), published on all host interfaces. In that mode NiFi performs **no authentication or authorization**: every client is an anonymous user with full access. That includes:

- Viewing all tenants' data in flight.
- Changing the ETL.
- Adding processors that run commands in the container.

The companion issue tazama-lf/biar#211 adds an image-level switch, `NIFI_AUTH=none|keycloak` (HTTP 8088 unauthenticated / HTTPS 8443 with Keycloak OIDC). This issue wires it into the stack:

- Local deployments default to `none`, reachable **only from the local machine**.
- Shared deployments (AWS, production) use `keycloak`.

## Work items

1. **Mode selection:** `NIFI_AUTH=none` in the committed `biar/env/biar-nifi.env` (local default). Deployments override it to `keycloak`. Mode-dependent variables:
   - `KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_URL`, `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID`
   - `NIFI_WEB_PROXY_HOST`, `INITIAL_ADMIN_IDENTITY`
2. **Ports (`docker-compose.dev.biar.yaml`, `docker-compose.hub.biar.yaml`):** publish both, permanently. Only the one matching the mode has a listener.
   ```yaml
   - "${NIFI_BIND_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}:${NIFI_PORT:-8088}:8088"         # none mode, localhost-only by default
   - "${NIFI_HTTPS_BIND_ADDRESS:-0.0.0.0}:${NIFI_HTTPS_PORT:-8443}:8443" # keycloak mode
   ```
   - The localhost default is a safeguard: an unauthenticated NiFi is never reachable from other machines unless someone deliberately sets `NIFI_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0`.
   - A shared deployment that forgets to switch modes **fails closed**: the UI is unreachable, not public.
   - Internal callers use the Docker network and are unaffected.
3. **`biar/nifi/init.sh`:** branch on `NIFI_AUTH`.
   - `none`: `http://biar-nifi:8088`, as today.
   - `keycloak`: `https://biar-nifi:8443`, with the machine identity (client certificate) defined in the biar issue.
4. **Keycloak (realm-import JSON `core/auth/keycloak/realms/00-tazama-test-realm.json`):**
   - Confidential client `nifi`, redirect `https://<nifi-host>/nifi-api/access/oidc/callback`, with a local test secret, as for `jupyterhub`.
   - Group tree `tazama-nifi/NIFI_ADMIN/<ORG>` (TENANT_ID on org leafs).
   - `keycloak` mode requires core's **Authentication** toggle.
5. **Secrets (`secrets.env` template, see the secrets-file work):**
   - New keys: `TAZAMA_NIFI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`, `TAZAMA_NIFI_SENSITIVE_PROPS_KEY`, `TAZAMA_NIFI_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `TAZAMA_NIFI_TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD`.
   - They are required only in `keycloak` mode, so compose uses `${X:-}`, and the image does the fail-fast check in `keycloak` mode.
6. **AWS (`infra/aws`):**
   - Deploy scripts set `NIFI_AUTH=keycloak` and **refuse** `none`.
   - Values come from SSM (`/tazama/creds/nifi/*`).
   - ALB target group `tazama-tg-nifi` becomes HTTPS:8443, with an adjusted health check (the current `/nifi-api/system-diagnostics` will require auth).
   - Server C's SG allows 8443 from the ALB SG.
   - Remove the plain-HTTP NiFi listener and SG rule. All in `modules/alb` + `modules/security-groups`.
7. **Launcher:** the biar launcher shows the current NiFi auth mode (read from the env file) in its header.
8. **Docs (`biar/README.md`):**
   - Both modes and the default.
   - Localhost-only binding in `none` mode, and `NIFI_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0` as a deliberate opt-out, with a warning.
   - The `keycloak` mode URL (`https://localhost:8443/nifi`) and its Keycloak dependency.
   - Correct the existing NiFi passages (UI URL and login statements).
   - Also: `infra/aws/aws-deployment-instructions.md` (NiFi listener/SG/health-check sections).

## Behaviour changes (disclosed)

- Local: NiFi on 8088 is no longer reachable from other machines by default (opt-out: `NIFI_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0`).
- Any existing shared deployment redeployed in `none` mode loses its NiFi UI through the load balancer (fail-closed). The ETL is unaffected.

## Out of scope

- Tenant (non-operator) access: NiFi has no tenant isolation. Design deferred until a use case exists.
- `ListenHTTP` on 8081 (published on all interfaces, unauthenticated): separate follow-up; check whether the host mapping is needed at all.

## Related

- tazama-lf/biar#211 (image switch)
- biar#184 (JupyterHub Keycloak OIDC; same convention as `JUPYTERHUB_AUTH`)
- Planned tazama-stack secrets file (`secrets.env`)

items.title: [E1-T11] Tenant onboarding and advisor seeding in the migrate job
items.body:
## Summary
`migrate --onboard-tenant` creates a tenant's chunks LIST partition with indexes, its tenants row and the IdP mapping, idempotently and without partition grants.

## Description
Implement the onboarding step in the `migrate` entrypoint (E0 created the entrypoint; Cloud Run job, role `fa_owner`): deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md §4.8 "`migrate` ... tenant onboarding (`--onboard-tenant <slug>`: LIST partition + indexes, `tenants` row, IdP mapping; the IdP tenant itself is provisioned by an onboarding script in E1 ...)". ADR-003: "Tenant onboarding creates its partition and indexes in the `migrate` job."

CLI: `migrate --onboard-tenant <slug> --display-name <name> --idp-tenant-id <id> [--tenant-id <uuid>] [--kind firm|public]`. In one transaction as `fa_owner`: insert the `tenants` row (`status='active'`, new uuid unless `--tenant-id`), call `create_chunks_partition` (E1-T5; partition plus the parent-declared indexes), commit. Rerunning with the same slug is a no-op that exits 0. If rows for that tenant already sit in the DEFAULT partition, exit non-zero with a clear message (do not move rows). The dedicated `eval` tenant is onboarded with `--tenant-id $EVAL_TENANT_ID`. The PUBLIC tenant already exists (E1-T4, E1-T5). Partitions get no grants. Print the new `tenants.id`.

Seed command (R18): `migrate --seed-advisors <file>` reads a JSON file of advisors (`tenant_slug, idp_uid, display_name, role, tier, jurisdictions, licenses`), resolves the tenant by slug, and inserts the `advisors` rows as `fa_owner` (upsert on `(tenant_id, idp_uid)`, idempotent). It is the only way the first advisors are created (demo setup uses it); there is no auto-provision on first login. Unknown tenant slug, invalid tier/role/jurisdiction, or malformed file exits non-zero and inserts nothing.

Out of scope: creating the IdP tenant (E1-T21), Terraform (E10), a tenant-creation HTTP endpoint ("Tenant onboarding (partition creation) is a job, not an endpoint").

Round 4 (ADR-027, ADR-031, ADR-029; deep-dive/04 section 4.8: onboarding creates the LIST partition, indexes, the per-leaf `EXCLUDE` constraint on `chunks`, the `tenants` row including `cell_id`, and the IdP mapping): (1) onboarding takes `--cell-id <cell>` (default: `HOME_CELL` from Settings) and optional `--residency-class none|eu_only|uk_only` and writes them to the `tenants` row. (2) The partition is created through `create_chunks_partition` (E1-T5), so it carries the `EXCLUDE` constraint; after creating it, `migrate` asserts that the new leaf has the constraint and the same indexes as `chunks_public` (like the other partition assertions of section 5.3) and exits non-zero otherwise. (3) `migrate --seed-advisors` also inserts one `pseudonym_map` row per seeded advisor (random `pseudonym_id`, E1-T23), idempotently with the advisor upsert.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given an empty database after migrations, when `migrate --onboard-tenant acme --display-name Acme --idp-tenant-id idp-acme` runs, then `tests/db/test_onboarding.py` passes: one `tenants` row with slug `acme` exists, `chunks` has a partition bound to its id, and `fa_tenant_lookup(p_idp_tenant_id => 'idp-acme')` returns that id.
- [ ] Given the same command is run a second time, then it exits 0 and `SELECT count(*) FROM tenants WHERE slug = 'acme'` is 1 and `chunks` still has exactly one partition for it.
- [ ] Given a chunk inserted for the onboarded tenant by `fa_owner`, then `tableoid::regclass` is the tenant's partition and `chunks_default` is empty (test).
- [ ] Given the new partition, then none of `fa_app, fa_worker, fa_etl, fa_etl_public, fa_dbt, fa_eval` has any privilege on it (`has_table_privilege`), and the same indexes as `chunks_public` exist on it (compared by definition).
- [ ] Given rows of the tenant already in `chunks_default`, when onboarding that tenant runs, then the command exits non-zero and creates no partition.
- [ ] Given a seed file with one valid advisor and one with an unknown `tenant_slug`, when `migrate --seed-advisors` runs, then it exits non-zero and the `advisors` table has no new rows; given only valid entries it inserts them, and a second run leaves the row count unchanged (`tests/db/test_seed_advisors.py`).
- [ ] Given the onboarded partition, then `pg_constraint` shows an exclusion constraint on it and the migrate step's own assertion passes; given a partition created without the constraint (test fixture), then the assertion makes `migrate` exit non-zero (`tests/db/test_onboarding.py::test_leaf_exclude_asserted`).
- [ ] Given `--cell-id eu --residency-class eu_only`, then the `tenants` row has those values; given `--residency-class us_only`, the command exits non-zero and inserts nothing.
- [ ] Given a seed file with two advisors, when `migrate --seed-advisors` runs twice, then `pseudonym_map` has exactly two rows with distinct `pseudonym_id` values and the second run changes none (`tests/db/test_seed_advisors.py::test_pseudonym_rows_seeded_once`).

items.title: DLH-API: temp-view registration tied to request lifecycle, not Spark session lifecycle which causes intermittent `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND` 500s after Spark session recreation
items.body:
## Problem

`datalakehouse-api/lakehouse_query_api.py::_execute_sql_sync` registers Hudi tables as Spark TempViews **inside each request** by iterating `GOLD_PATHS` and calling `createOrReplaceTempView` per table. The invariant "every table in `GOLD_PATHS` is addressable in the Spark catalog" is maintained by request handlers, not by the Spark session itself. When `get_spark()` recreates the session mid-stream (triggered when `_spark._sc._jvm is None` — Spark worker OOM, long-idle session reaping, Py4J connection drop), the new session starts with an empty catalog. Subsequent requests fail with `[TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND]` because `createOrReplaceTempView` can silently miss on sparse-commit Hudi tables when a writer lands a commit between `os.path.isdir(path)` and `spark.read.format("hudi").load(path)`.

Observed in UAT (air-gapped Tazama deployment, 2026-10-13, deployed image `eee16a0`, byte-identical to `origin/dev` HEAD `1613e03` at this file):

- `biar-datalakehouse-api` logged `WARNING:pipeline:Spark session missing or dead — recreating.` followed by sustained `AnalysisException: [TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND] The table or view 'conditions' cannot be found` 500s on `POST /execute_sql`, even though `/opt/Tazama_Warehouse/gold/condition` existed, `os.path.isdir(path)` returned `True` from inside the container, and direct `curl -X POST /execute_sql` from the host returned 200 OK on the same table.
- The 500s propagated to CMS backend as `HttpException: Failed to run SQL query on Gold Lakehouse: Request failed with status code 500` on `/api/v1/lakehouse/alert-navigator/*`, `/api/v1/lakehouse/transaction-detail/*`, and the entity-accounts-with-condition-counts sub-query. 32 failures captured across ~2h of frontend traffic. CMS frontend tabs rendered partially or not at all.
- Workaround confirmed: `docker restart biar-datalakehouse-api` — forces a clean session with clean registration. All 500s stopped. End-to-end: `AlertNavigator/46` → 200 OK in 16.6s cold, 0.5s warm; zero new "Failed to run SQL" in CMS backend logs since the restart.
- On tazama-c (beta env, 11 commits on `gold/condition` vs UAT's 1), the race never surfaces. Denser commit history makes the registration path atomic enough. The bug is latent on beta; UAT exposed it via sparse condition data.

Verified against `tazama-lf/biar` @ `1613e03` (`origin/dev` HEAD on 2026-10-13).

## Details

### Current `_execute_sql_sync` (origin/dev)

[`datalakehouse-api/lakehouse_query_api.py` L387-412](https://github.com/tazama-lf/biar/blob/dev/datalakehouse-api/lakehouse_query_api.py#L387-L412):

```python
def _execute_sql_sync(sql_query: str, tenant_id: str, limit: int = None):
    spark = get_spark()
    with _sql_lock:
        for tname, path in GOLD_PATHS.items():
            if os.path.isdir(path):
                tdf = spark.read.format("hudi").load(path)
                if TENANT_ID_COLUMN in tdf.columns:
                    tdf = tdf.filter(F.col(TENANT_ID_COLUMN) == tenant_id)
                tdf.createOrReplaceTempView(tname)
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Path for table '{tname}' not found: {path}")

        df = spark.sql(sql_query)
        if limit:
            df = df.limit(limit)
        return [row.asDict(recursive=True) for row in df.collect()]
```

`get_spark()` at L70-85 constructs a session but does not register any Hudi path. Catalog population is left entirely to request handlers.

### Why per-request registration is wrong

- **Tenant TempView name collision.** `createOrReplaceTempView(tname)` uses the same name regardless of tenant. Under concurrent multi-tenant load, request A (tenant=`DEFAULT`) can see B's (tenant=`PAYSYS`) filter applied — latent cross-tenant data leak, masked today by single-tenant deployments.
- **Repeated Hudi reads.** `spark.read.format("hudi").load(path)` scans `.hoodie/` metadata, reads commit timeline, resolves active files. 29 tables in `GOLD_PATHS`; a two-table query re-reads 29 metadata trees instead of 2.
- **Log spam.** The "Path for table X not found" warning fires per request per missing path. UAT snapshot: `typologies` emitted 294 warnings in one hour (genuinely missing on disk due to a separate ETL bug); `conditions` emitted 223 during the race window.
- **The race.** After session recreation the new catalog is empty. On the next request, between `os.path.isdir(path)` and `spark.read.format("hudi").load(path)` for a sparse-commit table, a Hudi writer landing a new commit can cause `.load()` to silently succeed with a stale file list; the subsequent `createOrReplaceTempView` registers a view Spark later cannot resolve. The next `spark.sql(...)` throws `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND`.

### Related work

Not fixed in any open or recently-merged PR as of `origin/dev` @ `1613e03`. Searched: `lakehouse_query_api`, `_execute_sql_sync`, `createOrReplaceTempView`, `Spark session missing`, `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `tempview`. PR #172 and issue #170 are adjacent but orchestrator-side (view scheduling), not DLH-API query-side registration. No existing issue tracks the symptom.

## Solution

**Register tenant-agnostic Hudi tables once per Spark session; move tenant filtering to query-rewrite time.** The invariant "a Spark session always has `GOLD_PATHS` registered" becomes an explicit property of the session lifecycle.

### Design

1. **Per-session registration helper** `_register_all_hudi_tables(spark)` registers each existing-on-disk `GOLD_PATHS` entry as a tenant-agnostic TempView.
2. **Per-session guard.** Module-level `_registered_session_id: Optional[int]` compares `id(spark)` on each `_execute_sql_sync` entry. Mismatch → re-register against the new session. Match → skip.
3. **Tenant filtering at query time.** `_execute_sql_sync` creates per-tenant filtered views (`__tenant_<name>`) on each registered base view, then rewrites the caller's SQL via word-boundary regex substitution so references resolve to the filtered views. Caller's query shape preserved.
4. The missing-path warning fires once per session, not per request.

### Implementation

[`datalakehouse-api/lakehouse_query_api.py`](https://github.com/tazama-lf/biar/blob/dev/datalakehouse-api/lakehouse_query_api.py):

```diff
+_registered_session_id: Optional[int] = None
+_registration_lock = threading.Lock()
+
+
+def _register_all_hudi_tables(spark: SparkSession) -> None:
+    """Register every GOLD_PATHS entry as a tenant-agnostic TempView.
+    Idempotent per session. Tenant filtering happens in _execute_sql_sync."""
+    for tname, path in GOLD_PATHS.items():
+        if os.path.isdir(path):
+            try:
+                spark.read.format("hudi").load(path).createOrReplaceTempView(tname)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                logger.error(f"Failed to register '{tname}' at '{path}': {exc}")
+        else:
+            logger.warning(f"Path for table '{tname}' not found: {path}")
+
+
 def _execute_sql_sync(sql_query: str, tenant_id: str, limit: int = None):
-    spark = get_spark()
-    with _sql_lock:
-        for tname, path in GOLD_PATHS.items():
-            if os.path.isdir(path):
-                tdf = spark.read.format("hudi").load(path)
-                if TENANT_ID_COLUMN in tdf.columns:
-                    tdf = tdf.filter(F.col(TENANT_ID_COLUMN) == tenant_id)
-                tdf.createOrReplaceTempView(tname)
-            else:
-                logger.warning(f"Path for table '{tname}' not found: {path}")
-
-        df = spark.sql(sql_query)
-        if limit:
-            df = df.limit(limit)
-        return [row.asDict(recursive=True) for row in df.collect()]
+    global _registered_session_id
+    spark = get_spark()
+
+    with _registration_lock:
+        if _registered_session_id != id(spark):
+            _register_all_hudi_tables(spark)
+            _registered_session_id = id(spark)
+
+    with _sql_lock:
+        for tname in GOLD_PATHS.keys():
+            if not spark.catalog.tableExists(tname):
+                continue
+            base = spark.table(tname)
+            if TENANT_ID_COLUMN in base.columns:
+                base.filter(F.col(TENANT_ID_COLUMN) == tenant_id) \
+                    .createOrReplaceTempView(f"__tenant_{tname}")
+            else:
+                base.createOrReplaceTempView(f"__tenant_{tname}")
+
+        rewritten = sql_query
+        for tname in GOLD_PATHS.keys():
+            rewritten = re.sub(rf"\b{re.escape(tname)}\b",
+                               f"__tenant_{tname}",
+                               rewritten)
+
+        df = spark.sql(rewritten)
+        if limit:
+            df = df.limit(limit)
+        return [row.asDict(recursive=True) for row in df.collect()]
```

Requires `import re` at module top (verify at PR time).

### Tests / validation

No existing unit test harness for this file. Minimum:

- **Unit:** mock `SparkSession`, assert `_register_all_hudi_tables` called exactly once per unique `id(spark)` across 100 interleaved `_execute_sql_sync` calls. Verify query-rewrite output for plain `SELECT`, aliased join, nested subquery, CTE.
- **Integration:** against a test warehouse with one Hudi commit on `gold/condition` (reproduces UAT condition), run 500 concurrent `_execute_sql_sync` calls, forcibly `spark.stop()` mid-stream from a sibling thread. Expect zero `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND`; one "session missing or dead — recreating" warning; registration log line once per session.
- **Multi-tenant regression:** `conditions` populated with rows for two tenants. 10 threads interleave queries per tenant. Each thread's result contains only its tenant's rows.

## Impact

- **Correctness.** Eliminates the `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND` 500 class caused by session recreation. Removes latent cross-tenant leak.
- **Performance.** Hudi `.load()` calls per request drop from `|GOLD_PATHS|` (29) to 0 on the hot path. Registration cost paid once per session lifetime.
- **Log hygiene.** Missing-path warning fires once per session per path, not per request (294 → 1 for `typologies` in the UAT snapshot).
- **Backwards compatible.** `GOLD_PATHS` shape, `/execute_sql` schema, all public endpoints unchanged. Callers see identical responses for identical queries.
- **Blast radius.** One file, one function body replaced, one helper added. Reversible with a one-commit revert.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_execute_sql_sync` no longer iterates `GOLD_PATHS` to call `createOrReplaceTempView` on every request.
- [ ] New `_register_all_hudi_tables(spark)` helper called at most once per Spark session instance.
- [ ] 500 sequential `_execute_sql_sync` calls with a mid-run session kill produce zero `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND` exceptions and one "session missing or dead" warning.
- [ ] Concurrent calls for two tenants against the same base table return correctly tenant-partitioned results (no cross-tenant leakage).
- [ ] "Path for table '<name>' not found" fires at most once per missing path per Spark session.
- [ ] CMS backend `GoldLakehouseService` and Jupyter notebooks see identical response bodies for identical queries.
- [ ] Grep across `datalakehouse-api/` at review time finds no remaining per-request `createOrReplaceTempView` loop over `GOLD_PATHS`.

## Test scenarios

1. **Baseline.** 100 sequential calls for `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM alerts`. All 200; registration log line once; no `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND`.
2. **Session recreated mid-stream (UAT bug).** 100 calls, inject `spark.stop()` after call 50. Call 51 triggers re-registration; calls 52-100 hit the cache. Zero `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND`.
3. **Sparse-commit Hudi race.** `gold/condition` has one commit; thread B lands a second commit as thread A's registration begins. A reads either snapshot cleanly; `spark.sql` succeeds. No `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND`.
4. **Multi-tenant.** 50 rows per tenant × 2 tenants; 10 threads interleave. Each thread's `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conditions` returns 50, not 100.
5. **Absent table (`gold/typologies` in UAT).** 100 calls to `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM typologies`. Warning fires once at session creation; all requests fail with `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND` — correct behaviour, surfacing as 404/structured 400 instead of raw 500 is a follow-up candidate.
6. **Query-rewrite correctness.** `SELECT * FROM conditions WHERE account_id = 'X'` → `SELECT * FROM __tenant_conditions WHERE account_id = 'X'`. Aliased joins and CTE-wrapped queries rewrite correctly in all body positions.

## Paired work

None required — fix is self-contained in `datalakehouse-api/lakehouse_query_api.py`.

Separate pre-existing bug observed alongside: `TypologiesETL.silver()` crashes at `TypologiesETL.py:63` on `getField("typology_name")` for configurations that don't emit that field. Current `typologies` warnings are a legitimate "data not written" condition caused by that ETL bug, not addressed here. File separately.

items.title: [E13] Regional cells and multiple logins
items.body:
## Summary
Regional cells and multiple logins (phase 3: Real data and lifecycle). Scope, ADRs and exit criteria are in the plan section below.

## Plan
- **Goal.** A firm's data lives only in its home cell, a wrong-cell request is refused without touching data, a tenant can move cell, and one person can work in several firms with one token per firm.
- **Scope.**
  - Signed static `cells.json` (tenant slug, `tenant_id`, `home_cell`, `residency_class`, endpoints) in GCS with a baked fallback, refreshed every 60 s, no control-plane database; unreadable means last good copy then the baked fallback; `GET /resolve?slug=` content (ADR-031, R4-D10).
  - Cell isolation: each cell holds only its tenants; the E1 `principal` check returns 421 plus a hint with zero DB reads on mismatch; no cross-cell replication or failover; PUBLIC ingested independently per cell by its own `etl-public` with a manifest (document count and `chunk_set_hash` per version) and a drift alert (the cell-versus-cell pair of the E12 reconcile job).
  - Two-cell docker compose suite (`cell-us`, `cell-eu` networks, a router serving `cells.json`; RAM 4-6 GB is an ASSUMPTION), Cloud Run in one region only (a real second region and Claude on Vertex EU are costed options, not built).
  - Residency wording (ADR-038): "Data at rest ... stays in the tenant's home cell. Prompt text and embedding and rerank inputs are processed by Anthropic and Voyage, which are US/global." Global data (user id, email, firm membership, tenant-to-cell map, PUBLIC manifest hashes, aggregate metrics) is declared in the privacy notice. Cells do not isolate an LLM-provider outage; it returns `LLM_UNAVAILABLE` in every cell and is not reported as a cell failure.
  - Tenant move: `move-tenant` job with states `active`, `freezing`, `copying`, `verifying`, `cutover`, `draining`, `source_erased`; freeze (chat off, outbox drained to 0), ordered per-table copy, verify by row counts and `md5(string_agg(id||hash ORDER BY id))` per table, atomic publish of a new signed `cells.json`, source `moved` (421) and erased after a 7-day grace through ADR-029 with a receipt; before cutover a failure unfreezes the source and deletes partial target rows; Langfuse traces do not move (ADR-033).
  - Multiple logins: the server verifies at project level, reads `firebase.tenant` and requires it to equal the URL tenant and the cell map; one token per firm; no identity merge; optional person-linking is opt-in UX and never an authorization input; if the E1 spike failed, per-firm email aliases replace the switcher flow (ADR-032, R4-D11).
- **Arch sections.** deep-dive/04-2-source-lifecycle-and-cells.md#4.24, deep-dive/08-security-and-privacy.md#8.2; ADR-031, ADR-032, ADR-033, ADR-038.
- **Dependencies.** E1 (tenant columns, `principal`, IdP tenants and the same-email spike result), E2 (hostnames, `/resolve`), E4 and E6 (a running stack for the compose suite), E5 (per-cell Kafka in compose); the move-tenant ticket also needs E12 (erasure and receipts). E12 never depends on E13, so the epic graph stays acyclic.
- **Spikes first.** The E2 ALB host-rule spike and the E1 same-email spike results are inputs; no new spike.
- **Phase.** 3 (Real data and lifecycle): the core runs in parallel with E11; the move-tenant ticket waits for E12.
- **Done when** (edge-case catalogue ids in brackets).
  - Stopping `cell-eu` leaves US tenants passing, EU tenants get 503 with a clear code, and no US data is touched (#6; N). A provider outage returns `LLM_UNAVAILABLE` in every cell and is not counted as a cell failure.
  - A wrong-cell request returns 421 and the DB query log is empty (#16; PR). A compose separation test shows a service in one cell cannot resolve the other. PUBLIC manifests are equal across cells, and a deliberate difference raises the drift alert.
  - `cells.json` unreadable: the last good copy is used, then the baked fallback; a tampered signature is rejected.
  - Token A on firm B's resource gives 403 or 421, the server-side check of #17 (the browser part, two sessions with separate `currentUser`, is in E8; PR).
  - Killing the move target mid-copy leaves the source intact and unfrozen and the target empty; on the success path counts and hashes are equal (#18; N). An erase of the moved source issues a receipt after the 7-day grace (test with a shortened grace).
  - The residency wording and the global-data list appear in the privacy notice; private ingest stays gated by `llm_egress_ack` (tested in E11).

## Architecture

items.title: # [Issue 21] Migrar dados do backend FastAPI para o backend Spring Modulith
items.body:
## Descrição
Planear e implementar o processo de migração de dados do backend atual em FastAPI (PostgreSQL) para o novo backend Spring Modulith (PostgreSQL), garantindo manutenção de `tenant_id`, utilizadores, merchants, catálogo, clientes, pedidos e agendamentos sem perda de integridade referencial.

## Contexto
A migração tecnológica não pode significar perda de dados. O sistema atual já possui tenants, utilizadores, catálogo (produtos/serviços), clientes, carrinho, pedidos e agendamentos em produção ou pré-produção. O novo schema (Spring Modulith + JPA) pode ter diferenças de nomes de tabelas, colunas, enums e estruturas JSON, exigindo um processo de ETL bem definido (extrair → transformar → carregar) e testado em ambiente controlado antes do go-live.

## Tarefas
- [ ] Comparar o schema atual (FastAPI) com o schema novo (Spring + Flyway) e:
  - [ ] Mapear tabelas equivalentes (ex.: `tenants`, `users`, `merchants`, `produtos`, `servicos`, `clientes`, `pedidos`, `itens_pedido`, `agendamentos`).
  - [ ] Identificar diferenças de tipos de dados, nomes de colunas, enums e estruturas JSON.
- [ ] Definir abordagem de migração:
  - [ ] Scripts SQL diretos.
  - [ ] Script Python/Java de ETL.
  - [ ] Ou combinação das duas abordagens.
- [ ] Criar scripts de extração de dados a partir do schema FastAPI:
  - [ ] Exportar dados por tabela, respeitando dependências (tenants → users → merchants → catálogo → clientes → pedidos/agendamentos).
- [ ] Implementar transformação dos dados:
  - [ ] Ajustar enums para os novos valores em Java (se necessário).
  - [ ] Converter/chavear campos JSON para o formato esperado pelo novo modelo.
  - [ ] Normalizar dados inconsistentes (ex.: valores nulos inesperados, estados antigos).
- [ ] Implementar carregamento dos dados no schema Spring:
  - [ ] Inserir os dados nas tabelas do novo schema na ordem correta, respeitando FKs.
  - [ ] Validar que `tenant_id` é preservado em todas as entidades.
- [ ] Criar um ambiente de teste de migração:
  - [ ] Restaurar backup da BD FastAPI.
  - [ ] Aplicar o processo de migração.
  - [ ] Comparar contagens por tabela (antes/depois) e amostras de registos.
- [ ] Documentar o processo de migração:
  - [ ] Passos para executar.
  - [ ] Riscos conhecidos.
  - [ ] Procedimentos de rollback.
- [ ] (Opcional) Automatizar o processo num script único (ex.: `migrate_fastapi_to_spring.sh`).

## Critérios de aceitação
- [ ] Todos os tenants existentes são migrados para o novo schema com os mesmos `id` e `slug`.
- [ ] Utilizadores, merchants, catálogo, clientes, pedidos e agendamentos são migrados mantendo a integridade referencial e o `tenant_id` correto.
- [ ] Contagens de registos por tabela (relevantes) entre BD antiga e nova coincidem ou são justificadas (ex.: entidades descontinuadas).
- [ ] O processo de migração foi testado num ambiente de staging com sucesso, sem erros de FKs ou perda de dados críticos.
- [ ] A documentação de migração está disponível e clara para ser executada no momento do go-live.

## Labels sugeridas
- `backend`
- `migration`
- `database`
- `multi-tenant`

items.title: Add an asymmetric fairness-metering experiment (sim-to-real residency comparison)
items.body:
# Add an asymmetric fairness-metering experiment (sim-to-real residency comparison)

> File this as a GitHub issue on `inference-sim/residency-vllm`. It extends the
> existing overhead A/B harness with one new workload and a sim-to-real
> comparison. It reuses the patched vLLM image, the k8s manifest, the `blis
> observe` driver, and `postprocess_trace.py` almost unchanged. Read it top to
> bottom and do the steps in order. Every command is spelled out.

## 1. Why we are doing this

The existing experiment runs a **homogeneous** workload (every tenant identical),
so the per-tenant residency is nearly equal (disparity ratio ≈ 1.04). That proves
the residency counter agrees with the simulator when there is nothing to be
unfair about.

The paper's whole claim is that **residency exposes per-tenant unfairness that
token-count and request-count meters miss**. To support that, we need to show the
residency counter is faithful **when the disparity is large and structural**, on
real hardware, and that the simulator reproduces that same disparity from the
same trace. That is the experiment below.

We measure one number on both sides and compare it:

- **Disparity ratio** `rho_mt = (largest tenant residency) / (smallest tenant
  residency)`. Under a skewed workload this is well above 1. If the simulator
  reproduces the real `rho_mt`, every simulation fairness result in the paper
  inherits that credibility.

We run **FCFS only** on the real server. Real vLLM has no KV-time fairness
scheduler, so FCFS is the only faithful real configuration. We are not trying to
show fairness *restored* on hardware (that stays a simulation result). We are
showing the **measurement instrument** (the residency counter) reads the same
under skew as the simulator's meter, so the simulation is trustworthy.

## 2. What changes vs the existing experiment (short list)

| Item | Existing | This experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Workload | homogeneous, all tenants equal | **asymmetric** (one light tenant, one heavy) |
| Rate | single rate per cell | **sweep across rates** (see §6, this is important) |
| Tenant id wiring | works for overhead test | **needs a 3-line fix** so the meter sees per-tenant ids (§4) |
| Token counts in analysis | nominal 1024 | **use the true `server_input_tokens`** (§7) |
| Scheduler | FCFS | FCFS (unchanged) |
| Server image, manifest, driver | — | **unchanged** |

## 3. The two workloads

We use two asymmetric workloads. **W5 is the headline; W7 is the robustness
check.** They skew residency through two different causes, so matching both shows
the meter is faithful regardless of *why* tenants differ.

### W5 — rate asymmetry ("free tier vs heavy customer")

Two tenants, equal-mean prompts, but tenant B arrives 5x as often as tenant A.
Under FCFS, B gets ~5x the service, so B's residency dominates and `rho_mt` skews
well above 1.

### W7 — prompt-length asymmetry ("chat vs RAG")

Two tenants, equal arrival rates, but tenant B's prompts are ~16x longer than
tenant A's. B consumes the cache disproportionately per request, so `rho_mt`
skews above 1 through a different mechanism.

The exact YAML specs are in §6 (they embed the rate sweep).

## 4. The one wiring fix you MUST make first (tenant id)

This is the single change to the patched vLLM, and the experiment produces garbage
without it. Do it first and verify it before anything else.

**The problem.** `blis observe` sends the tenant id as an HTTP **header**,
`x-gateway-inference-fairness-id`. The residency meter patch currently reads the
tenant id from the request **body**, `sampling_params.extra_args["tenant_id"]`.
These do not connect. Out of the box every request arrives with `tenant_id =
None`, so all residency collapses into a single bucket and `rho_mt` is undefined.

**The fix (do this, option a).** Make the vLLM patch read the tenant id from the
header. In `vllm/v1/request.py`, where `self.tenant_id` is currently set from
`extra_args`, fall back to the header when `extra_args` does not carry it. Concretely,
the request object already receives `trace_headers` (a mapping of incoming HTTP
headers). Set the tenant id from the header when the body did not provide it:

```python
# vllm/v1/request.py — where self.tenant_id is assigned
self.tenant_id = None
if sampling_params is not None and sampling_params.extra_args is not None:
    self.tenant_id = sampling_params.extra_args.get("tenant_id")
# Fall back to the GIE fairness header that `blis observe` sends.
if self.tenant_id is None and trace_headers:
    # header names are case-insensitive; normalize before lookup
    for k, v in trace_headers.items():
        if k.lower() == "x-gateway-inference-fairness-id":
            self.tenant_id = v
            break
```

Do **not** modify `blis observe` to write the body instead. Reading the header
keeps observe unchanged and matches how production llm-d routes tenants.

Rebuild and push the patched image (same Dockerfile, new tag), and point the
manifest at the new tag.

**Verify the fix before running the sweep.** Send two requests with two different
tenant ids and confirm `/metrics` shows two tenant labels:

```bash
# from inside the cluster or via port-forward to the patched server
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-gateway-inference-fairness-id: tenantA' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-14B","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8}' >/dev/null
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-gateway-inference-fairness-id: tenantB' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-14B","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8}' >/dev/null
curl -s http://localhost:8000/metrics | grep residency_token_seconds_total
# EXPECT two lines, one with tenant_id="tenantA" and one with tenant_id="tenantB".
# If you see one line with no tenant_id or tenant_id="", the fix did not take.
```

## 5. Setup parity (keep the real and sim setups identical)

Residency is memory held times time held, so lifetimes matter and lifetimes
depend on the serving setup. Keep both sides identical:

- Model `Qwen/Qwen3-14B`, one 80 GB H100, tensor-parallel 1, block size 16.
- Run the real server with defaults (`vllm serve --model Qwen/Qwen3-14B --port
  8000`), exactly as the existing manifest does. The simulator reconstructs the
  same KV capacity vLLM derives from those defaults.
- `blis observe` must enforce the output length so each request's residency is
  comparable. It already sets `min_tokens = max_tokens` by default. Keep that on.

## 6. Saturation differs between real and sim — so SWEEP the rate

This is the most important design point, do not skip it.

The real server and the simulator **do not saturate at the same offered load**.
Their exact KV capacities and batching dynamics differ, and the simulator's
latency model is an estimate. Residency is dominated by request lifetime, and
lifetime explodes near saturation. So a comparison at a single rate is
trustworthy only if both systems happen to be in the same regime at that rate,
which we cannot assume.

**Therefore sweep the aggregate rate** and report fidelity as a function of load.
In the unsaturated regime, lifetimes are short and insensitive to the latency
model, so residency fidelity is high and the `rho_mt` match is clean (this is the
headline). As load approaches saturation, any divergence is then visible and
labeled as a latency-model-at-saturation effect, not hidden.

Use a 1:5 rate ratio (A:B) held fixed, sweeping the **aggregate** rate. Suggested
points (per second, aggregate): **6, 12, 18, 24, 30**. The 1:5 split means tenant
A gets {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} req/s and tenant B gets {5, 10, 15, 20, 25} req/s.

Generate one W5 spec per rate point. Here is the template; substitute
`AGG_RATE` (e.g. write five files `w5_agg6.yaml` ... `w5_agg30.yaml`):

```yaml
# w5_aggAGG.yaml — rate-asymmetric, 1:5 split. Substitute AGG_RATE.
version: "2"
seed: 42
aggregate_rate: AGG_RATE          # 6, 12, 18, 24, 30
horizon: 600000000                # 600 s in microseconds
clients:
  - id: tenantA
    tenant_id: tenantA
    rate_fraction: 0.16667        # 1/6 -> light tenant
    streaming: true
    arrival: {process: poisson}
    input_distribution:  {type: constant, params: {value: 1024}}
    output_distribution: {type: constant, params: {value: 128}}
  - id: tenantB
    tenant_id: tenantB
    rate_fraction: 0.83333        # 5/6 -> heavy tenant
    streaming: true
    arrival: {process: poisson}
    input_distribution:  {type: constant, params: {value: 1024}}
    output_distribution: {type: constant, params: {value: 128}}
```

W7 (optional robustness cell), one spec, equal rates, asymmetric prompts. Sweep
the same aggregate rates:

```yaml
# w7_aggAGG.yaml — prompt-length-asymmetric, equal rates. Substitute AGG_RATE.
version: "2"
seed: 42
aggregate_rate: AGG_RATE
horizon: 600000000
clients:
  - id: tenantA
    tenant_id: tenantA
    rate_fraction: 0.5
    streaming: true
    arrival: {process: poisson}
    input_distribution:  {type: constant, params: {value: 256}}    # short
    output_distribution: {type: constant, params: {value: 128}}
  - id: tenantB
    tenant_id: tenantB
    rate_fraction: 0.5
    streaming: true
    arrival: {process: poisson}
    input_distribution:  {type: constant, params: {value: 4096}}   # ~16x longer
    output_distribution: {type: constant, params: {value: 128}}
```

> Note: the existing harness uses `constant` distributions, which is what these
> templates use too, so prompts are deterministic and easy to verify. If you want
> to match the paper's lognormal W5/W7 exactly later, copy the `lognormal` blocks
> from `figures/experiments1and2/workloads/W5.yaml` and `W7.yaml`. Start with
> constants. They make the residency arithmetic checkable by hand.

## 7. Collect the real data (one `blis observe` run per rate point)

For each generated spec, run the existing driver against the **patched** server
(the one with the §4 fix), exactly as `k8s/ab-experiment.yaml` does, only with the
new workload spec. Record the TraceV2 trace and scrape `/metrics`:

```bash
blis observe \
  --server-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-14B \
  --api-format chat \
  --workload-spec /data/w5_agg6.yaml \
  --seed 42 \
  --trace-header "${OUT}/trace.yaml" \
  --trace-data   "${OUT}/trace.csv" \
  --record-itl
# then, as the existing harness already does:
python3 /app/postprocess_trace.py \
  --trace-csv "${OUT}/trace.csv" --itl-csv "${OUT}/trace.itl.csv" \
  --output-dir "${OUT}" --server-url http://localhost:8000 --model Qwen/Qwen3-14B
```

Save each rate point under its own directory, e.g.
`results/w5_sweep/agg6/{trace.yaml,trace.csv,summary.json}`, and likewise for W7.

**Analysis correctness fix (token counts).** `postprocess_trace.py` reports the
**nominal** prompt length (1024) in `summary.json`, not the true tokenized length.
The true length is the `server_input_tokens` column in `trace.csv` (~986 for these
prompts, because the model's tokenizer plus chat template do not land on exactly
1024). For the residency comparison this does not change the counter itself, which
already charges real resident blocks, but **any per-request normalization in your
analysis must read `server_input_tokens` from `trace.csv`, never `prompt_tokens`
from `summary.json`.** The simulator already uses the true count on replay, so
using the nominal count on the real side would introduce a spurious ~4% gap.

The ground-truth residency you compare against is, per cell, per tenant:
`summary.json -> per_tenant.<tenant>.residency_token_seconds`.

## 8. Replay each trace through the simulator and compare

This is the half that is already built. The traces are TraceV2, which the
simulator reads directly. **Use the patched `blis-kvtime` from
`figures/vllmparityexperiment/`, not base `blis replay`.** Base `blis replay`
reads the same trace but has no residency meter; the meter lives only in the
patched simulator.

Build once (from the paper repo):

```bash
cd figures/vllmparityexperiment
export BLIS_REPO=/path/to/inference-sim
bash etl/stage1_build.sh        # builds blis-kvtime with patch 03 (trace replay)
```

Replay each real trace with the identical setup, FCFS, warmup 0:

```bash
./blis-kvtime --scheduler=fcfs \
  --trace-header=results/w5_sweep/agg6/trace.yaml \
  --trace-data=results/w5_sweep/agg6/trace.csv \
  --model=qwen/qwen3-14b --hardware=H100 --tp=1 \
  --model-config-dir=$BLIS_REPO/model_configs/qwen3-14b \
  --hw-config=$BLIS_REPO/hardware_config.json \
  --latency-backend=trained-physics \
  --seed=42 --warmup=0 \
  --output=results/w5_sweep/agg6/sim.json
```

Why this works and what to watch:

- The trace supplies arrivals and **true** token counts. The simulator derives
  step durations from the latency model. The meter integrates resident tokens
  times elapsed time over the simulation clock.
- The trace's arrival times are absolute (epoch microseconds). Patch 03 already
  derives the simulation horizon from the trace's own arrival span, so you do not
  pass `--duration`. (If you ever see `completed=0`, that is the symptom of this
  not happening; patch 03 handles it.)
- Per-tenant residency comes out as `sim.json -> tenants.<tenant>.kv_time_token_us`.
  Convert to seconds by dividing by 1e6 (the real side is already in seconds).

## 9. The comparison and the figure

For each cell (workload x rate point), compute:

- Per tenant: `sim_residency_s = kv_time_token_us / 1e6` vs real
  `residency_token_seconds`. Ratio and absolute percent error.
- `rho_mt_real = max/min` over real per-tenant residency; `rho_mt_sim` likewise
  for sim; and the absolute percent error between them. **This is the headline
  number.** Under W5 it is well above 1; the claim is sim reproduces it.

Plot **fidelity vs offered load**:

- x-axis: aggregate rate (6 ... 30).
- One curve: `rho_mt_real` and `rho_mt_sim` (they should track; the gap between
  them is the fidelity).
- Mark the saturation knee of **each** system (the rate at which mean end-to-end
  latency turns up sharply). Read the real knee from the trace's
  `last_chunk_time_us - send_time_us`; read the sim knee from `sim.json` request
  completion times. State plainly: below both knees, fidelity is high; above
  either knee, the latency model bounds fidelity.

The `figures/vllmparityexperiment/etl/stage3_extract.py` and `stage4_aggregate.py`
already do the per-tenant join and the `rho_mt` computation for the homogeneous
cells. Extend them to read the swept cells (add the `w5_sweep`/`w7_sweep`
directories to the cell list) and to plot against rate.

## 10. What success looks like

- In the **unsaturated** rate points, `rho_mt_sim` matches `rho_mt_real` to within
  a small tolerance (single-digit percent), at a `rho_mt` well above 1. This is
  the load-bearing result: the meter reads real, structural unfairness the way
  the simulator does.
- The fidelity-vs-load curve shows where the two systems' saturation points sit
  and that fidelity degrades only beyond them, for the understood latency-model
  reason. Reporting this honestly is stronger than a single lucky rate.

## 11. Checklist for the implementer

- [ ] Apply the §4 header fix to `vllm/v1/request.py`, rebuild the image, point
      the manifest at the new tag.
- [ ] Verify with the two-curl `/metrics` test that two tenant labels appear.
- [ ] Generate the W5 specs for aggregate rates 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 (and W7 if doing
      the robustness cell).
- [ ] Run `blis observe` + `postprocess_trace.py` once per spec against the
      patched server; save `trace.yaml`, `trace.csv`, `summary.json` per cell.
- [ ] Replay each trace through patched `blis-kvtime` (FCFS, warmup 0); save
      `sim.json` per cell.
- [ ] Join per tenant; compute `rho_mt_real`, `rho_mt_sim`, and the per-tenant
      errors **using `server_input_tokens` from `trace.csv`, not the nominal
      count**.
- [ ] Plot `rho_mt` (real and sim) vs aggregate rate, mark each system's
      saturation knee, and report the tolerance in the unsaturated regime.

items.title: feat(ai): 端到端 ETL Ingestion 管道与幂等去重生命周期治理 (RagIngestionTemplate)
items.body:
## Parent

#719

## What to build

As a knowledge base administrator, I want an atomic one-line ingestion facade `RagIngestionTemplate.ingest(...)` that orchestrates parsing, governance metadata injection, chunking, embedding, and storage, supporting `OVERWRITE` and `SKIP` deduplication policies, cascading document deletion, and managed asynchronous execution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `RagIngestionTemplate` facade implemented with `ingest(Resource/File/InputStream, IngestOptions)`.
- [ ] Automated execution sequence: format probing -> text/multimodal parsing -> metadata enrichment -> splitting -> batch embedding -> vector storage.
- [ ] Every chunk tagged with standard governance metadata: `doc_id`, `doc_name`, `doc_hash` (SHA-256), `tenant_id`, `created_at`, `chunk_index`.
- [ ] Deduplication policies implemented: `OVERWRITE` (purges old chunks matching `doc_id` before inserting new chunks) and `SKIP` (skips re-processing if `doc_hash` already exists).
- [ ] Symmetrical cascading cleanup method `deleteDocument(String docId)` purging all associated vector chunks from the `EmbeddingStore`.
- [ ] Asynchronous execution `ingestAsync(...)` leveraging Core managed thread pools (`ThreadPoolTaskExecutor`), propagating 4D context snapshots (MDC, tenant, user) and providing completion callbacks.
- [ ] Unit tests testing end-to-end ingestion, SHA-256 deduplication, overwrite replacement, cascading deletion, and async execution.

## Blocked by

- #720 — `feat(ai): Embedding 多模型命名注册表与动态切源 (EmbeddingModelRegistry)`
- #721 — `feat(ai): 多源异构文档解析基础 SPI 与文本/HTML解析器 (DocumentParserManager)`
- #724 — `feat(ai): 高级切分套件：Token 预算防溢出与父子分级切片 (Token & Parent-Child Splitters)`

items.title: Skill：存储、版本和加载，ETL 提示词迁成 Skill
items.body:
第 1 阶段设计调整的一部分（设计说明：https://claude.ai/artifact/LYST4MWq6Rfss1V2DBbeWT ）。接口约定见 `docs/api/apps-and-skills.md`。

## 做什么
- Skill 采用开放的 Agent Skills 格式：SKILL.md 正文 + 可选的 `references/*.md`；第 1 阶段只支持文字，不支持脚本。
- Postgres 存储 Skill 和版本（预留 `tenant_id`），提供 `/skills` 接口：列表、详情、指定版本、新建、保存草稿、删除草稿、发布。已发布的版本不可修改。
- 平台内置 Skill 放在 `backend/src/aep/skills/builtin/<name>/SKILL.md`，第一次启动时登记为版本 1。
- ETL 的"出方案"和"写代码"两段系统提示词拆成两部分：做法和规则迁到 `etl-plan`、`etl-codegen` 两个 Skill；JSON 输出格式要求留在代码里，由平台拼接。改 Skill 不会破坏输出解析。
- 节点通过 `AppContext` 按应用版本里锁定的 Skill 版本加载 Skill（版本锁定见 #48）。

## 验收标准
- 后端测试覆盖：内置 Skill 登记、草稿到发布的版本递增、已发布版本不可改、名称和长度校验、提示词由 Skill 加输出格式拼成。
- 使用默认 Skill 时，ETL 评测集结果与迁移前一致。

items.title: [Spec] Blueprint §33-§35 + §XII Layer 8: Data Moat strategy — 35 schemas longitudinal telemetry, vector embeddings, event log

labels.name: spec
labels.description: Spec-driven issue derived from engineering-spec-v1.0 or Blueprint v1.8

items.body:
## Frontmatter

---
owner: platform
depends_on: [21, 33, 41, 19]
blocks: []
spec_sections: ["section-4.1", "section-4.2", "section-4.3", "patch-1.7"]
blueprint_sections: ["section-33", "section-34", "section-35"]
maturity_target: lender_ready
acceptance:
  - All 35 schema categories implemented in PostgreSQL with correct domain grouping: schemas 1-25 (readiness), 26-30 (credit), 31-35 (BAI-powered)
  - Schemas 31-35 confirmed operational: lender_intelligence_realtime (BLIN), industry_benchmarks (BII), macro_market_indicators (BMS), predicted_funding_outcomes (BPFS), personalization_features (ML feature store)
  - Event log schema implemented: every score change, module completion, coaching interaction, document upload, and funding outcome recorded with timestamp, tenant_id, user_id, event_type, and payload
  - Audit log schema implemented: every admin action, data access by advisor, bureau pull consent, and data deletion request recorded with actor, target, action, and timestamp
  - Vector embeddings pipeline: business profile and coaching interaction summaries embedded via OpenAI embeddings and stored in Pinecone/Weaviate for similar-business case study retrieval
  - Snowflake ETL pipeline (dbt) ingests all 35 schema tables on a daily schedule for long-term warehouse analytics
  - Data compounding proof: a platform-level report demonstrates that BPFS accuracy improves as funded outcome records accumulate (measurable moat evidence)
  - Cross-tenant aggregation guardrails: tenant data used for aggregate ML training only with appropriate anonymization; no cross-tenant PII leakage
  - Data retention lifecycle enforced per §4.4: PII purged at 7 years post-last-activity or on verified deletion request
---

## Details

Implements the Data Moat strategy from Blueprint v1.8 §33 (The Closed Loop Only Bankable Owns), §34 (35 Data Schemas), and §35 (9 Moat-Forming Schemas), plus Layer 8 of the 12-Layer Architecture (Data Layer).

Per Blueprint v1.8 §35: The closed loop only BANKABLE owns: Credit Position -> Cash Flow Intelligence -> Lender Match -> Capital Outcomes. Banks have credit but no cash flow. Plaid has cash flow but no credit. Credit repair shops have credit but no lender match. Lender matchmakers have lender data but no credit position. Bankable has all four.

The 9 moat-forming schemas (§35):
1. bankability_scores (longitudinal score history per business)
2. credit_positions (tri-bureau + business credit longitudinal)
3. cash_flow_telemetry (Plaid-fed transaction and pattern data)
4. lender_outcomes (funded outcomes, terms, approval/denial history)
5. lender_intelligence_realtime (BLIN - actual lender underwriting behavior)
6. industry_benchmarks (BII - industry-adjusted norms)
7. macro_market_indicators (BMS - rate environment, credit cycle signals)
8. predicted_funding_outcomes (BPFS - per-business per-lender approval probability)
9. personalization_features (ML feature store for adaptive intelligence)

The moat compounds because every new funded outcome makes BPFS more accurate, every new lender outcome improves BLIN, and every new industry cohort improves BII. The data advantage grows with scale in a way competitors cannot replicate without years of similar transaction volume.

References: Blueprint v1.8 §33 Data Moat, §34 35 Data Schemas, §35 9 Moat-Forming Schemas, §XII Layer 8 Data Layer, Spec Patch 1.7, engineering-spec-v1.0.html §4.1, §4.2

items.title: [Epic] Refactor Network Analysis

type.name: Epic
type.description: Highest-level description of the product or a major delivery of functionality.

items.body:
# High-Performance eBPF Network Telemetry Engine

## Background Story

Multi-tenant OpenStack needs precise, line-rate, per-tenant network accounting for downstream billing. This epic productizes a **kernel-resident eBPF telemetry agent** that classifies every packet at the VM's tap, attributes it to the owning tenant, and exposes cumulative, billing-grade Prometheus counters.

Implementation lives in `bigstack-oss/lachesis` (formerly `cube-cos-network-telemetry`); the canonical design is `docs/DESIGN.md` in that repo. This issue is the umbrella; the User Stories and Features below decompose it by architecture layer (L1 data plane → L4 exporter) plus foundation and integration.

### Architecture (as built)

```
L4  Prometheus custom Collector + WAL          (bigstack-oss/lachesis#99)
L3  Go agent: scraper, delta math, boot,       (bigstack-oss/lachesis#77 classification)
    netlink dynamic attach, zombie hunter
L2  OpenStack metadata via Neutron v2.0 API,   (bigstack-oss/lachesis#88 control plane)
    LPM trie + MAC->tenant map
L1  eBPF TC clsact (ingress+egress at the tap) (bigstack-oss/lachesis#73 data plane)
```

## Success Criteria

- [x] **In-kernel line-rate accounting** via eBPF **TC `clsact`** (ingress + egress on each VM tap). XDP was evaluated and rejected — it is ingress-only on a tap and lacks `bpf_skb_ct_lookup`.
- [x] **Per-tenant zone classification** into six zones — `external`, `same_tenant`, `other_tenant`, `infra`, `shared`, `miss` — via a hybrid MAC-first / LPM-trie lookup, plus a `tx`/`rx` direction (VM-frame). (Richer than the original four-profile sketch.)
- [x] **OpenStack metadata** synced at cold-start through the **Neutron v2.0 REST API** (direct DB/MySQL access was considered and rejected — schema churn + blast radius; see DESIGN §C.3). Multi-hop static-route attribution included.
- [x] **Cumulative Prometheus counters** (`lachesis_bytes_total` / `lachesis_packets_total`, labels `tenant_id, zone, external_network, direction`) emitted by a **custom Collector** backed by a **Write-Ahead Log** for restart continuity. Billing model + consumption contract documented (DESIGN §11.5).
- [x] **Crash resilience** for the data path: read-don't-clear scrape, WAL restore, kernel-side drop counters; graceful shutdown is lossless.
- [x] Operator surface: `/debug` pages (topology, zones, lookup, flows, anomalies) + pprof; per-subsystem health metrics.
- [x] **Live metadata updates** — Kafka consumer (`notifications.info`, oslo) kicks a single-applier reconciler, plus a 5-minute periodic reconcile safety net.
- [x] **State lifecycle** — 60s Lingering-Ghost GC sweep, UnresolvedBuffer late-binding (10k-LRU cap + resolve write-back), and pressure-relief cold-flow GC.

- [x] **Live scenario-validation harness (`scenariotest`)** — automated cluster-level e2e incl. step-scripted operational scenarios (bigstack-oss/lachesis#123), running multi-node since 2026-07-16 (first 3-node HA deployment: agents on every hypervisor, per-node Prometheus scrape, multi-agent dashboards); routed-zone live runs on the HA cluster remain (bigstack-oss/lachesis#129).
- [x] **Per-server billing export** — mortal `lachesis_server_bytes_total` family, `external_network` label + attribution rules, multi-agent dashboards, live-validated on staging (bigstack-oss/lachesis#107, #118; CMP-side ETL tracked in bigstack-oss/cubecmp#837).
- [x] **Per-flow external-network attribution** — the `external_network` label resolves per flow from the peer router-interface MAC (three tiers: router-MAC → per-VM FIP/gateway-IP fallback → `none`), with a router-regateway settle fold preserving series monotonicity; flow-granular evidence queryable at `/debug/flows`, and the `multi-external-path` scenario asserts all three tiers with flow-peer gates reading the agents' own flow keys (bigstack-oss/lachesis#146; drive MAC-learn gate bigstack-oss/lachesis#153).
- [ ] **Netlink attach-presence robustness** — present-but-unattached gauge + periodic re-attach reconciler, closing the missed-NEWLINK silent-loss gap (bigstack-oss/lachesis#84).
- [ ] **Octavia LB re-attribution** — two-segment MAC-flag mechanism designed (conntrack refinement optional); not yet built (Octavia feature bigstack-oss/lachesis#131).
- [x] **eBPF map pinning** for zero-loss *agent-crash* recovery — today agent-crash recovery is WAL-bounded (≤ scrape/flush window), same as hard reboot (bigstack-oss/lachesis#83).
- [ ] **IPv6 zone resolution** — all v6 currently classifies `miss` (bigstack-oss/lachesis#132).
- [ ] **CubeCOS platform integration** — systemd packaging + build pipeline (bigstack-oss/lachesis#113).

## Existing Solution

Legacy tooling — sFlow sampling, OVS flow scraping, userspace packet parsing — cannot do per-tenant accounting at 10 Gbps+ without packet loss or CPU starvation, and it loses tenant context whenever traffic crosses an infrastructure proxy (router, load balancer, NAT). This epic replaces that approach with in-kernel classification at the tap.

## Practical Use Cases

1. **Monetization:** high-fidelity data foundation for traffic-based billing.
2. **Public-cloud parity:** comparable to AWS VPC Flow Logs / GCP Network Intelligence.
3. **Efficiency:** returns CPU to customer workloads vs. legacy userspace monitoring.

> **Live status:** tracked on the **[Bigstack] Scrum board** + Insights (story-point sums + burn-up), not in this body.

## Output artifacts (Definition of Done)

> Beyond code, docs, and config changes, completing this issue must also deliver:

- [ ] **Handbook knowledge update** — land the durable, team-readable knowledge from this
      work into the bigstack-handbook cubecos kb (`kb/cubecos/…`) via
      `/bigstack-core:save-to-handbook` (Topic / Runbook / Known-issue / ADR as fits).

items.title: [BUG] gold/metrics/tms lacks tenant dimension - cross-tenant metric leakage via query API and broken tenant-scoped notebooks

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: Possible defect or something isn't working as documented or expected

items.body:
# `gold/metrics/tms` has no tenant dimension - cross-tenant metric leakage and broken tenant-scoped consumers

## Problem

`MetricsTMSETL` (added in 86c32be) aggregates `gold/transactions` and `gold/evaluation` - both tenant-scoped tables - into `gold/metrics/tms`, but groups **only by time dimensions** (`metric_year/month/date/hour/quarter`). The `tenant_id` column is dropped entirely, so `transactions_received`, `transactions_evaluated`, `avg_evaluation_time_ms`, `p95_evaluation_time_ms`, and `dq_excluded_count` are all cross-tenant blends.

## Consequences

1. **Cross-tenant data leakage via the lakehouse query API.** `datalakehouse-api/lakehouse_query_api.py` enforces tenant isolation by filtering on `tenant_id` *when the column exists*, and logs "tenant isolation skipped for this table" when it does not. `metrics_tms` is a registered queryable table (`table_paths` map), so **any tenant's JWT can read platform-wide TMS throughput and latency metrics that include every other tenant's activity**. In a multi-tenant deployment this is an isolation defect, not a cosmetic gap.

2. **Per-tenant TMS metrics are impossible to derive.** The table cannot answer "what was tenant X's received-vs-evaluated rate" - the grain does not exist.

3. **Tenant-scoped consumers break.** `JupyterHub/notebooks/Lakehouse_Catalog.ipynb` scopes every table load through a strict `load_tenant_hudi` helper that raises when no tenant column is present. Its catalog loop (section 3) now hard-fails on any warehouse containing `gold/metrics/tms`:

   ```
   ValueError: Hudi table at /opt/Tazama_Warehouse/gold/metrics/tms has no tenant filter column;
   expected one of ('tenant_id', 'tx_tenant_id', 'tenantid')
   ```

   This reproduces on **every fresh deployment** of `dev` - the notebook's strict tenant scoping (44f45db, 2026-07-10) and the metrics ETL (86c32be, 2026-08-19) have been mutually incompatible since August.

4. **The incompatibility was previously noticed and bypassed instead of fixed.** `TMS_Performance_Dashboard.ipynb` contains the same strict helper but loads the metrics table with a raw `spark.read.format("hudi").load(...)` annotated `# tenant-agnostic aggregate table`. The workaround masks the isolation gap.

## Proposed fix

Fix the ETL, not the consumers:

- Add `tenant_id` to the aggregation `groupBy` keys, the Hudi record key (`hoodie.datasource.write.recordkey.field`), and the output schema of `MetricsTMSETL`.
- Rebuild the table - it is a derived aggregate and can be regenerated from `gold/transactions` + `gold/evaluation` at any time.

**Dual-grain caveat:** a platform-wide view cannot be fully reconstructed from per-tenant rows (`p95_evaluation_time_ms` does not roll up across tenants; `avg` needs weighting). If platform-level metrics are still required, the ETL should write both grains in the same table, e.g. per-tenant rows plus a `tenant_id = '__ALL__'` platform grain computed from the raw latency rows the ETL already retains for correct rollups. The query API's tenant filter would then naturally scope tenants to their own rows, and whether tenants may also see the `__ALL__` grain becomes an explicit policy decision instead of an accident.

Follow-ups once the ETL is fixed:

- Replace the raw-read bypass in `TMS_Performance_Dashboard.ipynb` with the standard `load_tenant_hudi` scope.
- No change needed in `Lakehouse_Catalog.ipynb` - it works as designed once the column exists.
- Consider making the query API's "tenant isolation skipped" path fail-closed (deny by default, explicit allowlist for genuinely global tables) so the next tenant-less table cannot silently leak.

## Environment / evidence

- Observed on the rebuilt AWS sandbox (2026-09-16), warehouse at `/opt/Tazama_Warehouse`, 59 Hudi tables discovered.
- Live `gold/metrics/tms` schema confirmed via Spark: `metric_quarter, metric_hour, metric_granularity, transactions_received, transactions_evaluated, received_vs_evaluated_rate_pct, avg_evaluation_time_ms, p95_evaluation_time_ms, evaluation_count, dq_excluded_count, written_at_ts, metric_year, metric_month, metric_date` - no tenant column, matching ETL source exactly (no server-side drift).

items.title: 应用配置与版本：节点设置、发布前评测、回滚
items.body:
第 1 阶段设计调整的一部分（设计说明：https://claude.ai/artifact/LYST4MWq6Rfss1V2DBbeWT ）。接口约定见 `docs/api/apps-and-skills.md`。

## 做什么
- 每个应用在代码里声明哪些节点有哪些可调设置（模型、Skill、参数），以及默认配置（即版本 1）。
- Postgres 存储应用版本（预留 `tenant_id`），提供 `/apps` 接口：列表、详情（设计、节点、可调设置、当前版本、草稿、可选模型和 Skill）、版本列表、保存或删除草稿、草稿评测、发布、回滚。
- 发布前评测：有评测集的应用（etl），草稿要先在后台跑评测集，平均分达到阈值（`AEP_EVAL_PUBLISH_THRESHOLD`，默认 0.8）才能发布。评测复用 `aep.evals` 的打分逻辑。
- 运行记录 `app_version`；`POST /runs` 可指定版本，不指定就用当前版本。运行中途重启后仍使用同一版本的配置。
- 流程视图显示每个模型节点这次用的模型、Skill 版本和实际提示词。
- 人工确认的提问和审批记录抽成 `aep.runtime.human`，ETL 的方案确认和上线审批都改用它。
- `GET /apps/{app}` 的可选模型列表从模型网关读取。

## 验收标准
- 后端测试覆盖：配置校验、草稿到发布、评测未通过不能发布、回滚、运行锁定版本（包括重启后恢复）、流程视图里的 Skill 和提示词。
- 现有 ETL 测试和评测行为不变。

items.title: G2 — Compras: as 14 operações estão no contrato e o módulo tem um arquivo só
items.body:
Macro-trilho **G2** da leva Softlux fase 2 (`prompts-leva-softlux-fase2.md`, pasta Cowork
`Vertz ERP (1)/`). Decisão do user 2026-08-22: executar os 15.

Norte obrigatório: `comparativo-softlux/` vols. 00-09 (mesma pasta) — o vol. citado no prompt é a
espec funcional.

## Prompt da leva — verbatim

```
Leia a memória do projeto e execute a issue #162 — o módulo COMPRAS nasce. Fonte:
comparativo-softlux/03-compras.md (fluxo completo) e 01-cadastros.md §2 (pré-requisitos do
fornecedor). O ActivityDto já aceita entityType purchaseOrder — a entidade que faltava é esta.

FASE A (web, contrato — serial): PurchaseRequest (pedido: N fornecedores, item com DESTINO
estoque×venda, elo opcional com Order de venda) · PurchaseOrder (ordem: 1 fornecedor, agrupa itens
de N pedidos rastreando origem POR ITEM, datas ordem/envio/prevista/REAGENDAMENTO, empresa
compradora, faturamento mínimo ecoado, transportadora, desconto/acréscimo, aba pagamento
reutilizando payment-terms do G1) · transições (enviar, reagendar, cancelar) · consultas: previsão
de chegada + compras para estoque/reserva (consome quantity_allocated da 0035).
FASE B (api): 2 migrações <reservar> (pedido, ordem — merge serial entre elas) · módulo compras ·
regras: ordem valida faturamento mínimo do fornecedor (geral + por grupo quando existir) · item
rastreia pedido de origem · integração com reserva de estoque (0035).
FASE C (web, telas): listagem + documento dos dois, padrão TelaDeDocumento/Secao da fusão v5;
navegação pedido↔ordem (botões do legado) · vínculo com o pedido de venda.

Pré-requisito DENTRO do trilho (fase A0, api+contrato mínimos): fornecedor ganha empresa
compradora com vigência + prazo de entrega + faturamento mínimo por grupo (vol. 01 §2 — ainda ❌).
DoD: padrão da casa · fluxo provado no par local: pedido de venda → pedido de compra → ordem →
consulta de previsão.
```

## Estado MEDIDO em 2026-08-23 (antes de começar, re-medir)

- **Fase A0 + A ENTREGUES** (web#316): 14 operações (95 → 109), 18 schemas, 4 URNs, tag `compras`.
  Publicadas: `/api/purchase-requests` (+`{id}`, `/cancel`), `/api/purchase-orders`
  (+`{id}`, `/send`, `/reschedule`, `/cancel`), `/api/purchases/arrival-forecast`,
  `/api/purchases/stock-replenishment`. Fase A0 junto: fornecedor com prazo de entrega,
  faturamento mínimo geral e **por grupo** (`SupplierBuyingCompanyDto` com vigência).
- **Fase B PARCIAL** (api#135 na `main`; a #129 foi **fechada sem merge** — conteúdo já estava lá,
  e o que sobrava era regressão em três pontos): migrações `0037_fornecedor_e_pedido_de_compra`,
  `0038_ordem_de_compra`, mais `0056_condicao_de_pagamento_na_compra` e
  `0057_correcoes_da_revisao_de_compras`.
- **Fase C ENTREGUE pelo trilho VISUAL, no mock**: `src/features/pedido-compra/` e
  `src/features/ordem-compra/` existem no web.

**O RESÍDUO, medido e é grande: `src/modules/compras/` tem UM arquivo — `faturamento-minimo.ts`.**
Não há `rotas.ts`. As **14 operações de compra estão publicadas no contrato e sem handler no api**
— declaradas como dívida com dono em seis guardas quando a api#131 sincronizou o contrato. É
exatamente a situação que o CLAUDE.md do web chama de *contrato maior que o backend*: a operação
responde **501**, e o mock cobre a tela.

Este trilho fecha quando as 14 saírem das allowlists e passarem a servir de verdade — e aí a
família inteira entra em `src/mocks/rotas-do-backend.ts` do web (a unidade de ligação é a FAMÍLIA,
nunca a rota: meia família põe id do servidor de um lado e id inventado do outro).

## Zona declarada

- **api (o grosso do que falta)**: `src/modules/compras/` (nasce `rotas.ts`; `faturamento-minimo.ts`
  já existe e é módulo PURO, 16 casos sem Postgres) · `src/core/http/servidor.ts` (mapa de
  handlers) · `src/core/http/classificacao.ts` (matriz de papéis) · `MapaDeCampos` das duas
  listagens · as seis allowlists que hoje declaram a dívida (`inventario-de-501`,
  `cobertura-do-contrato`, `filtros-do-contrato`, `ordenaveis-do-contrato`, `papeis`,
  `servicos-do-contrato`) · `migrations/<reservar>` **só se faltar índice** — as 4 tabelas já
  existem.
- **web**: `src/mocks/rotas-do-backend.ts` (a família inteira, num PR só) ·
  `src/data/<recurso>-api.test.ts` contra servidor falso.
- **Fora da zona**: `contracts/openapi-v1.json` — a fase A já mergeou; mexer nele aqui reabre a
  fila serial sem motivo.

## Faixa de migração — CONFERIR NA HORA

`migrations/` da `main` do api vai até **`0075_servico_da_empresa.sql`**; **próximo livre: `0076`**.
Medido 2026-08-23: as reservas escritas nas issues abertas (#110 #111 #112 #113 #114 #115 #116
#117 #118 #120 #122) são todas **≤ `0047` e estão vencidas** — a `main` passou por cima delas.
A única PR aberta com migração é a **#126** (`0040`/`0041` de tesouraria), superada pela `0065` já
mergeada. **Reservar nesta issue, num bloco `## RESERVA DE MIGRACAO`, antes de codar**, conferindo
`migrations/` **e** as issues abertas no momento — número em issue velha não vale nada, e número
em branch viva vale mais que número em issue.

## DoD (padrão da casa, por fase = 1 PR)

- `biome` + `check-types` + suíte verde · **prova negativa com piso por IGUALDADE** (tabela nova
  com `tenant_id` entra na bateria no MESMO commit).
- **Guardas provadas VERMELHAS antes do verde** — verde de primeira não prova nada.
- Problem Details do **vocabulário fechado**; operação nova nasce exigindo sessão, com 401 e 403
  por `$ref`.
- Contrato muda **só por PR no `cabinet-erp-web`**, serial: a fase-A de um G mergeia antes de a
  fase-A do próximo abrir. O api roda `sync:contract` + codegen **no mesmo commit**, depois do
  merge no web.
- Telas medidas no **par local** (`VITE_API_PROXY=http://localhost:3000 pnpm dev`) — o `*` dos
  padrões do MSW casa `localhost:3000` e mede o mock achando que mede o servidor.
- Commit Conventional ≤50 char · branch própria + worktree · **nunca `main`** · merge serial ·
  bloco `## Para o hub` na PR.

items.title: Phase 5 — Data Platform, BI, IA éducative et reporting institutionnel
items.body:
## Objectif
Transformer SchoolFlow Pro en plateforme data-driven : entrepôt analytique, tableaux de bord BI, indicateurs institutionnels, IA éducative, scoring étudiant, prédiction du décrochage, reporting ministère et pilotage stratégique.

Cette phase doit capitaliser sur les phases précédentes : production, sécurité, observabilité, SaaS, quotas et multi-tenant.

---

## Périmètre Phase 5

### 1. Data warehouse éducatif
- Créer une couche analytique séparée de l’OLTP opérationnel.
- Préparer schémas `bronze`, `silver`, `gold` ou équivalent.
- Construire des marts analytiques : élèves, inscriptions, présences, notes, finances, enseignants, campus, paiements.
- Prévoir refresh incrémental.
- Ne pas ralentir la base opérationnelle.

### 2. Modèle décisionnel BI
- Créer dimensions : date, tenant, campus, classe, niveau, programme, matière, enseignant, élève, parent, statut paiement.
- Créer faits : inscriptions, présences, notes, factures, paiements, absences, incidents, communications, connexions.
- Préparer modèle étoile compatible Superset/Metabase/Power BI.

### 3. Dashboards Superset / BI
- Dashboard direction établissement.
- Dashboard finance scolaire.
- Dashboard pédagogique.
- Dashboard présence/absentéisme.
- Dashboard multi-campus.
- Dashboard ministère / institution : indicateurs agrégés anonymisés.
- Dashboard SaaS platform usage si nécessaire.

### 4. Indicateurs clés éducatifs
- Taux de présence.
- Taux d’absentéisme.
- Moyenne par classe/matière/campus.
- Taux de réussite.
- Taux d’impayés.
- Recouvrement financier.
- Charge enseignants.
- Risque décrochage.
- Evolution inscriptions.
- Performance par période académique.

### 5. IA éducative
- Résumé automatique d’un élève.
- Recommandations pédagogiques.
- Détection d’élèves à risque.
- Aide à la rédaction de bulletins/commentaires.
- Assistant direction : synthèse activité établissement.
- Assistant parent : explication simple des notes/absences.
- Assistant enseignant : suggestions d’accompagnement.

### 6. ML prédictif
- Scoring risque décrochage.
- Scoring impayés.
- Prédiction absentéisme.
- Détection anomalies notes/paiements.
- Modèle simple au départ : règles + features SQL.
- Evolution future : scikit-learn / XGBoost / MLflow.

### 7. Gouvernance et confidentialité
- Anonymisation pour reporting institutionnel.
- Séparation données opérationnelles et analytiques.
- RLS analytique par tenant/campus/rôle.
- Masquage PII dans les vues ministère.
- Journalisation des exports BI.

### 8. Pipelines data
- Préparer jobs ETL/ELT async ou DBT.
- Option 1 : vues matérialisées PostgreSQL.
- Option 2 : dbt + PostgreSQL analytique.
- Option 3 futur : Airflow + warehouse séparé.
- Ajouter tests de qualité data : unicité, non-null, cohérence référentielle.

---

## Règles de sécurité
- Ne jamais exposer PII entre tenants.
- Les dashboards institutionnels doivent être anonymisés/agrégés.
- Les modèles IA ne doivent pas utiliser des données d’un tenant pour répondre à un autre tenant.
- Les exports doivent être journalisés.
- Toute vue analytique doit être filtrable par tenant ou explicitement globale/anonymisée.

---

## Découpage recommandé en PR

### PR 1 — Cadrage modèle analytique
- Ajouter `docs/data/ANALYTICS_MODEL.md`.
- Définir dimensions, faits, KPIs, règles de confidentialité.

### PR 2 — Vues analytiques PostgreSQL MVP
- Ajouter vues/matérialisées pour dashboard direction : élèves, présences, finances, notes.
- Ajouter migration non destructive.

### PR 3 — Data quality tests
- Ajouter tests SQL/pytest sur cohérence analytique.
- Vérifier tenant_id, dates, montants, statuts.

### PR 4 — Dashboard API analytics
- Ajouter endpoints API dashboard analytiques optimisés.
- Prévoir cache Redis court.

### PR 5 — Superset/BI pack
- Ajouter documentation connexion Superset.
- Ajouter datasets recommandés.
- Préparer export dashboard JSON si possible.

### PR 6 — IA éducative MVP
- Ajouter service de résumé élève.
- Ajouter garde-fous PII/tenant.
- Utiliser Groq/OpenRouter uniquement si clé configurée.

### PR 7 — Scoring risque décrochage V1
- Règles simples : absentéisme, baisse notes, impayés, retards.
- Score explicable, non bloquant.
- Dashboard alertes.

### PR 8 — Reporting institutionnel anonymisé
- Vues agrégées par région/campus/niveau/période.
- Pas de nom/prénom/email/téléphone.
- Documentation conformité.

---

## Critères d’acceptation
- Les données analytiques ne ralentissent pas les workflows opérationnels.
- Les KPIs direction sont disponibles avec cache ou vues optimisées.
- Les vues BI respectent le tenant isolation.
- Superset peut se connecter à un modèle propre sans requêter directement toutes les tables OLTP.
- Les premiers scores IA/ML sont explicables et non décisionnels.
- Le reporting institutionnel est anonymisé.
- Les exports analytiques sont traçables.
