items.body:
**Epic:** #7 · #16
**Depends on:** #24, #30
**Size:** M · **Milestone:** M0 Foundations
**Spec:** developer-spec.md §9 · shared-docs/specs/mv-go/A-data-model.md (branch mv-go)
**Branch:** `mv-go-T11-<topic>` cut from `mv-go`; PR into `mv-go` only, never `main` (R90)

## Scope
- minio-go client; `S3_ENDPOINT` for server-side calls and `S3_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT` (browser/APK-reachable origin used only to sign presigned URLs; local `http://localhost:9000`); in deployed environments the Caddy site `MEDIA_DOMAIN` fronts MinIO for presigned and public object URLs; `S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` = base URL of public-bucket objects (R74)
- `S3_BUCKET` private, `S3_PUBLIC_BUCKET` public (only `app_releases/`); `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is applied only to the private bucket's CORS
- `POST /v1/uploads/presign` -> `file_objects` pending (purpose, uploaded_by, tenant_id, expires_at) + presigned PUT (`S3_PRESIGN_PUT_TTL`, max `UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES`); commit = StatObject inside the entity tx
- `GET /v1/files?key=` 302 to presigned GET (`S3_PRESIGN_GET_TTL`); `storage.gc` hourly
- Evidence token helper (R30, R47): non-expiring when `EVIDENCE_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS=0`, revocable via `evidence_token_revoked_at` on `trip_records` and `standby_records`; a new token is minted only on the next forced LINE send; gallery images are short presigned GETs (`EVIDENCE_PRESIGN_TTL`)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Browser presigned PUT from `http://localhost:3000` succeeds against compose MinIO (CORS from `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`)
- [ ] Presigned URLs carry the `S3_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT` host, never the internal `S3_ENDPOINT` host
- [ ] Commit with wrong size/content-type -> 422, row stays pending; success -> committed
- [ ] Pending objects older than 24 h are deleted with their rows; committed objects never
- [ ] Presigned GET expires after its TTL; evidence token verifier accepts a token after 365 simulated days and rejects it after revocation

## Notes
- Deploy target is the single VM + compose (R30); only the `MEDIA_DOMAIN` name is an owner input (§19 Q8); presigned-only vs public-read photos is owner question §19 Q5; ETL dumps go to `S3_BUCKET` under `etl/dumps/{ts}/`

## Owner additions (2026-10-10): local disk storage until S3-compatible config exists
The first deployment (VM `showkhun.co`, pm2 + nginx, no S3 yet) stores uploads on the server's disk. This is part of this task.
- **Two backends behind one storage interface.** `local` (files under `LOCAL_MEDIA_DIR`, outside any web root) and `s3` (minio-go, as above). `STORAGE_BACKEND=local|s3` picks the backend for **new** uploads. Reads always dispatch on the object's own recorded backend, so local files keep working after the switch to `s3`. An optional later copy job can move them; none is needed for correctness. Retiring local means setting `STORAGE_BACKEND=s3` once the S3 env is filled in.
- **Every stored image says where it lives.** Add `file_objects.storage_backend text NOT NULL CHECK (storage_backend IN ('local','s3'))` in migration `0011+` (never edit 0002-0010). Then list every table that stores an image or file (e.g. trip photos, standby, incident, expense receipts, maintenance, chat attachments, driver/truck documents, company logo, broadcast media, APK releases) and how each reaches `file_objects`. Any table that keeps an image reference without a `file_objects` FK gets its own `storage_backend` column, or the FK, in the same migration. Put the table list in the spec (§9 / Appendix A) and in the PR.
- **Local upload flow mirrors presign/commit.** `POST /v1/uploads/presign` returns, for `local`, an upload URL on the API with an HMAC-signed, expiring token (same TTL `S3_PRESIGN_PUT_TTL`, same `UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES`, content-type allow-list). The upload route has its own body limit (the default Fiber limit is 4 MiB) and is reachable by the web (through the BFF) and by mobile (public listener). Commit = stat + size/type check of the file on disk inside the entity tx, as for S3. Writes are atomic (temp file + fsync + rename) and keys are validated against traversal (no `..`, no absolute paths, the S3 key layout reused). Files are mode 0640.
- **Local download URLs** are `${LOCAL_MEDIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/<key>`; on the deployment that is `https://logi.showkhun.co/media/<key>` (nginx maps `logi.showkhun.co/media/` to the Go public listener).
  - Private objects need a signed, expiring URL (same TTL as the presigned GET, `GET /v1/files?key=` 302s to it).
  - The public prefix `app_releases/` is unsigned.
  - Never serve a directory index: a path ending in `/` -> 404.
  - Serving may use `X-Accel-Redirect` to an internal nginx location, or stream from Go.
  - The `/media` route group on the public listener is an owner-approved widening of `PUBLIC_ROUTE_GROUPS` / `ingress.PublicPrefixes`: record it in spec §2.6 and ADR 0029 notes.
- **storage.gc and evidence work on both backends.** Pending local files older than 24 h are deleted with their rows.
- **New env names** (`STORAGE_BACKEND`, `LOCAL_MEDIA_DIR`, `LOCAL_MEDIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `LOCAL_MEDIA_SIGNING_KEY` (secret)) go into §16.1, `.env.example` and the compose anchors. Compose dev keeps `s3` (MinIO) as the default.
- **Extra acceptance criteria:**
  - with `STORAGE_BACKEND=local`, presign -> upload -> commit -> signed GET works end to end, and an expired or tampered signature -> 403;
  - after switching to `s3`, an object uploaded under `local` still downloads;
  - `file_objects.storage_backend` is set on every row;
  - a path traversal key is rejected;
  - a directory path returns 404.

items.title: SlaEscalationRecordsETL drops tenant_id in gold projection
items.body:
## Problem

`SlaEscalationRecordsETL` does not carry `tenant_id` through to the gold layer, so downstream consumers that filter by tenant cannot query `gold/sla_escalation_records`.

The gold layer uses an explicit `select(...)` that lists only `id`, `case_id`, `notified_at`, `notified_at_ts`, `sla_state`, `ingested_at_ts`, `source_file_path` — [`Table_ETLs/SlaEscalationRecordsETL.py` lines 79-87](https://github.com/tazama-lf/biar/blob/main/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/SlaEscalationRecordsETL.py#L79-L87). `tenant_id` is not projected, so even when it is present in the source JSON and survives bronze/silver, it is dropped in gold.

Bronze does not explicitly cast `tenant_id` either — [lines 33-42](https://github.com/tazama-lf/biar/blob/main/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/SlaEscalationRecordsETL.py#L33-L42) — so its type is not normalised the way peer ETLs do it.

This diverges from the convention used by every other tenant-scoped ETL in the same directory (`CasesETL`, `TasksETL`, `SlaEscalationThresholdsETL`), which cast `tenant_id` as `string` in bronze and silver and re-select it in gold. See `SlaEscalationThresholdsETL.py` lines 36, 60, 86 for the pattern.

## Logs

Lakehouse Catalog notebook, after ODS was updated to emit `tenant_id`, the warehouse `sla_escalation_records` bronze/silver/gold layers were truncated, and the NiFi pipeline was reset and restarted:

```
ValueError                                Traceback (most recent call last)
Cell In[4], line 45
     43 t0  = time.time()
     44 # Load the authoritative Hudi table used by downstream metrics.
---> 45 cnt = load_tenant_hudi(path).count()
     46 elapsed = time.time() - t0

Cell In[1], line 12, in load_tenant_hudi(path, **options)
     10 tenant_col = next((c for c in TENANT_FILTER_COLUMNS if c in df.columns), None)
     11 if tenant_col is None:
---> 12     raise ValueError(
     13         f"Hudi table at {path} has no tenant filter column; "
     14         f"expected one of {TENANT_FILTER_COLUMNS}"
     15     )

ValueError: Hudi table at /opt/Tazama_Warehouse/gold/sla_escalation_records has no tenant filter column; expected one of ('tenant_id', 'tx_tenant_id', 'tenantid')
```

## Proposed solution

Update `automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/SlaEscalationRecordsETL.py` to match the tenant-carrying pattern already used by `SlaEscalationThresholdsETL`:

1. In `bronze()` (line 33-42): add `.withColumn(\"tenant_id\", F.col(\"tenant_id\").cast(\"string\"))`.
2. In `silver()` (line 55-63): add `.withColumn(\"tenant_id\", F.col(\"tenant_id\").cast(\"string\"))`.
3. In `gold()` `select(...)` (line 79-87): add `F.col(\"tenant_id\").cast(\"string\").alias(\"tenant_id\")`.

No schema changes required elsewhere — `tenant_id` is already emitted by NiFi from the ODS.

## Impact

- Lakehouse Catalog notebook cannot load `gold/sla_escalation_records`; the tenant filter step raises `ValueError` and downstream metrics dependent on this table fail.
- Any tenant-scoped query or view over SLA escalation records is blocked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gold/sla_escalation_records` contains a `tenant_id` column of type `string`.
- [ ] `silver/sla_escalation_records` and `bronze/sla_escalation_records` also contain `tenant_id`.
- [ ] `load_tenant_hudi(\"/opt/Tazama_Warehouse/gold/sla_escalation_records\")` returns a filtered DataFrame without raising.
- [ ] Behaviour matches `SlaEscalationThresholdsETL` for tenant column handling.

items.title: PRD: pbiadmin — Power BI tenant administration CLI
items.body:
﻿## Problem Statement

Power BI / Microsoft Fabric tenant administrators have no unified, scriptable CLI to inventory, back up, restore, and migrate artifacts across workspaces and tenants. The existing options are either point-and-click in the PBI web portal (no automation), the PowerShell `MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt` module (incomplete coverage, no Fabric Gen2 support), or raw REST API calls written from scratch each time. This creates risk: manual processes are error-prone, migrations are slow and untraceable, and there is no repeatable way to snapshot a tenant's state before a change.

## Solution

`pbiadmin` is a Python CLI toolkit and Copilot agent skill set for Power BI / Microsoft Fabric tenant administration. It lets administrators list, download, upload, delete, copy, and migrate artifacts (reports, datasets, dashboards, dataflows, paginated reports) across workspaces and tenants, with structured output, profile-based multi-tenant auth, and full CI/CD integration.

## User Stories

### Inventory
1. As a PBI admin, I want to list all workspaces in a tenant so that I can audit what exists before making changes.
2. As a PBI admin, I want to list all reports in a workspace so that I can see what content is published.
3. As a PBI admin, I want to list all datasets/semantic models in a workspace so that I can track data dependencies.
4. As a PBI admin, I want to list all dashboards in a workspace so that I have a complete inventory.
5. As a PBI admin, I want to list all dataflows (Gen1 and Gen2) in a workspace so that I know what ETL exists.
6. As a PBI admin, I want to list all paginated reports in a workspace so that I can manage them separately.
7. As a PBI admin, I want to export inventory as JSON or CSV so that I can import it into other systems or audit tools.

### Backup / Download
8. As a PBI admin, I want to download all PBIX reports from a workspace so that I have a local backup before changes.
9. As a PBI admin, I want to download all datasets from a workspace so that I can restore them if needed.
10. As a PBI admin, I want to download all dataflows (Gen1 and Gen2) from a workspace so that I can version them.
11. As a PBI admin, I want to download all paginated reports (.rdl/.rdlx) from a workspace for safekeeping.
12. As a PBI admin, I want to download a metadata+tile snapshot of dashboards (even though no native PBIX export exists) so that I have a partial backup of dashboard layout.
13. As a PBI admin, I want a `manifest.json` written alongside every download so that I know exactly what was captured and when.
14. As a PBI admin, I want existing files to be skipped (with a warning) on re-download so that I don't accidentally overwrite a manually-edited file.
15. As a PBI admin, I want a `--force` flag that overwrites existing files (renaming them to `.bak`) so that I can refresh a backup without losing the previous copy.

### Restore / Upload
16. As a PBI admin, I want to upload a PBIX file to a workspace so that I can restore a backed-up report.
17. As a PBI admin, I want to publish a PBIX file to a workspace so that I can deploy a new report.
18. As a PBI admin, I want to upload a dataset definition to a workspace so that I can restore data connectivity.
19. As a PBI admin, I want to import a dataflow JSON into a workspace so that I can restore ETL pipelines.
20. As a PBI admin, I want to upload a paginated report file to a workspace so that I can restore operational reports.
21. As a PBI admin, I want failed uploads to be written to an `errors.json` log so that I can remediate them individually.

### Delete
22. As a PBI admin, I want to delete a specific report from a workspace so that I can clean up stale content.
23. As a PBI admin, I want delete operations to require explicit confirmation so that I never accidentally remove production content.

### Copy & Migrate
24. As a PBI admin, I want to copy a report within the same tenant (different workspace) so that I can promote content through environments.
25. As a PBI admin, I want to migrate reports and datasets from one workspace to another so that I can restructure tenant layout.
26. As a PBI admin, I want to migrate artifacts across tenants (using two named profiles) so that I can move content between dev and prod Entra tenants.
27. As a PBI admin, I want `pbiadmin migrate` to detect a Premium-less target workspace upfront and surface a clear error so that I'm not surprised by a failure mid-migration.
28. As a PBI admin, I want to rebind dataset connections after upload so that cross-tenant migrations work end-to-end.
29. As a PBI admin, I want `--artifact-types` to filter what gets migrated so that I can migrate only reports without touching datasets.
30. As a PBI admin, I want `--dry-run` on migrate to show what would happen without transferring anything so that I can validate the plan first.

### Permissions
31. As a PBI admin, I want to set a user's role in a workspace so that I can manage access at scale.
32. As a PBI admin, I want to set a service principal's role in a workspace so that I can grant automation accounts access.
33. As a PBI admin, I want workspace name-to-id resolution so that I don't have to look up GUIDs manually.

### Auth & Configuration
34. As a PBI admin, I want named profiles in `profiles.toml` so that I can switch between tenants with `--profile prod`.
35. As a PBI admin, I want secrets loaded from env vars (not config files) so that credentials are never committed to git.
36. As a PBI admin, I want Service Principal auth mode for CI/CD pipelines so that automation works unattended.
37. As a PBI admin, I want interactive (device-code) auth mode for developer workstations so that I can authenticate with my own account.
38. As a PBI admin, I want token caching per profile so that I'm not prompted to re-authenticate on every command.

### Output & Observability
39. As a PBI admin, I want a rich table output by default so that I can read results at a glance in my terminal.
40. As a PBI admin, I want `--format json` output so that I can pipe results into `jq` or other tools.
41. As a PBI admin, I want `--format csv` output so that I can import results into Excel.
42. As a PBI admin, I want a structured `errors.json` per run so that I can identify exactly which items failed and why.
43. As a PBI admin, I want a `summary.json` per run (attempted/succeeded/failed/skipped counts) so that I can report on bulk operations.
44. As a PBI admin, I want `--verbose` mode to print HTTP request/response details so that I can debug API issues.
45. As a PBI admin, I want rate-limit (HTTP 429) handling with automatic backoff so that bulk operations complete without manual retries.
46. As a PBI admin, I want `--fail-fast` to abort on first error so that CI pipelines don't silently accumulate failures.

### CI/CD & Automation
47. As a DevOps engineer, I want a thin PowerShell wrapper (`pbiadmin.ps1`) so that I can call `pbiadmin` from Azure DevOps YAML pipelines without switching shells.
48. As a DevOps engineer, I want `PBIADMIN_PROFILE` env var support so that pipelines can select a profile without passing flags.

### Copilot Skills
49. As a developer using GitHub Copilot, I want a `pbi-list` skill so that I can ask "list all reports in workspace X" in natural language.
50. As a developer using GitHub Copilot, I want a `pbi-download` skill so that I can trigger a workspace backup via chat.
51. As a developer using GitHub Copilot, I want a `pbi-upload` skill so that I can restore artifacts via chat.
52. As a developer using GitHub Copilot, I want a `pbi-migrate` skill so that I can orchestrate cross-workspace migrations via chat.
53. As a developer using GitHub Copilot, I want a `pbi-permissions` skill so that I can manage workspace roles via chat.

## Implementation Decisions

### Language & Runtime
- Python 3.11+ only. `semantic-link`/`sempy` (required for Fabric Gen2 Dataflows) is Python-only, making Python the only viable single-language choice.
- Thin PowerShell wrapper scripts allowed only at the OS/CI boundary (not in the Python package).
- Package manager: `uv` with `pyproject.toml`. Replaces pip+venv.

### CLI Framework
- **Typer** for the CLI: auto-generated help, type validation, shell completion, subcommand groups.
- Root command: `pbiadmin`. Subcommand groups: `workspaces`, `reports`, `datasets`, `dashboards`, `dataflows`, `paginated`, `permissions`, `migrate`.

### Architecture — `src/` Layout
- `src/pbiadmin/` is the installable package. It cannot be imported without `uv pip install -e .`, preventing shadow imports.
- Layers: `cli/` (Typer commands) → `ops/` (operation logic) → `core/` (auth, client, config, output, errors) + `models/` (dataclasses) + `utils/` (retry, file helpers).

### Authentication
- `msal` Python library for all token acquisition (SP and interactive/device-code flows).
- Token caching per profile; automatic re-acquire on 401.
- Secrets never in config files — loaded from `PBIADMIN_{PROFILE}_CLIENT_SECRET` env vars or Azure Key Vault.

### Configuration
- `profiles.toml` stores non-secret profile config (tenant_id, client_id, auth_mode). Git-ignored by default; only `profiles.toml.example` committed.
- Profile selected via `--profile <name>` flag or `PBIADMIN_PROFILE` env var.

### API Layer
- PBI REST API (`requests`/`httpx`) for reports, datasets, dashboards, workspaces, permissions.
- `semantic-link`/`sempy` for Fabric Gen2 Dataflows; adapter pattern with REST fallback if sempy is incomplete.
- `fabric_client.py` isolated — no sempy imports in core `client.py`.

### File Output Structure
- `output/{tenant}/{workspace}/{artifact-type}/` — artifact files.
- `runs/{run_id}/errors.json` + `summary.json` — run logs.
- Conflict resolution: skip+warn (default), `--force` overwrites with `.bak`.

### Error Handling & Resilience
- Continue-on-error default for bulk operations; `--fail-fast` for CI.
- HTTP 429: exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries, capped at 60s.
- Structured error log: item id, artifact type, operation, HTTP status, message, timestamp.

### Skill Architecture
- Skills live in `.agent/skills/` (project-level, open-standards compatible).
- Five skills: `pbi-list`, `pbi-download`, `pbi-upload`, `pbi-migrate`, `pbi-permissions`.
- Each skill is a natural-language prompt that invokes `pbiadmin` CLI commands.

### Known Limitations
- Dashboards have no native PBIX export via PBI REST API. Export is metadata + tile JSON snapshot only.
- Fabric Gen2 Dataflows via sempy may lag PBI REST API feature parity; REST fallback documented.
- Importing PBIX to a workspace without Premium capacity will fail; `migrate` detects this upfront.
- Cross-tenant migration requires explicit post-upload `rebind` step for dataset connections.

## Testing Decisions

Good tests verify external behavior, not implementation details. A test should fail if and only if observable behavior changes.

### What to test
- **`core/auth.py`**: token acquisition for SP and interactive profiles (mock MSAL); missing profile raises clear error; token refresh on 401.
- **`core/config.py`**: loads valid `profiles.toml`; resolves secrets from env vars; rejects malformed config.
- **`core/client.py`**: injects Authorization header; retries on 429 with backoff; re-acquires token on 401.
- **`utils/retry.py`**: backoff timing, max retries, jitter bounds.
- **`core/output.py`**: table/JSON/CSV renderers produce correct output for a given data set.
- **`ops/` modules**: each operation calls the expected REST endpoint with the expected payload (mock `client`).
- **`cli/` commands**: Typer command routing, flag validation, `--dry-run` produces no side effects.

### Testing framework
- `pytest` + `pytest-mock`. Test files mirror the source tree under `tests/unit/` and `tests/integration/`.
- Integration tests require real credentials and are opt-in (`pytest -m integration`).
- No tests for `scripts/` (PS wrapper) or `.agent/skills/` (SKILL.md files).

## Out of Scope

- **Publishing to PyPI**: `pbiadmin` is a local admin tool, not a public library.
- **GUI or web interface**: CLI only.
- **Power BI Embedded / embed tokens**: not an admin use case.
- **Report rendering / screenshot capture**: not an artifact management operation.
- **Data-plane operations** (running queries, refreshing datasets via schedule): covered by existing PBI tooling.
- **Fabric items beyond Dataflows Gen2** (Lakehouses, Notebooks, Pipelines): future scope.
- **Workspace creation/deletion**: future scope.
- **Tenant-level settings** (capacity management, gateway config): future scope.
- **Windows-only features**: the Python package is cross-platform; only `scripts/pbiadmin.ps1` is Windows/PS-specific.

## Further Notes

- `pbi-tools` (by Bernat Agulló) is an existing third-party tool — the CLI root command must remain `pbiadmin`.
- Design document: `pbiadmin-design.md` in repo root (full pre-mortem session output).

### Child slices (implementation work items)

- #16 — S1: Project scaffold
- #17 — S2: Auth & profile config
- #18 — S3: REST API client + retry
- #19 — S4: Workspace listing (first working command)
- #20 — S5: Reports operations
- #21 — S6: Datasets operations
- #22 — S7: Dashboards operations
- #23 — S8: Dataflows Gen1 operations
- #24 — S9: Dataflows Gen2 / Fabric operations
- #25 — S10: Paginated Reports operations
- #26 — S11: Permissions management
- #27 — S12: Migration orchestration
- #28 — S13: Agent skills
- #29 — S14: PowerShell CI wrapper

items.title: Feature: Multipart upload API (initiate/upload/complete/abort)
items.body:
Implement the S3/Azure-compatible multipart upload lifecycle supporting up to 10,000 parts, out-of-order and re-uploaded parts, per-part checksum verification, idempotent completion, and quorum-per-part writes. Includes listing in-progress uploads and part listings for audit/cleanup.

items.title: DLH BUG: event_history.transaction data is not the source for gold/transactions in DLH

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: Possible defect or something isn't working as documented or expected

items.body:
## Description

`event_history.transaction` and the pacs.008/pacs.002 tables are **fundamentally different data sources**. . The current `gold/transactions` is built by `TransactionsETL` reading `bronze/pacs008` + `bronze/pacs002` — **this is the wrong source**. The NiFi `Transaction` processor that correctly extracts `event_history.transaction` to Ozone has been confirmed dead code: the automation orchestrator explicitly skips every batch it sends with the message `"Skipped: transactions are derived from PACS gold"`. The right data exists and is being discarded on every poll cycle.

**Related issues:**
- #108 — `transaction_data` naming collision (the `transactionData` column in `bronze/transactions` misrepresents the pacs payload as if it were `event_history.transaction` data — conceals this wrong-source problem; resolves as a natural consequence of this issue)
- #111 — downstream consumer updates (view builder and consumer code changes triggered by this issue)

---

## Guiding Principle

> **Principle:** The core TMS database tables — `event_history.transaction`, `event_history.entity`, `event_history.account`, and `event_history.account_holder` — are the definitive source of truth for all BIAR analytics and CMS views. Raw pacs message tables (`raw_history.pacs008`, `raw_history.pacs002`) should only be used as a source when information is genuinely not available in those core TMS tables.

Every issue in this ticket is a violation of this principle. The DLH pipeline currently uses raw pacs messages as the primary source for all transaction data, bypassing the core TMS tables entirely.

---

## How This Happened

Two mechanisms in `lakehouse_automation_pipeline.py` are responsible:

**1. The automation orchestrator skip guard** actively discards every `event_history.transaction` batch that NiFi sends:

```python
if table in ("transaction", "transactions"):
    return "Skipped: transactions are derived from PACS gold"
```

This is not a silent failure — it is an intentional but incorrect guard. NiFi receives HTTP 200 and never retries. The Ozone files at `{bucket}/transaction/` are written on every poll cycle and immediately ignored.

**2. `CombinedPacsETL`** (`Table_ETLs/CombinedPacs.py`) uses marker files to detect when both pacs tables reach Gold, then fires `TransactionsETL(mode="from_pacs")`. `Pacs008ETL` and `Pacs002ETL` have zero dependency on each other — the "combining" adds no value to their pipelines. `CombinedPacsETL` exists solely to trigger `TransactionsETL` from the wrong source. It must be **deleted**, not updated.

---

## Correct Architecture

| DLH table | Correct source | Current state |
|---|---|---|
| `gold/transaction` | `event_history.transaction` ODS exclusively (MVP); Gold layer pacs enrichment is post-MVP — see Design Requirement 6 | ❌ Does not exist — currently wrong-named `gold/transactions` built from pacs.008/002 |
| `gold/pacs008` | `bronze/pacs008` | ✅ Correct — pacs.008 ISO 20022 credit transfer messages |
| `gold/pacs002` | `bronze/pacs002` | ✅ Correct — pacs.002 ISO 20022 payment status messages |

---

## Structural Difference — What Each Source Provides

`event_history.transaction.transaction` JSONB is a **TMS-normalized flat record**:

```json
{"EndToEndId": "...", "Amt": 100, "Ccy": "USD", "MsgId": "...", "CreDtTm": "...", "TxTp": "pacs.008.001.10", "TxSts": "ACCC", "TenantId": "..."}
```

The table adds two FK-validated structural columns not present anywhere in the pacs schema:

- `source varchar NOT NULL` — FK to `event_history.account(id, tenantId)` — TMS debtor account ID
- `destination varchar NOT NULL` — FK to `event_history.account(id, tenantId)` — TMS creditor account ID

| Field | event_history.transaction | bronze/transactions (pacs — current wrong source) |
|---|---|---|
| `source` — TMS debtor account ID (FK to `account`) | ✅ Present for **all rows** — pacs.008 AND pacs.002 | ❌ Not present |
| `destination` — TMS creditor account ID (FK to `account`) | ✅ Present for **all rows** | ❌ Not present |
| `amt` / `ccy` — transaction amount and currency | ✅ Top-level `transaction->>'Amt'` / `'Ccy'` | pacs.008 only — null for every pacs.002 row |
| `txSts` — TMS-managed transaction status | ✅ Present for all rows | pacs.002 only — null for every pacs.008 row |
| Party identifiers (`entity.id` = `PrvtId.Othr[0].Id + SchmeNm.Prtry`, e.g. `+27730975224MSISDN`) | ✅ `source`/`destination` → `account` → `account_holder` → `entity.id` — all rows; `entity.id` is derived from the pacs.008 entity data | ✅ `CdtTrfTxInf.Dbtr.Id.PrvtId.Othr[0].Id` + scheme — pacs.008 only; entity join preferred because it covers pacs.002 rows |
| Party display names (`Dbtr.Nm` / `Cdtr.Nm`) | ❌ Not stored in TMS ODS — not a TMS data model concept | ⚠️ Transient pacs.008 message field — null for every pacs.002 row; current view builders use this incorrectly |
| Interbank settlement amount, exchange rate, agent IDs, charges | ⚠️ **Post-MVP:** not in MVP `gold/transaction`. Short-term: consumers needing `xchg_rate` or `intr_bk_sttlm_amt` add `LEFT JOIN gold/pacs008 ON (end_to_end_id, tenant_id)` at view layer | ✅ Source for short-term view join and post-MVP Gold enrichment |

---

## Design Requirements

### 1. Table name must be `transaction` (singular) — matching ODS source and NiFi routing attribute

- `bronze/transaction`, `silver/transaction`, `gold/transaction` (not plural). Drop and rebuild the existing plural-named tables.

### 2. Source: `event_history.transaction` exclusively — all tiers (MVP scope)

`bronze/transaction`, `silver/transaction`, and `gold/transaction` must all be sourced from `event_history.transaction` exclusively. For MVP, **there is no pacs enrichment at the Gold layer**. Pacs-specific fields not present in `event_history.transaction` (e.g. exchange rate, interbank settlement amount) are not part of the MVP `gold/transaction` schema; see requirement 6 (post-MVP) for the longer-term approach. TMS core fields must never be overridden by pacs data.

### 3. Orchestrator skip guard: remove and replace with registry entries

```python
# Before:
if table in ("transaction", "transactions"):
    return "Skipped: transactions are derived from PACS gold"

# After:
"transaction":  TransactionsETL,   # primary key
"transactions": TransactionsETL,   # plural alias
```

### 4. `CombinedPacsETL`: delete entirely

Route pacs tables directly:

```python
"pacs008": Pacs008ETL,
"pacs002": Pacs002ETL,
```

Also delete the `.pipeline_state/pacs008_gold_done` and `.pipeline_state/pacs002_gold_done` marker files.

### 5. `_join_mode` must be removed, not adapted

Rewrite `TransactionsETL.py` to read exclusively from `{bucket}/transaction/`. Remove `_join_mode()` entirely.

### 6. (Post-MVP) Gold layer enrichment — pacs-specific fields joined from `gold/pacs008`

> **Deferred — not in MVP scope.** For MVP, `gold/transaction` is sourced exclusively from `event_history.transaction` with no pacs enrichment. This requirement defines the short-term workaround and the longer-term architecture.

**Short-term workaround (tracked in #111):** Consumers requiring exchange rate (`xchg_rate`) or interbank settlement amount (`intr_bk_sttlm_amt`) must add a `LEFT JOIN gold/pacs008 ON (end_to_end_id, tenant_id)` at the view/query layer. The composite key — not `end_to_end_id` alone — avoids cross-tenant collision risk. These fields are pacs.008-only and will be `null` for rows where no matching pacs.008 record exists. Known affected consumers: `transaction_detail_view.py`, `transaction_history_view.py`, CMS Transaction Detail, CMS Alert transactional data — to be confirmed during implementation.

**Longer-term (post-MVP):** `TransactionsETL` should be enhanced to enrich `gold/transaction` at the Gold layer by joining `gold/pacs008` on `(end_to_end_id, tenant_id)`. This centralises the enrichment and eliminates per-consumer pacs joins:

| Field added | Source in `gold/pacs008` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `intr_bk_sttlm_amt`, `intr_bk_sttlm_ccy` | Interbank settlement amount and currency | null if no matching pacs.008 row |
| `xchg_rate` | Exchange rate | null if no match |
| `instg_mmb_id`, `instd_mmb_id` | Instructing / instructed agent member IDs | null if no match |
| `charge_count` | Charges | null if no match |

### 7. Party identifiers: entity table join (same underlying data as pacs.008 entity identification)

The TMS stores party identifiers in `event_history.entity` as `entity.id` = `PrvtId.Othr[0].Id + SchmeNm.Prtry` (e.g. `+27730975224MSISDN`). This is derived from the entity identification data in the pacs.008 message. Joining via the entity table is preferred because it works for all rows (pacs.002 as well as pacs.008):

```
source      → account → account_holder → entity.id → debtor_entity_id
destination → account → account_holder → entity.id → creditor_entity_id
```

**Party display names are not part of the TMS data model.** `event_history.entity` stores only `id`, `tenantId`, `creDtTm` — confirmed from `frms-coe-lib`. `Dbtr.Nm`/`Cdtr.Nm` are transient pacs.008 message fields, not persisted to the ODS. `gold/transaction` will not include a display name column.

---

## Required Actions

> **Before starting:** Confirm with Justus whether `event_history.transaction.txSts` is updated after pacs.002 receipt, which affects upsert key strategy.

1. **Rewrite `TransactionsETL`** (MVP): read from `{bucket}/transaction/`. Extract `source`, `destination`, and flat TMS-normalized fields from `event_history.transaction`. Remove `_join_mode()`. Populate `debtor_entity_id` / `creditor_entity_id` via entity table join per Design Requirement 7. No pacs enrichment at this stage.
2. **Short-term consumer pacs join** (tracked in #111): Consumers requiring `xchg_rate` or `intr_bk_sttlm_amt` must add `LEFT JOIN gold/pacs008 ON (end_to_end_id, tenant_id)` at the view/query layer. Known affected: `transaction_detail_view.py`, `transaction_history_view.py`, CMS Transaction Detail, CMS Alert transactional data.
3. **Delete `CombinedPacsETL`** and add `"pacs008": Pacs008ETL`, `"pacs002": Pacs002ETL` directly to `_ETL_REGISTRY`.
4. **Re-enable the NiFi `Transaction` processor**: remove both skip-guard entries; add `"transaction"` and `"transactions"` to `_ETL_REGISTRY`; drop and rebuild the `*transactions` tables as `*transaction`.
5. **Downstream consumer updates** — tracked in #111.
6. **Post-MVP:** Enhance `TransactionsETL` with Gold layer pacs enrichment per Design Requirement 6 — centralises pacs field augmentation and eliminates per-consumer `gold/pacs008` joins.

---

> **⚠️ AI-assisted analysis — please fact-check before acting.**
> This issue description was produced with the assistance of Claude (GitHub Copilot). The analysis is based on static code review of `nifi/tazama.xml`, `lakehouse_automation_pipeline.py`, `TransactionsETL.py`, `CombinedPacs.py`, the view builder files, the PostgreSQL ODS schema, and `tazama-lf/frms-coe-lib` (`saveEntity` confirmed as `INSERT INTO entity (id, tenantId, creDtTm)` — no name column). All findings should be verified against the live codebase and confirmed with the development team before any implementation work begins.

items.title: G8 comissoes FASE 0: a RT automatica nunca teve estado na venda
items.body:
Trilho **G8 — COMISSÕES**. Esta issue entrega a **FASE 0** (investigação, sem código) e trava o
resto até a resposta ser aceita. Fontes: `cabinet-erp-web/docs/legado/` (extração do
`SOFTLUX.exe` de 2026-08-11) e `schema/bdprincipal-*.csv` (catálogo + contagem de linhas medida).

---

## FASE 0 — a contradição `Par_RTautomatico = True` × `Ven_RtAutomatico` vazio

O achado de 11/08 deixou duas hipóteses: *(a)* a coluna da venda não é alimentada pelo parâmetro,
ou *(b)* a RT automática é aplicada sem registrar na venda. **É a (b), e mais forte do que estava
escrito: as colunas de RT da `Venda` são somente-leitura para o programa inteiro.**

### 1. Nada no código escreve `Ven_RtAutomatico` (nem `Ven_RtCalcular`)

`exe/sql-do-codigo.sql` guarda **todo** o SQL literal do executável — 2.137 SELECT · 857 UPDATE ·
666 INSERT · 129 DELETE. As duas colunas aparecem **zero vezes** ali. Aparecem em exatamente um
lugar do produto:

```
exe/formularios/FrmCons_Orcamento.txt:221  object QryorcamentoVen_RtAutomatico: TBooleanField
exe/formularios/FrmCons_Orcamento.txt:222    FieldName = Ven_RtAutomatico
exe/formularios/FrmCons_Orcamento.txt:223  object QryorcamentoVen_RtCalcular: TBooleanField
```

`TBooleanField` persistente de um `select *` — **sem `TcxGridDBColumn` ligada e sem editor**.
Nenhuma tela mostra, nenhuma tela grava. São as colunas 40 e 41 da `Venda`
(`schema/bdprincipal-colunas.csv:5988`), `bit` anulável, sem default: nasceram vazias e ficaram.

Confiança **alta** — é ausência medida sobre o corpus completo de SQL do exe, não sobre amostra.

### 2. O parâmetro liga o CÁLCULO, não um carimbo na venda

O rótulo do checkbox resolve o mal-entendido do nome da coluna:

```
FrmParamentro.txt:3119  object RTAutomatico: TDBCheckBox
FrmParamentro.txt:3124    Caption = Calcular Automaticamente a Part.
FrmParamentro.txt:3125    DataField = Par_RTautomatico
```

"Part." = **Participação** — o mesmo nome das telas `FrmRT` (*Participação*) e
`FrmOpc_reserva_tecnica` (*Participações*). O parâmetro liga o cálculo automático do VALOR da
participação a partir dos percentuais. Ele nunca prometeu marcar a venda.

### 3. …e o bloco desse parâmetro está pela metade, medido

| item | estado medido |
|---|---|
| `Par_RTautomatico` | `True` |
| `Par_RTAutomaticoProj` · `Par_RTAutomaticoAvu` · `Par_RTAutomaticoTipo` · `Par_RTPrimeiraPorc` | **vazios em `Paramentros`, e sem NENHUM controle no `FrmParamentro`** (grep no DFM: zero) |
| rádio do modo de pagamento da RT (`Values.Strings = [P, L, C]`) | **`Visible = False`** (`FrmParamentro.txt:3130-3137`) |
| `ParametrosRTCategoriaVenda` (categoria de venda — grade "Inclusão") | **1** linha |
| `ParametrosRTIndicacao` (grade "Profissional (Exclusão)") | **1** linha |
| `ParametrosRTDiaPag` (dias de pagamento) | **1** linha |
| `ParametrosRTGrupoProdutos` (% padrão por grupo) | **7** linhas |
| `ParametrosRTGrupoProdutosDesconto` | **0** linhas |

Os três itens do rádio escondido são o desenho que ficou no papel: *vincular pagamento da RT às
condições de recebimento da venda* · *escolher os dias de vencimento, não será controlado* ·
*pagamento em dois pagamentos, o primeiro de X%* — este último é o destino do
`Par_RTPrimeiraPorc` vazio.

**Flag do `Paramentros` não é prova de uso, nos dois sentidos:** `Par_RTFornecedor = False`
enquanto `FornecedorRTGrupProd` tem **7.504 linhas** e `FrmRT` roda uma query inteira em cima dela
(`QryRTFornecedor`, RT bancada pelo FORNECEDOR por grupo). Ligado sem dado de um lado, desligado
com dado do outro. Quem for portar mede a tabela, não o parâmetro.

### 4. Onde a participação realmente vive — e o que mede o "automático"

| documento | linhas |
|---|--:|
| `Venda` | 34.136 |
| `VendaIndicacao` (profissional externo por documento) | 34.666 |
| `VendaIndicacaoGrupProd` (% por grupo dentro da indicação) | **232.415** |
| `Reserva_tecnica` (o LANÇAMENTO que vira dinheiro) | **1.212** |
| `Reserva_tecnica_GrupoProd` | 12.108 |
| `CreditoIndicacao` | **1** |

≈1 profissional por documento (34.666 / 34.136), mas só **1.212 lançamentos de RT** contra 11.103
pedidos — **10,9%**. A participação é REGISTRADA em quase todo documento; o passo que gera título
a pagar aconteceu em um décimo deles. Mesmo com o checkbox ligado, o que vira dinheiro foi decisão
humana, uma a uma. É esse comportamento que o Cabinet reproduz.

**`CreditoIndicacao` com 1 linha contra 1.212 RTs** — o caminho "crédito do profissional" tem
tela (`FrmCreditoIndicacao`, e `FrmRT` lê `qryCreditoInd`) e não tem operação. Não portar agora.

### 5. Conclusão da FASE 0 (a resposta que destrava a modelagem)

> A RT automática do Softlux **nunca teve estado na venda**. `Ven_RtAutomatico` e `Ven_RtCalcular`
> são colunas órfãs: declaradas, lidas por um `select *` de tela de consulta, escritas por
> ninguém. O parâmetro `Par_RTautomatico` liga o **cálculo** da participação; a configuração que
> esse cálculo exigia (tipo, projeto/avulsa, % da primeira parcela, modo de pagamento) está vazia
> e sem UI, com o rádio correspondente `Visible = False`. O estado real da participação mora em
> `VendaIndicacao`/`VendaIndicacaoGrupProd` (congelado por documento) e o pagamento, em
> `Reserva_tecnica` → `contas_apagar`.
>
> **Consequência para o Cabinet: não existe flag de "RT automática" para portar.** Portar o
> `Ven_RtAutomatico` seria copiar uma coluna que nunca teve valor — e, pela regra da casa, campo
> que a listagem não devolve nunca vira corpo de PUT; este nem valor teve. O automático é
> propriedade do **cálculo** (servidor recalcula sobre venda fechada), não do documento.

---

## O que a FASE 0 achou de quebra, e muda a FASE A

### 5.1 O "operador" não é sinal aritmético — é comparação contra o DESCONTO da venda

As quatro camadas de percentual por grupo carregam o **mesmo trio**: percentual · desconto ·
operador.

| camada | tabela | linhas |
|---|---|--:|
| padrão da empresa | `ParametrosRTGrupoProdutos(GrupoProduto_Codigo, ParRTGrupProd_porcentagem, ParRTGrupProd_Operador, ParRTGrupProd_Desconto)` | 7 |
| perfil do profissional | `IndicacaoGrupProd(ind_codigo, GrupoProduto_Codigo, IndGruProd_Porc, IndGruProd_DescPorc, IndGruProd_Operador)` | 7.569 |
| congelado no documento | `VendaIndicacaoGrupProd(…, VenIndGrup_Porc, VenIndGrup_DescPorc, VenIndGrup_Operador)` | 232.415 |
| congelado no lançamento | `Reserva_tecnica_GrupoProd(Ret_codigo, GrupoProduto_Codigo, RetGProd_PorcRT, RetGProd_DescPorc, RetGProd_Operador)` | 12.108 |

Três evidências de que o operador compara desconto:

1. **A PK das três inclui o próprio percentual** — `(Ret_codigo, GrupoProduto_Codigo,
   RetGProd_PorcRT)`, `(ind_codigo, GrupoProduto_Codigo, IndGruProd_Porc)`. Grupo com uma linha só
   não precisaria disso: são **várias faixas por grupo**, uma por condição.
2. **A query que casa as duas pontas puxa o desconto da venda junto** —
   `sql-por-tela.sql:169`: `select VendaIndicacaoGrupProd.*, Venda.Ven_DescontoPorc … where
   venind_ndocpre = :codigopre and ind_codigo = :ind_codigo`. O `%` do grupo só significa alguma
   coisa ao lado do `Ven_DescontoPorc`.
3. **O irmão explícito** — `ComissaoPremiacaoCond.ComPreCond_SimbDesc char(2)` ao lado de
   `ComPreCond_Desconto`: "símbolo" de 2 caracteres = `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `=`.

Leitura: **quanto mais desconto o vendedor dá, menor a participação do profissional.** É a regra
que o caso de teste do DoD tem de reproduzir, e é o motivo de `VendaIndicacaoGrupProd` ter 232 mil
linhas — 6,7 linhas por (documento × profissional): não é "12 grupos", é faixa por grupo.

Confiança **média** nesta leitura: vem da forma (PK, join, coluna irmã), não do dado. **O caso
real conferido pelo user resolve** — é exatamente o item do DoD.

### 5.2 Pagamento já tem chave de idempotência pronta

```
sql-do-codigo.sql:2747  select * from contas_apagar where Ctp_cod_documento = :CODIGO and tpd_codigo = 1004
sql-por-tela.sql:10193  … (contas_apagar.Tpd_codigo = 1004) and Reserva_tecnica.Ret_codigo = :codigo
sql-do-codigo.sql:2885  SELECT … FROM Tipo_documento WHERE (NOT (Tpd_codigo IN (1001,…,1007)))
```

O título de RT é `contas_apagar` com **`Tpd_codigo = 1004`** e `Ctp_cod_documento = Ret_codigo`;
parcelas em `contas_apagar_det`. 1001–1007 são tipos de documento **reservados do sistema** — a
lista escolhível pelo usuário os exclui. **O par (tipo de documento reservado, id do lançamento) é
a chave natural do refechamento idempotente** — não inventar uma.

### 5.3 Estados e vocabulário medidos

- `Reserva_tecnica`: `Ret_tipo` ∈ {`PROJETO`, avulsa} (`update … ParSV_serie='1' where Ret_tipo
  ='PROJETO'` / `'2' where <> 'PROJETO'`) · `Ret_situacao = 'ATIVO'` · valores quebrados em
  `Ret_tec_luminaria` / `_materiais` / `_servico` / `_total` — **a participação é apurada por
  natureza de item, não num total só** · `Ret_TpFinanceiro` char(1).
- `VendaIndicacao` / `VendaAtendente` têm o MESMO formato: `(TpDoc, NDocPre, <pessoa>, Emp_Codigo)`
  + `Porcentagem` + `Principal` + `DtVigencia`. `VendaAtendente` = **37.707 linhas para 34.136
  vendas** — o N atendentes por venda que a FASE A pede JÁ é o caso comum do legado, não exceção.
- `TpDoc` discrimina o documento: `ORC` (orçamento) · `PRO` (pedido/projeto) · `AUT` (autorizo de
  inclusão) · `DEM` · `PST`. A participação atravessa o ciclo inteiro, e o `FrmTransfInd`
  (`TransfIndicacao`/`TransfIndicacaoDet`) transfere venda de um profissional para outro depois
  do fato — existe, e a FASE A não previu.
- Devolução reduz a base: `FrmRT.Qrydevolucao` desconta `DevolucaoProduto` por grupo antes de
  apurar. Fechamento que ignora devolução paga a mais.
- Fechamento de colaborador é outro trilho, já modelado: `FechamentoComissao(MesAno, dataInicial,
  dataFinal, Situacao, ContaUnica)` 7 linhas + `FechamentoComissaoConta` 32 · `ComissaoPremiacao`
  (2) com `CategoriaRemuneracao`, meta, rateio e vigência · `ComissaoPremiacaoGrup` (16, % por
  grupo). **Período fechado tem `Situacao` e uma conta única** — o refechamento do Cabinet responde
  Problem Details olhando para isso.
- `Venda.Ven_DescGanhoVenda` / `Ven_AcrescGanhoVenda` (colunas 38/39) são escritas de verdade
  (`update venda set Ven_DescGanhoVenda = Ven_DescontoPorc where year(Ven_DataEmissao) = 2012`) —
  é o desconto que **reduz o ganho do colaborador**, o análogo interno da regra de 5.1.

---

## Estado do trilho depois da FASE 0

**FASE A (web/contrato) — bloqueia tudo que é rota.** O `contracts/openapi-v1.json` de hoje tem
**60 caminhos e nenhum** de participação, comissão, apuração ou fechamento; `salespersonId`
aparece 5 vezes, singular. Rota que não está no contrato não existe — a FASE B entra **por baixo**
(migração + módulo de cálculo + isolamento), como a #101 fez com serviços.

O que a FASE A precisa pedir no `cabinet-erp-web`, já corrigido pelo que a FASE 0 mediu:

1. **Atendentes N por venda** — `{personId, percent, principal, validFrom}`; manter
   `salespersonId` por compat e deprecar depois. (O legado já era N: 37.707 / 34.136.)
2. **Participação do profissional externo** — percentual geral **+ faixas por grupo de produto**,
   cada faixa `{productGroupId, percent, discountPercent, operator}` com `operator` no vocabulário
   fechado `>=,<=,>,<,=`. **Não é um percentual por grupo — é uma lista de faixas por grupo.**
3. **% de comissão no cadastro** — grupo comissão/premiação do colaborador e perfil de
   participação do profissional (vol. 01 §3/§4), com a mesma forma de faixa.
4. **Reserva Técnica** — perfil no profissional + lançamento por venda, com valor por natureza
   (produto/serviço), situação e tipo (projeto/avulsa).
5. **Apuração** — consulta de ganhos por período + fechamento gerando CP via G6.
6. **NÃO pedir:** flag `rtAutomatic` no documento (§5 — nunca teve valor) e crédito do
   profissional (`CreditoIndicacao`, 1 linha).

**FASE B (api).** Migrações **`0044` e `0045` RESERVADAS aqui** — `0036`–`0043` já estão tomadas
(`0036` na `permissoes-especiais-s5`; `0037`/`0038` #110; `0037` também #111; `0039`/`0040` #113;
`0040`/`0041` #112; `0042`/`0043` #115). Zona disjunta não protege `NNNN`.

Regras que a modelagem já herda, sem discussão: dinheiro em centavos `bigint` e percentual **nunca
em float** · toda tabela nova com `tenant_id` nasce com o pacote completo de RLS + linha em
`src/core/tenancy/tabelas.ts` + caso próprio na bateria · cabeçalho de procedência de 3 linhas
com a fonte no `NOTICE` · cálculo **no servidor** sobre venda fechada, nunca aceito do cliente
(percentual vindo do corpo é afirmação do cliente sobre o próprio ganho) · fechamento idempotente
pela chave de 5.2, refechar responde Problem Details em vez de duplicar título · `audit_log` sai
da borda, com linha própria em `ENTIDADES` para caminho com trecho fixo depois do parâmetro.

**FASE C (web/telas)** — aba Participação na venda · consulta de ganhos · tela de fechamento.

## DoD

- [ ] Padrão da casa (fechamento de 9 passos do `CLAUDE.md`).
- [ ] **Caso de teste com os percentuais por grupo reproduzindo um caso real conferido pelo user** —
      é o que fecha a confiança média de §5.1 sobre o operador.
- [ ] Fechamento → títulos no CP conferidos.

## Bloqueios

1. **FASE A é serial e mora no `cabinet-erp-web`.** PR de contrato aberta lá deixa toda PR do api
   vermelha até mergear.
2. **O caso real de §5.1 precisa do user.** Sem o dado de uma venda de verdade, o operador fica
   inferido da forma. É o único ponto da FASE 0 que a extração não fecha sozinha.

items.title: Report data exports

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

Several stories in this epic assume an export exists — #384 exports indicator aggregates, #385 exports receivables, #591 bundles an assessment pack, #593 attaches artefacts to scheduled deliveries — but no export capability has been built. Each of those would otherwise implement its own CSV writer, its own file naming, its own delivery mechanism and its own audit record, which guarantees inconsistency in exactly the area where inconsistency is most expensive.

Export is the point at which data leaves the platform's control. Once a file is downloaded, RLS, OpenFGA, the audit trail and the platform's retention schedule have all ended; the hospital, as Data Fiduciary under DPDP 2023, remains accountable for personal data it can no longer see, restrict or erase. The platform's own audit rules list data exports alongside prescriptions, refunds and break-glass access as events requiring tamper-evident records, and the tenant isolation rules call out data-export controls explicitly. An export capability built casually undermines every access control built carefully elsewhere.

There is an operational dimension too. Hospital finance and MIS staff genuinely need data in Excel — for board packs, for auditor submissions, for the accountant's own reconciliation — and refusing exports simply pushes them to screenshots, copy-paste and unmanaged database access, which is strictly worse. And exports are frequently large: a year of invoice lines or encounter facts is not a synchronous HTTP response, so a naive implementation will time out on the first real request and produce a truncated file that the recipient will not notice is truncated.

Affected roles: finance controller, MIS clerk, quality manager, hospital administrator, TPA co-ordinator, laboratory and pharmacy managers, the DPO and the platform security team.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** finance controller
**I want** to export any report I am entitled to as a complete, correctly formatted file delivered by a time-limited link
**So that** I can work with the data outside the platform, while the hospital retains a full record of what was exported, by whom and containing what.

### Scope

**In scope**

* A shared export service consumed by every report in this epic, so no report implements its own file writing or delivery.
* Formats: CSV (RFC 4180), XLSX with typed columns and frozen headers, PDF for presentation reports and compliance packs, and JSON for machine consumption.
* Asynchronous job model with progress, cancellation and streaming generation so file size is bounded by storage, not by request timeout.
* Delivery exclusively by signed, time-limited object-storage URLs scoped to the requesting user; never a direct download from an application response, never a permanent URL.
* Export manifest per job recording the report, parameters, resolved period, row count, column list, sensitivity classification, requester and generation time, embedded in the file where the format permits and always stored server-side.
* Entitlement enforcement at generation time using the same field-level relations as #592, with a distinct exporter relation separate from viewing.
* Per-tenant and per-user export quotas, row caps by sensitivity class, and an approval step for exports above a configured row threshold or containing identifying fields.
* Tamper-evident audit record per export, and a tenant-visible export register the DPO can review.
* Retention: generated artefacts expire and are deleted from object storage after a configurable period, default 7 days.

**Out of scope**

* Report content, query logic and the semantic layer — owned by #583–#592.
* Scheduling and channel delivery of exports — owned by #593, which calls this service.
* Bulk data extraction for migration, warehousing or ETL to a customer's own systems — that is a platform data-portability concern, not report export.
* DPDP data-principal access requests producing a patient's own record copy — that is the rights workflow in the Security and Compliance epic, which has different content and identity-verification requirements.
* Direct database or warehouse credentials issued to tenants.

---

## Recommended Solution

Build `export-service` as a Go module invoked over an internal interface by report handlers, never called directly by the browser with a report payload. The caller passes a report reference and parameters; the service re-executes the query itself. This matters: if the client supplied the rows, the export would inherit whatever the client had rather than what the requester is entitled to, and the manifest could not be trusted.

**Job model and data:**

```sql
CREATE TABLE export_job (
  job_id         uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id      uuid NOT NULL,
  facility_id    uuid,
  requested_by   uuid NOT NULL,
  source_kind    text NOT NULL CHECK (source_kind IN ('fixed_report','custom_definition','pack')),
  source_key     text NOT NULL,
  parameters     jsonb NOT NULL,
  format         text NOT NULL CHECK (format IN ('csv','xlsx','pdf','json')),
  sensitivity    text NOT NULL CHECK (sensitivity IN
                   ('aggregate','financial','clinical','identifying')),
  status         text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN
                   ('queued','awaiting_approval','running','completed','failed',
                    'cancelled','expired','denied')),
  row_count      int,
  byte_size      bigint,
  object_key     text,
  checksum_sha256 text,
  approved_by    uuid,
  requested_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  completed_at   timestamptz,
  expires_at     timestamptz,
  idempotency_key text,
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, requested_by, idempotency_key),
  CONSTRAINT approval_required CHECK (
    sensitivity <> 'identifying' OR status IN ('queued','awaiting_approval','denied','cancelled')
      OR approved_by IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE TABLE export_manifest_column (
  job_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES export_job ON DELETE CASCADE,
  ordinal int NOT NULL, field_key text NOT NULL,
  display_name text NOT NULL, sensitivity text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (job_id, ordinal)
);
```

The `approval_required` check enforces in the database what policy states: an export containing identifying fields cannot reach `completed` without a recorded approver. Putting this in a constraint rather than only in service code means no future code path can bypass it.

**Generation** runs as a Temporal workflow: authorise → estimate rows → gate on quota, cap and approval → stream-generate → checksum → store → sign → notify. Generation streams from a server-side cursor over the analytics cluster directly into an object-storage multipart upload, so peak memory is a buffer rather than a result set, and a 2-million-row CSV is bounded by time and storage rather than by heap. XLSX uses a streaming writer for the same reason; PDF is generated section-wise with checkpointing, matching the pack approach in #591. The SHA-256 checksum is recorded and shown to the requester so a truncated or corrupted download is detectable — a silently truncated financial export is the failure mode that does real damage, because nobody notices a file that opens successfully.

**Delivery.** The only egress is a signed object-storage URL with a short expiry, default 15 minutes, bound to the requesting user and single-use where the storage provider supports it. Artefacts are stored under tenant-dedicated storage paths, and object lifecycle rules delete them at `expires_at` regardless of application state, so retention does not depend on a cleanup job running.

**API surface:**

* `POST /api/v1/exports` — body carries source reference, parameters, format; returns job id. `Idempotency-Key` header required.
* `GET /api/v1/exports/{job_id}` — status, progress, row count, checksum.
* `POST /api/v1/exports/{job_id}/download-url` — mints a fresh signed URL; each mint is separately audited.
* `POST /api/v1/exports/{job_id}/cancel`
* `POST /api/v1/exports/{job_id}/approve` — requires the approver relation, records the approver.
* `GET /api/v1/exports/register?from=&to=&user_id=` — the tenant export register for the DPO.

**Events published:** `ExportRequested`, `ExportApproved`, `ExportCompleted`, `ExportDownloaded`, `ExportDenied`, `ExportExpired`. `ExportDownloaded` is emitted on each signed-URL mint, not on job completion, because the auditable act is retrieval, not generation.

**OpenFGA:**

```
type export_job
  relations
    define facility: [facility]
    define requester: [user]
    define exporter_aggregate: quality_manager from facility or hospital_admin from facility
    define exporter_financial: finance_controller from facility
    define exporter_identifying: hospital_admin from facility
    define approver: dpo from tenant or hospital_admin from facility
    define register_viewer: dpo from tenant
```

Export relations are deliberately narrower than the corresponding view relations across this epic — being able to read a receivables report on screen is not the same permission as taking it out of the platform. The approver is a different person from the requester by construction: the service rejects self-approval even where a user holds both relations.

**Sequencing.** Must land alongside or before #593, which attaches exports to scheduled deliveries, and it consumes the field sensitivity classifications defined by #592's semantic layer. Fixed-report exports for #384 and #385 can be wired first while the semantic layer is still in progress.

**Risks.** The largest is an export whose contents no longer match its entitlements because the query re-ran after a permission change mid-job — mitigated by resolving relations once at job start, recording them on the job, and failing the job rather than downgrading if a relation is revoked during generation. Quota exhaustion by one tenant degrading generation for others is contained by a per-tenant worker concurrency limit. Signed URLs being forwarded is mitigated by short expiry, user binding and single-use where supported, and accepted as residual risk otherwise — which is precisely why identifying exports require approval and appear in the DPO's register.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** a finance controller holding `exporter_financial` for her facility requests an XLSX export of the last quarter's receivables ageing report
**When** the export job runs to completion
**Then** the file contains every row the on-screen report would show for the same parameters with typed columns and a frozen header, the manifest records the report, resolved period, row count, column list and requester, the download is delivered by a signed URL expiring in 15 minutes, the recorded SHA-256 matches the downloaded file, and `ExportCompleted` followed by `ExportDownloaded` appear in the tamper-evident audit trail.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a user requests an export containing patient-identifying columns and holds `exporter_identifying` but there is no separate approver
**When** the job is created
**Then** it is held at `awaiting_approval`, no file is generated and no URL is minted, an approval request is raised to the DPO, self-approval by the requester is rejected even though they hold the approver relation, and if approval is refused the job moves to `denied` with the refusal recorded in the export register.

### Edge Cases

* Generation fails at 80% of a 2-million-row CSV — no partial object is exposed, the multipart upload is aborted, the job moves to `failed` with the stage recorded, and the requester is told to retry rather than being handed a truncated file.
* The same request is submitted twice with the same `Idempotency-Key` — the second returns the existing job rather than generating a duplicate file and a second audit entry.
* A requester's exporter relation is revoked while the job is running — the job fails closed with `denied`, and no URL is minted for an already-generated object.
* A signed URL is requested after `expires_at` — minting is refused, the object is already deleted by the storage lifecycle rule, and the requester is directed to raise a fresh job rather than the artefact being silently regenerated.
* An export resolves to zero rows — a file is still produced containing headers and the manifest, so the recipient can distinguish an empty result from a failed generation.
* A field containing a leading `=`, `+` or `-` is written to CSV — it is neutralised so the file cannot execute a formula on open in a spreadsheet, a genuine injection path in exported reports.
* A tenant exceeds its monthly export quota — further requests are refused with the quota and reset date named, existing running jobs complete, and other tenants are unaffected.

---
## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team’s agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team’s agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** any entitled user exports any report they can view, in a format fit for the tool they will use it in, delivered by a short-lived link with a verifiable checksum and a complete manifest.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** screenshots, copy-paste and unmanaged database access are displaced by a single governed egress path, and the DPO can answer what left the platform, when, to whom and containing what, from one register.
* **Success metric or validation method:** a 2-million-row CSV generates within 5 minutes with steady-state memory under 256 MB per worker; 100% of completed exports carry a manifest, checksum and audit record, asserted by an invariant test over the job table; zero exports completed with identifying sensitivity and no distinct approver, enforced by the database constraint and verified adversarially; zero cross-tenant object access across the isolation test suite; artefact deletion at `expires_at` verified by an object-storage lifecycle audit.
* **Monitoring period, where applicable:** 8 weeks post-deployment, tracking job outcome distribution, p95 generation time by format and row band, quota refusal rate, approval turnaround for identifying exports, and orphaned-object count in tenant storage paths (target zero).

---
## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

**Guardrail:** Accessibility and User Journey — "The change meets the team's agreed WCAG accessibility level" and "Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly", as applied to the generated artefacts themselves.
**Reason:** the export service's own UI surface is small — a format chooser, a job progress state and a download control — and those are covered in full. The exported CSV, XLSX and PDF files are consumed in third-party applications whose accessibility the platform cannot control, and a WCAG conformance claim cannot meaningfully be made about a spreadsheet.
**Alternative validation:** the in-platform export controls, progress states, approval flow and export register are tested to the agreed WCAG level with keyboard operation and screen-reader labelling; generated PDFs are produced with a document title, logical reading order and tagged headings so they are not gratuitously inaccessible; XLSX carries proper column headers and typed cells rather than a single text column.
**Residual risk:** a recipient using assistive technology may encounter a poorly navigable file in their spreadsheet application. Low impact, as the same data remains available in the accessible on-screen report.
**Approved by:** Design System lead and Head of Data, to be recorded on the pull request.

items.title: [Note] AI Engineer
items.body:
## AI Engineer 能力地圖：Frame × 關鍵字

以下以每個 frame 作為領域；每個關鍵字一列，欄位固定為一句話理解、概念、技術、實作、情境、注意；「一句話理解」以 Full Stack 工程師熟悉的系統開發視角說明。

### Data Engineering

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ETL / ELT | 像後端資料搬運管線：抽取資料、整理格式，再送進分析系統。 | 把來源資料可靠地送到分析層；ETL先轉換、ELT先落地再轉換。 | 批次/增量、CDC、schema evolution、Spark/dbt。 | 以Airflow排程、dbt轉換、資料品質檢查與重跑機制落地。 | 報表、數據同步、資料湖到倉庫。 | 避免全量重跑；處理重複、遲到資料、PII與schema變更。 |
| Data Warehouse | 專門給報表與分析查詢的集中式資料庫。 | 面向分析的集中式資料儲存，重視一致性與查詢效能。 | 星型模型、分區、columnar storage、OLAP。 | 建立raw/staging/mart分層與維度/事實表。 | BI、KPI、跨來源報表。 | 不要把交易庫直接當分析庫；控管成本與資料新鮮度。 |
| Data Lake / Lakehouse | 像大型物件儲存倉庫，但加上可查詢、版本與治理能力。 | 保留大量原始資料並兼顧治理與分析能力。 | Object storage、Parquet、Delta/Iceberg、schema-on-read。 | 以bronze/silver/gold分層，設定catalog、partition與compact。 | 半結構化資料、ML訓練、歷史留存。 | 小檔案與無治理會拖垮查詢；需管理版本、權限與生命週期。 |
| Streaming / Real-time | 把資料當事件即時處理，類似 WebSocket 或 queue consumer。 | 資料事件產生後即時處理，而非等待批次窗口。 | Kafka/PubSub、Flink/Spark Streaming、watermark、幂等。 | 設計topic/schema、consumer group、checkpoint與DLQ。 | 即時告警、推薦、即時儀表板。 | 至少一次不等於不重複；處理順序、背壓、遲到事件與重放。 |
| Data Modeling | 替資料設計可長期維護的 schema、關聯與統計口徑。 | 把業務實體、關係與指標轉成可查詢且可演進的結構。 | 正規化/反正規化、維度建模、SCD、data contract。 | 先定義grain，再建立主鍵、外鍵、指標與欄位字典。 | 跨團隊共用資料、報表與特徵。 | grain不清會造成重複計算；避免只為當下報表硬編模型。 |
| Data Quality & Governance | 替資料加上測試、ownership、權限與可追溯性。 | 確保資料正確、完整、及時、可追溯且有人負責。 | 契約測試、expectations、lineage、catalog、SLA。 | 在pipeline加入schema、null、範圍、freshness與異常告警。 | 重要報表、監管資料、ML輸入。 | 品質規則要可執行；告警過多會被忽略，需訂責任人與處置流程。 |
| Orchestration | 像 CI/CD workflow，負責安排資料任務的順序、重試與排程。 | 管理資料工作流的依賴、重試、排程與可觀測性。 | DAG、Airflow/Dagster、sensor、backfill、retry。 | 任務保持冪等，設定timeout、重試、依賴與失敗通知。 | 多步ETL、每日報表、模型pipeline。 | 不要把業務邏輯塞進排程器；避免隱性依賴與無限重試。 |

### RAG / LLM Application

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture | 把 ingestion、搜尋、LLM 與 API 拆成有清楚邊界的服務。 | 定義RAG元件如何串接、資料流如何走，以及同步/非同步邊界。 | Retriever-generator pipeline、API gateway、cache、queue。 | 拆 ingestion、retrieval、generation、evaluation 與 serving。 | 企業知識問答、客服、文件搜尋。 | 先定義延遲、成本、權限與失敗降級，再選框架。 |
| Chunking | 把長文件切成模型搜尋得到、又看得懂的小段落。 | 把文件切成適合檢索與模型上下文的片段。 | 固定長度、語意切分、recursive splitter、overlap。 | 依標題/段落切分，保留metadata並用檢索指標調整大小。 | 長文件問答、規章與技術文件。 | 切太小失去上下文，切太大降低召回；不要切斷表格與程式碼。 |
| Embedding | 把文字轉成可比較相似度的數字向量。 | 將文字轉成向量，讓語意相近內容在向量空間靠近。 | Transformer embedding、cosine similarity、批次embedding。 | 固定模型與版本，建立向量索引並記錄embedding model。 | 語意搜尋、相似案例、RAG召回。 | 模型換版需重建索引；多語、領域詞與向量維度要驗證。 |
| Vector DB | 替 embedding 建索引，讓系統能快速做語意搜尋。 | 儲存與查詢向量及其metadata的資料庫。 | HNSW/IVF、ANN、top-k、filter、Qdrant/pgvector/Milvus。 | 建立collection、索引、metadata filter與刪除/更新流程。 | 大量文件的語意檢索。 | top-k不是品質保證；注意索引更新、租戶隔離與查詢成本。 |
| Metadata Filtering | 像 SQL WHERE，先用權限、租戶或日期縮小搜尋範圍。 | 先用結構化條件縮小可檢索範圍，再做語意搜尋。 | 欄位filter、ACL filter、tenant_id、時間/版本條件。 | 把權限與來源metadata寫入chunk，檢索時強制套用。 | 依部門、產品、日期、權限搜尋。 | filter不能由模型自由決定；缺metadata會造成越權或漏召回。 |
| Hybrid Search | 同時跑關鍵字搜尋和語意搜尋，再合併結果。 | 結合關鍵字精確匹配與向量語意匹配。 | BM25、dense retrieval、rank fusion、RRF。 | 並行查詢兩路召回後融合、去重並評估權重。 | 專有名詞、編號與自然語言混合查詢。 | 只用向量容易漏掉ID/術語；融合權重需用資料驗證。 |
| Reranker | 像搜尋結果的第二輪排序器，把真正相關的內容往前排。 | 對初步召回結果重新排序，提升前幾筆相關性。 | Cross-encoder、Cohere rerank、top-N reranking。 | 先取較大的candidate pool，再對前N筆重排。 | 召回很多但答案常不在前幾筆。 | 會增加延遲與成本；不要把reranker當作權限層。 |
| Query Rewriting | 把使用者模糊的問題改寫成更容易查到資料的查詢。 | 把模糊、口語或多輪問題改寫成更適合檢索的查詢。 | Query expansion、multi-query、HyDE、conversation rewrite。 | 保留原問題，產生候選查詢並記錄改寫結果。 | 追問、省略主詞、跨語言與複雜問題。 | 改寫可能改變原意；需防止注入與錯誤擴張。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |
| Faithfulness | 檢查答案是否真的有文件證據支持。 | 答案是否能被提供的上下文支持，而非模型自行捏造。 | Citation checking、NLI、LLM-as-judge、groundedness。 | 要求引用來源，逐句比對claim與context並設拒答門檻。 | 法規、客服、內部知識問答。 | 有引用不代表真的支持；避免把judge分數當絕對真值。 |
| Hallucination | 模型講得很像真的，但內容其實沒有依據。 | 模型產生與證據不符或不存在的內容。 | Grounding、temperature control、answer abstention、fact check。 | 無證據時拒答，輸出引用與信心，記錄錯誤案例回歸。 | 資料不完整或問題超出知識庫。 | 降低temperature無法根治；需改善召回與輸出驗證。 |
| Failure Modes | 列出系統會怎麼壞，並預先設計偵測、降級與復原。 | 系統在資料、檢索、模型、工具或網路異常下的失敗型態。 | Failure taxonomy、chaos test、timeout、retry、DLQ。 | 建立錯誤分類、fallback、告警與可重現測試案例。 | 上線前演練與事故分析。 | 只測happy path不夠；重試可能放大流量與費用。 |

### Agent

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Workflow | 像後端狀態機，把 Agent 任務拆成可控制的步驟。 | 把Agent任務拆成可追蹤、可重試、可控的步驟。 | State machine、DAG、LangGraph、workflow engine。 | 明確定義節點輸入輸出、轉移條件與終止條件。 | 多步研究、客服處理、資料操作。 | 避免讓模型自行決定所有流程；限制迴圈與最大步數。 |
| Tool Calling | 讓模型用結構化參數呼叫 API，而不是只產生文字。 | 讓模型以結構化參數呼叫外部工具完成工作。 | Function calling、JSON schema、tool registry。 | 驗證參數、套用權限、執行工具並把結果回傳模型。 | 查詢API、寄信、寫入資料庫。 | 工具呼叫等同權限操作；需白名單、審計與人工核准。 |
| State | 保存 Agent 做到哪裡、拿到什麼結果，以及下一步要做什麼。 | 保存Agent在多步任務中的上下文、結果與目前階段。 | State schema、checkpoint、短期/長期記憶。 | 用明確schema儲存狀態，支援重試、恢復與版本遷移。 | 長流程、多輪對話、非同步任務。 | 不要把所有對話無限塞進prompt；避免狀態污染與競態。 |
| Planning | 讓 Agent 先拆任務再執行，但每一步仍要驗證。 | 先決定子任務與執行順序，再逐步完成目標。 | ReAct、plan-and-execute、task decomposition。 | 限制計畫深度，逐步驗證工具結果並允許重新規劃。 | 研究、複合查詢、跨系統流程。 | 計畫不是事實；每一步都需驗證，並防止無限重新規劃。 |
| Guardrails | 像 middleware 與 policy layer，限制模型與工具能做什麼。 | 在輸入、工具、輸出各階段限制Agent可做的事。 | Policy engine、schema validation、content filter、allowlist。 | 建立前置/後置檢查，違規時拒絕、修正或轉人工。 | 高風險自動化、金融、客服。 | 只做輸出過濾不夠；工具層和資料層也要防護。 |
| Human-in-the-loop | 高風險動作先停住，交給人核准後才繼續。 | 在高風險或不確定步驟由人審核、接管或核准。 | Approval gate、confidence threshold、escalation。 | 設計待審佇列、審核理由、逾時與回滾流程。 | 付款、刪除、對外發信、敏感回答。 | 人工介入點要可量化；避免所有案件都卡在人工作業。 |
| Structured Output | 要求模型回傳符合 JSON Schema 的資料，方便程式接續處理。 | 要求模型輸出可被程式可靠解析的固定結構。 | JSON schema、Pydantic、constrained decoding。 | 解析後做schema與業務規則驗證，失敗則修復或重試。 | API回應、分類、工作流節點。 | 格式正確不代表內容正確；限制欄位長度與注入內容。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |

### LLM Evaluation

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |
| LLM Judge | 用另一個模型依評分規則批改 AI 回答。 | 用另一個模型依評分規準評估回答品質。 | Rubric、pairwise judge、calibration、human agreement。 | 固定prompt與模型版本，抽樣人工複核並監控偏差。 | 大量離線回歸、主觀品質評估。 | judge有偏見與位置效應；不要只依賴單一judge。 |
| Golden Dataset | AI 版本的固定測試案例與標準答案。 | 代表真實使用情境、具標準答案或評分規準的固定案例集。 | Versioned dataset、stratified sampling、edge cases。 | 標記來源、難度、語言與失敗類型，納入CI與變更審查。 | 模型/提示詞版本比較。 | 資料過時會誤導；要避免資料洩漏與只收集簡單案例。 |
| Observability | 把 metrics、logs、traces 串起來，看懂線上系統發生什麼。 | 讓團隊知道系統發生什麼、品質如何、成本多少。 | Metrics、logs、traces、dashboards、alerts。 | 關聯request id、tenant、model、prompt版本與結果指標。 | 線上除錯、SLA與容量規劃。 | 避免記錄原始敏感prompt；指標需能對應行動。 |
| Tracing | 像 distributed tracing，追蹤一次 AI 請求經過的所有步驟。 | 追蹤一次請求跨模型、檢索、工具與服務的完整路徑。 | OpenTelemetry、span、trace ID、Langfuse/Phoenix。 | 每個節點建立span，記錄輸入輸出摘要、耗時、token與錯誤。 | 定位慢點、錯誤與幻覺來源。 | trace資料可能含機密；設採樣、遮罩、保留期限。 |
| Token Cost | 把每次模型呼叫換算成可追蹤、可分攤的成本。 | 量化輸入輸出token帶來的模型使用成本。 | Token counter、pricing table、budget、cost attribution。 | 每次請求記錄token與模型，按租戶/功能聚合並設預算告警。 | 成本最佳化、租戶計費、模型選擇。 | 價格會變；不要只看平均值，要看p95與異常尖峰。 |
| Latency | 拆解使用者等候時間，找出慢在 queue、搜尋、模型或工具。 | 從請求到回應的時間，需拆分各階段觀察。 | p50/p95/p99、TTFT、streaming、timeout。 | 分別量測queue、retrieval、LLM、tool與post-process。 | 互動式聊天、SLA設計。 | 平均值會掩蓋尾延遲；重試與串行工具會放大等待。 |
| Fallback | 主要模型失敗時，自動切到備援模型或簡化流程。 | 主要模型或服務失效時切換到可接受的替代路徑。 | Circuit breaker、model routing、retry、degraded mode。 | 定義觸發條件、替代模型、超時與回復策略並記錄原因。 | 供應商故障、流量尖峰、模型超時。 | fallback品質與成本要測試；避免故障時形成重試風暴。 |
| Prompt Versioning | 把 prompt 當程式碼版本管理、測試與回滾。 | 讓prompt變更可追蹤、可回滾、可比較。 | Git、template registry、semantic version、feature flag。 | 保存版本、變更原因、評測結果與生產流量分配。 | 持續改善提示詞、A/B測試。 | prompt改一字也可能改變行為；不可只靠人工感覺上線。 |
| Model Versioning | 固定並追蹤實際使用的模型版本、參數與評測結果。 | 讓模型、權重、參數與供應商版本可重現。 | Model registry、pinned version、canary、rollback。 | 記錄模型ID、參數、system prompt、資料與評測結果。 | 模型升級、事故回溯、品質比較。 | 供應商別名可能指向不同版本；需定期重跑基準。 |

### Production AI / Observability

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LLM Evaluation | 替 AI 上線流程建立品質測試與持續監控。 | 用固定案例與線上訊號衡量LLM應用品質。 | Offline eval、online eval、human eval、LLM judge。 | 在CI做回歸，線上抽樣並把失敗案例回寫資料集。 | 上線前驗證與持續監控。 | 離線高分不代表真實使用高分；要分群看結果。 |
| LLM as a Judge | 讓模型按 rubric 大量評分，再由人工抽查校準。 | 以模型依rubric評分回答，降低大規模人工評估成本。 | Pointwise/pairwise、rubric、calibration、human audit。 | 固定評分規準，抽樣人工校準並追蹤judge drift。 | 大量問答品質排序。 | 模型偏好流暢而非正確；需提供證據與反偏差測試。 |
| Evaluation Dataset / Golden Dataset | 保存可重複執行的 AI 測試案例、證據與通過標準。 | 可重複的標準案例與預期結果集合。 | Dataset versioning、stratified split、red-team cases。 | 標記問題類型、答案、證據與通過門檻。 | 版本回歸、模型選型。 | 涵蓋長尾與對抗案例，避免只測demo資料。 |
| LLM Observability | 在 production 追蹤 AI 的品質、成本、延遲與安全事件。 | 觀察LLM請求品質、成本、延遲與安全事件。 | Trace、token metrics、quality sampling、alerting。 | 串接prompt/model/tenant與feedback，建立可鑽取面板。 | 生產事故、成本異常、品質下降。 | 敏感資料遮罩與權限隔離不可省略。 |
| LLM Tracing | 把 prompt、retrieval、tool call 與模型回應串成一條 trace。 | 把一次LLM請求的prompt、retrieval、tool與模型步驟串起來。 | Trace/span、OpenTelemetry、correlation ID。 | 每個步驟記錄版本、耗時、token、錯誤與來源。 | 除錯RAG與Agent鏈路。 | 控制trace payload與保留期限，避免把機密寫入日誌。 |
| Token Cost | 把每次模型呼叫換算成可追蹤、可分攤的成本。 | 量化輸入輸出token帶來的模型使用成本。 | Token counter、pricing table、budget、cost attribution。 | 每次請求記錄token與模型，按租戶/功能聚合並設預算告警。 | 成本最佳化、租戶計費、模型選擇。 | 價格會變；不要只看平均值，要看p95與異常尖峰。 |
| Latency | 拆解使用者等候時間，找出慢在 queue、搜尋、模型或工具。 | 從請求到回應的時間，需拆分各階段觀察。 | p50/p95/p99、TTFT、streaming、timeout。 | 分別量測queue、retrieval、LLM、tool與post-process。 | 互動式聊天、SLA設計。 | 平均值會掩蓋尾延遲；重試與串行工具會放大等待。 |
| Model Fallback | 模型故障或太慢時，依規則切換可接受的替代方案。 | 模型不可用或不符成本/延遲要求時切換替代模型。 | Router、circuit breaker、timeout、health check。 | 按錯誤、延遲、token預算與品質門檻路由。 | 供應商中斷與高峰流量。 | 替代模型要有已驗證的品質底線。 |
| Prompt Versioning | 把 prompt 當程式碼版本管理、測試與回滾。 | 讓prompt變更可追蹤、可回滾、可比較。 | Git、template registry、semantic version、feature flag。 | 保存版本、變更原因、評測結果與生產流量分配。 | 持續改善提示詞、A/B測試。 | prompt改一字也可能改變行為；不可只靠人工感覺上線。 |
| Model Versioning | 固定並追蹤實際使用的模型版本、參數與評測結果。 | 讓模型、權重、參數與供應商版本可重現。 | Model registry、pinned version、canary、rollback。 | 記錄模型ID、參數、system prompt、資料與評測結果。 | 模型升級、事故回溯、品質比較。 | 供應商別名可能指向不同版本；需定期重跑基準。 |

### Multi-tenant

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-tenant Architecture | 同一套後端服務多家公司，但每家的資料與資源必須隔離。 | 同一平台服務多個租戶，同時共享效率與隔離安全。 | Shared service、tenant context、quota、policy。 | 每個request注入tenant context，所有資料與快取操作強制帶租戶。 | SaaS型AI平台。 | 租戶邊界必須端到端驗證，不能只靠前端參數。 |
| Tenant Isolation | 確保任何查詢、快取、檔案與向量都不會跨租戶。 | 防止一個租戶讀寫另一個租戶的資料與資源。 | Logical/physical isolation、ACL、RLS、network policy。 | 在資料庫、快取、向量庫、物件儲存與日誌都套隔離。 | 共享基礎設施的SaaS。 | 要測越權與錯誤租戶context；背景任務也要帶tenant。 |
| Tenant ID | 像 request context 的主鍵，必須一路帶過 API、DB、queue 與 log。 | 識別請求所屬租戶並貫穿整個資料流。 | JWT claims、request context、composite key。 | 由可信身份來源取得，寫入資料表、trace、queue與cache key。 | 多租戶API與非同步工作。 | 不可信任使用者自行傳入的tenant_id；防止IDOR。 |
| Shared Database / Shared Schema | 所有租戶共用表，用 tenant_id 與 RLS 做隔離。 | 所有租戶共用資料庫與schema，以成本換取隔離複雜度。 | tenant_id、RLS、composite index、partition。 | 所有表加tenant_id，Repository層強制篩選並做隔離測試。 | 大量小租戶、成本敏感SaaS。 | 漏一個where就可能資料外洩；索引與熱租戶需特別處理。 |
| Database per Tenant | 每個租戶一個資料庫，隔離更強但維運成本更高。 | 每個租戶使用獨立資料庫，隔離與客製化較強。 | Database provisioning、migration orchestration、connection pool。 | 自動建立/升級/備份資料庫並管理租戶路由。 | 少量大型或合規租戶。 | 運維與連線成本高；migration與跨租戶分析更複雜。 |
| Row-Level Security | 讓資料庫本身強制每列資料能被哪個租戶看到。 | 由資料庫在每一列層級強制租戶存取政策。 | PostgreSQL RLS、session context、policy。 | 交易開始設定tenant context，並測試直接SQL與服務帳號路徑。 | 共享schema的強制隔離。 | 繞過RLS的管理連線很危險；政策需納入migration與測試。 |
| Tenant-aware API | API 從驗證到查詢都必須知道目前是哪個租戶。 | API在授權、資料查詢與回應中都理解租戶邊界。 | JWT、middleware、OPA、quota。 | middleware解析tenant，服務層拒絕不一致context並套用配額。 | 多租戶REST/GraphQL服務。 | 不要只在controller過濾；內部服務與webhook也要驗證。 |
| Multi-tenant Scaling | 避免單一大租戶吃光資源，並能依租戶分片、限流與擴容。 | 在租戶數、流量與資料量成長時維持隔離與效能。 | Quota、sharding、partition、autoscaling、noisy-neighbor control。 | 依租戶分片/限流，監控單租戶資源與升級路徑。 | SaaS成長與大型租戶加入。 | 平均容量會掩蓋熱租戶；需壓測最壞分布。 |
