> 來源：Miro board 的 10 個 frame；內容以 Full Stack 工程師理解 AI 工程能力地圖為目標整理。

## AI 系統從建置到上線：三段流程

閱讀順序只有三段：**先準備資料 → 再處理使用者請求 → 最後用線上結果持續改善**。底部三項是每個階段都必須具備的系統能力。

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph PREP["A. 事前準備：把資料變成 AI 可用的知識"]
    direction LR
    DE["1. Data Engineering<br/>收集、清理、治理資料"]
    DS["2. Data Science<br/>分析資料、定義指標與特徵"]
    ML["3. ML 基礎<br/>選模型、Embedding 與推論方式"]
    KB[("可檢索知識庫<br/>Chunks + Metadata + Vectors")]
    DE --> DS --> ML --> KB
  end

  subgraph REQUEST["B. 線上請求：使用者問問題時，系統實際怎麼跑"]
    direction LR
    USER["使用者 / 前端"] --> API["API 接收問題"]
    API --> RAG["4. RAG / LLM Application<br/>找資料、排序、組 Prompt"]
    RAG --> NEED{"需要執行動作？"}
    NEED -->|否| ANSWER["LLM 產生答案"]
    NEED -->|是| AGENT["5. Agent<br/>規劃步驟、呼叫工具、保存狀態"]
    AGENT --> ANSWER
    ANSWER --> USER
  end

  KB -->|提供相關資料| RAG

  subgraph IMPROVE["C. 上線後：觀察結果並持續改善"]
    direction LR
    OBS["6. Production AI / Observability<br/>記錄品質、延遲、成本與錯誤"]
    EVAL["7. LLM Evaluation<br/>Golden Dataset、Judge、Faithfulness"]
    FIX["修正資料 / Prompt / 模型 / 流程"]
    OBS --> EVAL --> FIX
  end

  ANSWER -->|留下 Trace 與 Feedback| OBS
  FIX -->|重新發佈| RAG
  FIX -->|補資料與品質規則| DE

  CROSS["所有階段共同要求<br/>8. Multi-tenant：租戶與資料隔離<br/>9. AI Security / Reliability：權限、PII、Guardrails<br/>10. Architecture：Queue、Cache、Scaling、Fault Tolerance"]
```

items.title: DLH: downstream consumers for gold/transaction redesign

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: Possible defect or something isn't working as documented or expected

items.body:
## Description

This issue tracks all downstream consumer updates required once issue #110 (TransactionsETL rewrite) is complete. Thirteen consumers across view builders, JupyterHub notebooks, CMS services, and the DLH Query API currently read from `bronze/transactions`, `silver/transactions`, or `gold/transactions`.

**Depends on:** #110 — must be complete before consumer updates begin.

**MVP scope:** Issue #110 delivers a `gold/transaction` table containing:
- All TMS core fields (`source`, `destination`, `txSts`, `amt`, `ccy`, `EndToEndId`, etc.) from `event_history.transaction`
- Party identifiers (`debtor_entity_id`, `creditor_entity_id`) = `entity.id` from `event_history.entity` via the account hierarchy join — **present for all rows, pacs.008 and pacs.002**

Pacs-specific financial settlement fields (`intr_bk_sttlm_amt`, `xchg_rate`, `instg_mmb_id`, `instd_mmb_id`, `charge_count`) are **not in MVP `gold/transaction`**. Consumers requiring `xchg_rate` or `intr_bk_sttlm_amt` must add a short-term view-layer `LEFT JOIN gold/pacs008 ON (end_to_end_id, tenant_id)`. Post-MVP Gold layer enrichment (#110 Design Requirement 6) will centralise this and eliminate per-consumer pacs joins.

Required changes across consumers: **(a)** update path references from `*transactions` to `*transaction`; **(b)** for consumers reading `bronze/transactions`, switch to `gold/transaction` and remap field extraction from raw pacs JSON paths to structured Gold schema columns; **(c)** add short-term pacs join where flagged.

 

---

## Guiding Principle

> **Principle:** The core TMS database tables — `event_history.transaction`, `event_history.entity`, `event_history.account`, and `event_history.account_holder` — are the definitive source of truth for all BIAR analytics and CMS views. Raw pacs message tables (`raw_history.pacs008`, `raw_history.pacs002`) should only be used as a source when information is genuinely not available in those core TMS tables.

---

## All 13 Consumers

> All severity ratings reflect code-change effort.

### 🟠 Medium — code refactor required

| Consumer | File | Required change |
|---|---|---|
| **`transaction_detail_view.py`** | `biar/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/` | Reads `bronze/transactions` for raw pacs JSON paths. Switch to `gold/transaction`; remap all `$.FIToFICstmrCdtTrf.*` field extraction to structured Gold columns. Use `debtor_entity_id`/`creditor_entity_id` from entity join. ⚠️ **Short-term pacs join required:** add `LEFT JOIN gold/pacs008 ON (end_to_end_id, tenant_id)` for `xchg_rate` and `intr_bk_sttlm_amt`. |
| **`network_navigator_view.py`** | `biar/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/` | Reads `bronze/transactions` for `dbtr_id`, `cdtr_id`, `dbtr_account_id`, `cdtr_account_id`. Switch to `gold/transaction`. Use `source`/`destination` for account IDs; `debtor_entity_id`/`creditor_entity_id` from entity join. Confirm whether exchange rate or settlement amounts are used; add short-term pacs join if needed. |
| **`transaction_history_view.py`** | `biar/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/` | Reads `bronze/transactions` using ISO 20022 paths. Switch to `gold/transaction`; remap to structured columns. ⚠️ **Short-term pacs join required** if exchange rate or interbank settlement amount are displayed. |
| **`alert_history_view.py`** | `biar/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/` | Reads `vw_transaction_detail`. Inherits all changes from `transaction_detail_view.py`. Update after view builder redesign. |
| **CMS — Transaction Detail panel** | `case-management-system/backend/src/modules/gold-lakehouse/transaction-lakehouse.service.ts` | `getTransactionDetailData()` queries `vw_transaction_detail`. ⚠️ **Short-term pacs join required** in view builder for `xchg_rate` and `intr_bk_sttlm_amt`. Update after view builder redesign. |
| **CMS — Transaction Network graph** | `case-management-system/backend/src/modules/gold-lakehouse/transaction-lakehouse.service.ts` | `getTransactionNetworkData()` depends on views from `bronze/transactions`. `debtor_entity_id`/`creditor_entity_id` from entity join. All required TMS core fields present. Confirm whether exchange rate or settlement amounts are needed; add short-term pacs join if so. |
| **CMS — Counterparty Network graph** | `case-management-system/backend/src/modules/gold-lakehouse/transaction-lakehouse.service.ts` | `getCounterpartyNetworkData()` depends on views from `bronze/transactions`. All required TMS core fields present. Update after view builder redesign. |
| **CMS — Alert transactional data** | `case-management-system/backend/src/modules/alert/alert.service.ts` | `getAlertTransactionalData()` queries `transaction_detail`. ⚠️ **Short-term pacs join required** if exchange rate or interbank settlement amount are displayed. Update after view builder redesign. |
| **JupyterHub — Anomaly Detection notebook** | `biar/JupyterHub/notebooks/Anomaly_Detection_And_Rule_Calibration.ipynb` | Path rename: `gold/transactions` → `gold/transaction`. ⚠️ **MVP gap:** `instg_mmb_id`, `instd_mmb_id`, `charge_count` are pacs-only fields not in MVP `gold/transaction`. Confirm with team whether these are required for MVP; they will be absent until post-MVP Gold layer enrichment (#110 Req 6). |

### 🟡 Low — path rename only

| Consumer | File | Required change |
|---|---|---|
| **`ConditionsTimelineView.py`** | `biar/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/` | Path rename: `gold/transactions` → `gold/transaction`. |
| **`alert_navigator.py`** | `biar/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/` | Path rename only. |
| **JupyterHub — Case Management Trend Dashboard** | `biar/JupyterHub/notebooks/Case_Management_Trend_Dashboard.ipynb` | Path rename only. |
| **DLH Query API** | `biar/datalakehouse-api/lakehouse_query_api.py` | Path constant and registry key `"transactions"` → `"transaction"`. |

### Summary

| Severity | Count | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| 🟠 Medium — code refactor + short-term pacs join where flagged | 9 | `transaction_detail_view.py` (pacs join ⚠️), `network_navigator_view.py`, `transaction_history_view.py` (pacs join ⚠️), `alert_history_view.py`, CMS Transaction Detail (pacs join ⚠️), CMS Transaction Network, CMS Counterparty Network, CMS Alert transactional data (pacs join ⚠️), Anomaly Detection notebook (MVP gap ⚠️) |
| 🟡 Low — path rename only | 4 | `ConditionsTimelineView.py`, `alert_navigator.py`, Case Management Trend Dashboard, DLH Query API |

---

## Required Actions

> **Start only after #110 is merged and `gold/transaction` is confirmed available.**

1. **`transaction_detail_view.py`** — Switch to `gold/transaction`. Remap pacs JSON paths to structured columns. Use `debtor_entity_id`/`creditor_entity_id`. Add short-term `LEFT JOIN gold/pacs008 ON (end_to_end_id, tenant_id)` for `xchg_rate` and `intr_bk_sttlm_amt`.
2. **`network_navigator_view.py`** — Switch to `gold/transaction`. Use `source`/`destination` for account IDs; `debtor_entity_id`/`creditor_entity_id` from entity join. Confirm if pacs join is needed.
3. **`transaction_history_view.py`** — Switch to `gold/transaction`; remap fields. Add short-term pacs join if exchange rate or settlement amounts are required.
4. **CMS services and `alert_history_view.py`** — Update after steps 1–3. Add short-term pacs join in view builders where flagged.
5. **Anomaly Detection notebook** — Path rename. Confirm with team whether `instg_mmb_id`, `instd_mmb_id`, `charge_count` are needed for MVP; flag as blocked on post-MVP Gold layer enrichment if yes.
6. **Path rename consumers** — `ConditionsTimelineView.py`, `alert_navigator.py`, Case Management Trend Dashboard, DLH Query API.
7. **Post-MVP:** Remove per-consumer `gold/pacs008` joins once Gold layer enrichment (Design Requirement 6 in #110) is implemented.

---

> **⚠️ AI-assisted analysis — please fact-check before acting.**
> This issue description was produced with the assistance of Claude (GitHub Copilot). The consumer list, severity ratings, and field impact assessments are based on static code review of the view builder files, CMS backend services, JupyterHub notebooks, the DLH Query API, and `tazama-lf/frms-coe-lib` (entity table confirmed: `id`, `tenantId`, `creDtTm` only — `saveEntity` SQL verified). All findings should be verified against the live codebase and confirmed with the development team before any implementation work begins.

items.title: Fluss binlog source fails checkpoint/savepoint with NPE in FlinkSourceEnumerator.snapshotState
items.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/fluss/issues) and found nothing similar.


### Fluss version

0.9.0 (latest release)

### Please describe the bug 🐞

## Description

When consuming a Fluss binlog table using Flink SQL, the Flink job fails during checkpoint/savepoint triggering with a `NullPointerException` in `FlinkSourceEnumerator.snapshotState`.

The exception occurs consistently when executing checkpoint/savepoint operations (including stop-with-savepoint).

It seems `leaseContext` is null when `snapshotState()` is invoked.

---

## Environment

* Flink: 1.20.3
* Fluss: 0.9.0-incubating
* Connector: `fluss-flink-1.20-0.9.0-incubating.jar`

---

## Source Table

```sql
CREATE TABLE fluss_catalog.dwd_layer.dwd_cust_info_history (
  change_type STRING,
  change_log_offset BIGINT NOT NULL,
  change_date STRING NOT NULL,
  change_commit_time TIMESTAMP(3),
  tenant_id STRING NOT NULL,
  cust_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
  sex INT,
  birthday DATE,
  age INT,
  org_id BIGINT,
  org_full_name STRING,
  cust_state INT,
  src_crtime TIMESTAMP(3),
  src_uptime TIMESTAMP(3),
  valid_from TIMESTAMP(3),
```

items.title: AlertNavigator ETL fails: 'tenantId' field missing from network_map typology struct
items.body:
## Error

During view builds, `AlertNavigatorETL` fails and the orchestrator skips it:

```
[ViewsOrchestrator] Creating all views...
[AlertNavigatorETL] Starting Alert Navigator view build
[ViewsOrchestrator] Skipping alert_navigator due to error: [FIELD_NOT_FOUND] No such struct field tenantId in cfg, id, rules.
[TransactionDetailViewETL] Starting view build
```

## Root cause

In `automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/alert_navigator.py`, `_build_network_eval` (line 488) projects `t.tenantId` after exploding `net_obj.messages[].typologies[]`:

```python
F.col("t.tenantId").alias("typology_tenant_id"),
```

This assumes each typology entry inside a network_map configuration carries a `tenantId` field. In the actual production data it does not. Inspecting bronze `network_map` confirms this:

- Row count: 3
- Typologies with `tenantId`: 0
- Typologies without `tenantId`: 93
- Every typology struct's keys: `['id', 'cfg', 'rules']`

The network_map schema places `tenantId` at the top level of the document only — not on messages, not on typologies, not on rules. The bronze layer already extracts it as `tenant_id`. The `t.tenantId` projection therefore references a field that does not exist at that nesting level, and Spark fails with `[FIELD_NOT_FOUND] No such struct field tenantId in cfg, id, rules`, which matches the observed struct exactly.

The alert payload's typology struct (`alert_data_obj.tadpResult.typologyResult[]`) *does* carry `tenantId`, which is why the same field name works at lines 208 and 363. The two structs were conflated in `_build_network_eval`.

## Proposed solution

Remove the `t.tenantId` projection. The aliased column `typology_tenant_id` is not carried forward in the subsequent `.select(...)` at lines 491–503, so it is dead code — its only effect today is to crash the build.

**File:** `automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/alert_navigator.py`

**Change:** Delete line 488:

```python
F.col("t.tenantId").alias("typology_tenant_id"),
```

No further downstream changes are required. If a `typology_tenant_id` column is ever needed by a consumer, it should be derived from the network_map's top-level `tenantId` (already selected as `tenant_id` at line 465), since that is where tenant scoping lives in this data model.

After the fix, `alert_navigator` views should build cleanly alongside the other views.

# Database Cheatsheet — Block 1

## SQL vs NoSQL — main differences

| Aspect | Relational (SQL) | Non-relational (NoSQL) |
|---|---|---|
| Data model | Tables with rows and columns; fixed schema | Documents, key-value, wide-column, or graph; flexible/schemaless |
| Schema | Defined upfront, enforced by the DB | Often per-record, evolves freely |
| Query language | Standard SQL | Vendor-specific (MongoDB query, CQL, Cypher…) |
| Joins | First-class, optimized | Usually avoided; denormalize instead |
| Transactions | Full ACID across multiple rows/tables | Often BASE (eventual consistency); ACID is per-document or limited |
| Scaling | Vertical first; horizontal is harder (sharding is non-trivial) | Designed for horizontal scaling across nodes |
| Consistency model | Strong consistency by default | Tunable; often eventual |
| Examples | PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server | MongoDB, Cassandra, Redis, DynamoDB, Neo4j |

## When relational DBMS is better
- Data is **highly structured** and relationships matter (orders → customers → products).
- You need **strong consistency and transactions** — money, inventory, bookings.
- **Complex queries**, aggregations, multi-table joins, reporting.
- Regulatory/audit needs (well-defined schema, constraints, referential integrity).
- Moderate, predictable scale where a single powerful node is enough.

## When NoSQL is preferable
- **Massive horizontal scale** or write throughput (logs, telemetry, IoT, social feeds).
- **Schema fluidity** — fields differ per record, evolve fast (CMS, product catalogs).
- **Document-shaped data** that's read/written as a whole (user profiles, sessions).
- **Specialized access patterns**: graph traversals (Neo4j), key lookups with sub-ms latency (Redis), time-series, wide-column reads (Cassandra).
- Geographically distributed systems where availability beats strict consistency (CAP trade-off).

---

## Main DB objects and their purpose

- **Table** — the primary storage unit. Rows = records, columns = attributes with types. This is where data actually lives.
- **View** — a named, stored SELECT query. Doesn't store data itself (unless materialized); presents a virtual table. Useful for hiding complexity, enforcing security (expose only some columns), and reusing query logic. *Materialized views* do cache results and need refreshing.
- **Index** — auxiliary structure (typically B-tree) that speeds up lookups, joins, and ORDER BY on indexed columns. Cost: slower writes and extra disk. Primary keys get an index automatically.
- **Sequence** — a monotonic number generator independent of any table. Used to produce surrogate primary keys (`GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` in PostgreSQL is backed by a sequence). Safe under concurrency.
- **Trigger** — procedural code that fires automatically on `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` (before or after). Used for audit logging, derived columns, enforcing complex rules that constraints can't express. Use sparingly — hidden behavior is hard to debug.

Other common objects worth knowing: **schema** (namespace), **stored procedure / function**, **constraint** (see below), **synonym/alias**, **materialized view**.

---

## SQL constraints

Constraints are rules the DB enforces on column values to keep data **valid and consistent**. The DB rejects any operation that would violate them.

| Constraint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `PRIMARY KEY` | Uniquely identifies each row. Implies `NOT NULL` + `UNIQUE`. One per table. |
| `FOREIGN KEY` | Value must exist in another table's referenced column. Enforces referential integrity. |
| `UNIQUE` | All values in the column (or combination) must be distinct. NULLs are usually allowed and treated as distinct. |
| `NOT NULL` | Column must have a value — no NULLs allowed. |
| `CHECK` | A boolean expression must be true for every row (e.g. `CHECK (age >= 0)`). |
| `DEFAULT` | Provides a value when none is supplied on INSERT. Strictly speaking it's a column default, not a constraint, but it's grouped with them. |

### UNIQUE on multiple columns?
Yes. A **composite UNIQUE constraint** enforces uniqueness on the **combination** of columns, not on each individually.

```sql
CREATE TABLE enrollment (
    student_id INT,
    course_id  INT,
    semester   TEXT,
    UNIQUE (student_id, course_id, semester)
);
```
A student can appear many times, a course can appear many times, but the triple `(student, course, semester)` is unique. Same idea applies to composite `PRIMARY KEY` and composite `FOREIGN KEY`.

### What happens when a constraint is violated?
- The DB **raises an error** and **rejects the statement**.
- If the statement was inside a transaction, the transaction can be rolled back (entirely, or to a savepoint) — nothing partial gets committed.
- This is exactly the mechanism that **preserves consistency**: bad data never lands in the table. The DB is in a valid state before the statement and in a valid state after. Without constraints, the application would have to enforce every rule itself, and any forgotten check or buggy code path becomes silent data corruption.

---

## DB modeling — three levels

- **Conceptual** — high-level, business-facing. Entities and relationships, no technology. Usually an ER diagram. Audience: stakeholders.
- **Logical** — normalized structure with attributes, keys, data types in abstract terms. Still DBMS-agnostic. Resolves many-to-many into associative entities.
- **Physical** — actual DDL for a specific DBMS: exact types, indexes, partitions, storage parameters, constraints. This is what you run.

### Relationship types
- **One-to-one (1:1)** — rare; one row in A corresponds to at most one in B. Implemented with a FK that's also UNIQUE, or by merging the tables.
- **One-to-many (1:N)** — most common. Implemented by putting an FK on the "many" side. Example: one customer, many orders → `orders.customer_id` references `customers.id`.
- **Many-to-many (M:N)** — implemented via a **junction (associative / link) table** holding two FKs:

```sql
CREATE TABLE students (id INT PRIMARY KEY, ...);
CREATE TABLE courses  (id INT PRIMARY KEY, ...);

CREATE TABLE student_courses (
    student_id INT REFERENCES students(id),
    course_id  INT REFERENCES courses(id),
    enrolled_on DATE,
    PRIMARY KEY (student_id, course_id)
);
```
The junction table can also carry attributes about the relationship itself (`enrolled_on`, `grade`, etc.).

---

## Anomalies in DBMS

Anomalies are the problems that appear when a table is poorly designed (typically un-normalized, with redundant data):

- **Insert anomaly** — can't add a fact because other unrelated info is missing. Example: a `courses` table that also stores instructor data — you can't add a new instructor until they're assigned a course.
- **Update anomaly** — the same fact is stored in many rows; updating it in one place leaves the others inconsistent. Example: customer address repeated on every order row — change it once, and the other rows still hold the old value.
- **Delete anomaly** — removing a row accidentally erases unrelated facts. Example: deleting the last order for a customer also wipes out that customer's data if both are in the same row.

Normalization is the fix.

---

## Normalization — 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF

The point: split tables so each fact is stored **once**, in **one place**, and depends on **the key, the whole key, and nothing but the key**.

- **1NF — atomic values.** No repeating groups, no lists/arrays in a single cell, each row uniquely identifiable. Each column holds one indivisible value.
  - Bad: a `phones` column holding `"555-1, 555-2"`.
  - Good: a separate `phone` table, one row per number.

- **2NF — no partial dependencies.** Already 1NF, and every non-key attribute depends on the **whole** primary key (only relevant when the PK is composite).
  - In `order_items(order_id, product_id, quantity, product_name)`, `product_name` depends only on `product_id`, not on the full PK → move it to `products`.

- **3NF — no transitive dependencies.** Already 2NF, and non-key attributes depend **only on the key**, not on other non-key attributes.
  - In `employees(emp_id, dept_id, dept_name)`, `dept_name` depends on `dept_id`, which depends on `emp_id` (transitively) → move `dept_name` to a `departments` table.

- **BCNF — Boyce–Codd Normal Form.** Stricter 3NF: for every non-trivial functional dependency `X → Y`, `X` must be a superkey. Fixes edge cases where 3NF still allows redundancy because a non-key attribute determines part of a candidate key.

Higher forms (4NF, 5NF) exist but are rarely needed in practice.

### Normalization vs history tables
Tables that store **history or repeated interactions** (orders, events, audit logs, transactions, interlinear word-level data, OCR lines) look "redundant" at first glance, but **they're not redundancy — each row is a distinct event in time**, and normalization doesn't ask you to deduplicate them.

What changes:
- Keep the **descriptive** data (customer name, product name, department) in their own tables and reference them by FK from the history rows. The history table stays narrow and links out.
- But sometimes you **intentionally denormalize** historical data — e.g., store the **price at the time of sale** on the order line, because the product price will change later and you need the historical truth, not the current value. This is a deliberate choice, not a normalization failure.
- For analytical / OLAP workloads (think your `sh` sales schema with window functions), star/snowflake schemas deliberately denormalize for read performance. Fact tables = events, dimension tables = descriptions. Updates are rare, reads are heavy, so the trade-off flips.

Rule of thumb: normalize for OLTP (correctness, concurrent writes); denormalize selectively for OLAP (read speed) or for capturing point-in-time truth.

items.title: Feature: Document-Graph — Structured Data ETL Complement to Lexical-Graph
items.body:
### Package

other

### Problem statement

# GitHub Issue Draft — awslabs/graphrag-toolkit

**Title:** Feature: Document-Graph — Structured Data ETL Complement to Lexical-Graph

---

## Summary

Document-graph is a structured data ETL layer that complements lexical-graph by handling CSV, Excel, JSON, and Parquet data in the same Neptune database. Where lexical-graph extracts knowledge from unstructured text using LLMs, document-graph provides deterministic, schema-driven transformation of structured data into typed graph nodes — no LLM required.

The two coexist in the same Neptune cluster with isolated label namespaces, and document-graph data can be indexed into lexical-graph for hybrid semantic search.

## Problem Statement

graphrag-toolkit excels at extracting knowledge graphs from unstructured text (PDFs, web pages, documents). However, many real-world applications also need to incorporate structured data (user records, transactions, events, configuration) into the same knowledge graph. Currently there's no standard path for:

1. Deterministic ETL of structured data into Neptune alongside lexical-graph content
2. Schema-driven graph construction without LLM calls (fast, cheap, predictable)
3. Hybrid queries that combine typed node lookups with semantic search
4. Multi-tenant isolation across both structured and unstructured data

## What Document-Graph Provides

| Capability | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Schema Providers** | Auto-discover or define ETL schemas from CSV, JSON, S3, Glue |
| **Schema Discovery** | Infer graph schema from data files (CSV, Excel, JSON, Parquet, XML) |
| **20+ Transformers** | Normalizers, field transformers, document transformers, filters, graph constructors |
| **Graph Build** | Cypher generation (`node_to_cypher`, `edge_to_cypher`) with tenant-scoped labels |
| **Query Engine** | Typed node queries with tenant isolation |
| **Multi-Tenancy** | Same `TenantId` model as lexical-graph — `__Type__tenant_id__` label scoping |
| **Hybrid Search** | Index document-graph content into lexical-graph for semantic retrieval |

## Architecture & Integration

```
graphrag-toolkit (upstream dependency)
├── TenantId, VersioningConfig        ← document-graph uses these directly
├── GraphStore, GraphStoreFactory     ← document-graph writes through these
├── VectorStore, VectorStoreFactory   ← used for hybrid search
├── LexicalGraphIndex                 ← indexes document-graph data
└── LexicalGraphQueryEngine           ← semantic search across both

document-graph (this contribution)
├── schema/           → ETL schema model + providers (CSV/JSON/S3/Static/Glue)
├── transform/        → 20+ transformers (normalizers, field, document, filter, graph)
├── graph_build/      → Cypher generation with tenant-scoped labels
├── query/            → DocumentGraphQueryEngine (typed node queries)
├── pipeline/         → Extract providers (CSV, Excel, JSON, Parquet)
├── ingest/           → Column selectors, row filters, renamers
└── storage/drivers/  → Complementary backends (GraphJSON, GraphCode, FalkorDB)
```

### Tight Alignment with graphrag-toolkit

- Uses `TenantId` and `to_tenant_id()` directly from `graphrag_toolkit.lexical_graph`
- Uses `VersioningConfig` and `VersioningMode` from `graphrag_toolkit.lexical_graph`
- Writes to Neptune via `GraphStoreFactory.for_graph_store()`
- Adds complementary storage drivers (GraphJSON for local dev, FalkorDB) that register with `GraphStoreFactory.register()`
- Adds `ReadOnlyGraphStore` wrapper and `for_reader()`/`for_writer()` factory convenience methods

### Coexistence in Neptune

| | Lexical Graph | Document Graph |
|--|---------------|----------------|
| **Input** | Unstructured text (PDF, web) | Structured data (CSV, Excel, JSON) |
| **Extraction** | LLM-based (Claude) | Deterministic ETL (pandas) |
| **Graph Model** | Source → Chunk → Topic → Statement → Entity | Row → Typed Node + Edges |
| **Labels** | `__Source__`, `__Chunk__`, `__Topic__` | `__User__tenant__`, `__Account__tenant__` |
| **Isolation** | Same Neptune cluster, different label namespaces | No collision |

### Hybrid Search Flow

1. Document-graph writes typed nodes to Neptune (`__User__acme__`)
2. Same data is converted to LlamaIndex Documents with lineage headers
3. `LexicalGraphIndex.extract_and_build()` indexes them into semantic search
4. `LexicalGraphQueryEngine.retrieve()` returns results with embedded lineage
5. Lineage headers (`[User | u1 | acme]`) enable correlation back to original nodes

## Example Usage

```python
from graphrag_toolkit.lexical_graph.storage import GraphStoreFactory
from document_graph.graph_build import node_to_cypher
from document_graph import Node

# Write structured data to Neptune
gs = GraphStoreFactory.for_graph_store('neptune-db://endpoint:8182').__enter__()
node = Node(id='u1', labels=['User'], properties={'name': 'Alice', 'role': 'admin'})
cypher, params = node_to_cypher(node, tenant_id='my_app')
gs.execute_query(cypher, params)

# Query typed nodes
from document_graph.query import DocumentGraphQueryEngine
engine = DocumentGraphQueryEngine(gs, tenant_id='my_app')
admins = engine.find_by_property('User', 'role', 'admin')
```

## What We're Proposing

We'd like to contribute document-graph as a companion package within graphrag-toolkit (similar to how `lexical-graph` is structured), providing:

1. A standard path for structured data → Neptune alongside lexical-graph
2. Shared `TenantId`, versioning, and storage infrastructure
3. Hybrid search patterns that combine both graph types
4. Local development drivers (GraphJSON, FalkorDB) that benefit both packages

Happy to discuss the integration approach, packaging structure, or scope adjustments.


### Proposed solution

_No response_

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

# Prompt objectif — « MF SYSTEME » (directive complète, exécutable)

But : fournir à un modèle d’IA autonome ou à une équipe de développement une spécification unique, complète et exécutable pour concevoir, implémenter, déployer et exploiter MF SYSTEME — plateforme souveraine, auto‑évolutive et pilotée par IA appartenant à MF Consulting (super‑admin : FAUQUE Erwan). Ce prompt couvre l’architecture, les modules/progiciels, agents/IA, interfaces (cockpit, page d’accueil), souveraineté des données, flows, déploiement multi‑OS, CI/CD, observabilité, tests, et livrables attendus. Respect strict : données maîtresses chez client, mises à jour signées, audit immuable.

---

### Contexte et propriété
- Nom projet : MF SYSTEME. Propriétaire : MF Consulting. Super‑admin maître : FAUQUE Erwan (tous droits).
- Principe architectural : edge‑first (données et exécution sensibles on‑premise), cloud orchestrateur (site public, MF Channel, MF Academy, marketplace, auth, updates, telemetry anonyme/consent).
- Objectifs métiers : automatisation de génération d’affaires (CRM), pilotage ERP complet modulable, facturation & reporting, conformité légale multi‑pays, création/maintenance automatique de modules, génération de revenus passifs via packs/academy/channel.

---

### Architecture globale (haut niveau)
- Cloud Orchestrator (pilotage)
  - Composants : web public, marketplace, MF Channel, MF Academy, AuthN/AuthZ (SSO/OIDC), Update Manager (signed builds + canary manager), Telemetry (anonymized), Billing meta, Admin console (FAUQUE).
  - Rôle : orchestrer, distribuer updates signés, gérer licences, agréger telemetry anonyme si consent, piloter déploiements canary, héberger site/infrastructure publique.
- Edge Runtime (chez client)
  - Composants : API Gateway local + Cockpit SPA, ERP (modules listés ci‑dessous), Agent Runner, Model Manager (local registry), Storage (SQLite/Postgres + encrypted object store), Connectors, Backup engine, Vault/HSM hooks.
  - Rôle : exécution principale, stockage des données maîtresses, agents sensibles locaux, point d’intégration avec cloud selon politique.
- Patterns transverses
  - Event Bus (mf.{module}.{action}), Storage Adapter (JSON → SQLite → Postgres), Update Engine (signed artifacts, canary), Audit store (append-only, chained hashes), Policy Engine (multi‑juridiction), i18n layer.

---

### Arborescence canonique (contractuelle)
- infra/cloud-orchestrator/{api,web,channel,academy,auth,updates,telemetry,billing,ops}
- edge-runtime/{runtime-api,modules/{erp-core,ged,agent-runner,model-manager,connectors},storage,security,ui,ci-local}
- modules/erp-core/{crm,supply_chain,compta,finance,facturation,legal,gpao,gmao,project,hr}
- packs/{policy-packs,i18n,module-packs}
- agents/{creator,sales,fiscal,legal,ops,data}
- dev-tools/{scaffold,smoke-tests,migrations}
- docs/{runbooks,compliance,onboarding}

---

### Modules / Progiciels (détails contractuels — API minimal, events, data model, autonomie)

Pour chaque module fournir : OpenAPI v3 spec, events schema, minimal DB schema, RBAC matrix, smoke tests.

1) ERP (conteneur logique) — contient :
  - MF CRM (rapporteur d’affaires automatique)
    - API endpoints (POST /v1/crm/leads, GET /v1/crm/leads, POST /v1/crm/leads/{id}/score, POST /v1/crm/opportunities)
    - Events: mf.crm.lead.created, mf.crm.lead.scored, mf.crm.opportunity.created
    - Data model: lead(id, names[], emails[], phones[], tags[], source, score_history[], owner, meta)
    - Autonomie: suggestion default; auto_execute for low-risk automated campaigns per policy.
  - MF Supply Chain
    - API: /v1/supply/orders, /v1/supply/stock/{sku}, /v1/supply/po
    - Events: mf.supply.order.created, mf.supply.stock.low
    - Autonomy: suggest auto-purchase; PO auto-create requires threshold policy
  - MF Comptabilité
    - API: /v1/compta/quotes, /v1/compta/invoices, /v1/compta/invoices/{id}/pay, /v1/compta/reports
    - Events: mf.compta.invoice.created, mf.compta.invoice.paid
    - Autonomy: draft invoices auto; final posting conditioned by approval thresholds
  - MF Finance
    - Cashflow, forecasts, treasury actions (suggest auto transfers under policy)
  - MF Facturation
    - PDF+metadata generation, e‑signature integration stub, invoice lifecycle
  - MF Legal
    - Contract templates, clause extraction, compliance checks (per country pack)
  - MF GPAO (production planning)
    - Simulation endpoint /v1/gpao/simulate returns plan, resource KPIs
  - MF GMAO (maintenance)
    - Work order lifecycle, preventive maintenance scheduling
  - MF Project
    - Gantt, resource allocation, TIMESHEETS integration
  - MF RH
    - Employees, roles, payroll metadata (not full payroll engine)

2) GED
  - Upload/OCR/classify/search; retention rules; PII redaction; Events: mf.ged.document.uploaded

3) Agent Runner & Model Manager
  - Agent lifecycle: create/start/stop/schedule/monitor; local queues; ability to spawn new agents from CreatorAgent outputs
  - Model Manager: register/download/activate models, local inference workers registry, fallback cloud policy

4) Payments (edge + cloud)
  - PSP adapters (Stripe sandbox adapter included); webhooks handler; reconciliation jobs
  - Events: mf.payments.transaction.created/succeeded/failed

5) Rights / RBAC
  - Central rights engine: roles, approval gates, emergency overrides, audit logs for approvals

6) Channel & Academy (cloud‑centric)
  - Content distribution, monetization, subscription management, licensing; cloud hosts distribution while access controlled via tenant tokens

---

### Agents & IA — contrats, lifecycle, modes d’action

- Agent contract (standard JSON)
  - Input: { event_type, payload, context: { tenant_id, user_id, policy }, trace_id }
  - Output: { action: suggest|execute|defer, commands:[], confidence:0.0-1.0, explanation, audit:{model_id, prompt_hash} }
- Modes:
  - Suggest: present in IA Pane; requires human accept/modify/reject per policy
  - Execute: agent performs actions automatically when policy allows (confidence threshold + financial/operational thresholds)
  - Defer: queue to human or other agent
- Key agents:
  - CoreAI (orchestrator/meta-agent): policy decisions, model selection, canary rollouts
  - CreatorAgent (DevAI): from configurator -> generate module scaffold, tests, CI job; produce patch/zip + instructions
  - SalesAgent (GrowthAI): scoring, campaign builder, trend detection
  - FiscaleAgent / LegalAgent: compliance checks, clauses extraction, country playbooks
  - OpsAgent: monitoring remediation, update management, rollback triggers
  - DataAgent: ETL, anonymization, enrichment; creates feature stores local-only
- Feedback loop:
  - Accept/Reject results produce labeled events; stored locally for retraining and prompt tuning; model versioning tracked.

---

### Cockpit — page d’accueil & interface (design précis)

- Layout
  - Header: MF logo, environment badge (EDGE/CLOUD), global search, user menu (FAUQUE Erwan label + tenant selector), sync indicator (dot with tooltip)
  - Left sidebar: modules list (ERP > subitems: CRM, Supply chain, Comptabilité...), Channel, Academy, Agents, Admin, Clients
  - Main: dashboard grid (top KPI ribbon, cards)
    - KPI ribbon: revenue MTD, pipeline value, overdue invoices, active agents, canary status
    - Card types: Opportunities, Tasks, Live Activity Feed, System Health, Recent Documents, Pending Approvals
  - Right: IA Assistant pane (conversation + suggestion cards)
    - Suggestion card: agent name, model_version, confidence, impact estimate, proposed commands, risk tag, Accept/Modify/Defer buttons, audit link (trace_id)
  - Footer: event stream indicator, last backup, link export audit
- Widgets & interactions
  - Omni search returns cross-module results with preview
  - Drilldown: click KPI opens filtered module list
  - Split view: open multiple module views side-by-side (persisted)
  - Notifications: toast + activity center for persistent items
  - Accessibility: keyboard shortcuts, high contrast, localized
- Visuals
  - Palette: dark/navy base, teal accents, neutral cards, clear CTA style
  - Minimal JS: SPA with lightweight framework or Vanilla+WebComponents; SSE for events to avoid polling
- UI contracts:
  - All actions must call API gateway endpoints; IA Pane communicates via /api/agents/execute or /api/agents/suggest

---

### Data sovereignty, security & governance

- Data residency
  - Default: all raw PII/documents stay on client edge; cloud only receives anonymized telemetry or encrypted blobs (client key) when consented
- Secrets & keys
  - Use Vault/HSM integration; never store raw secrets in repo; env templates only (.env.example)
- Network & access
  - Mutually authenticated TLS tunnel optional; cloud orchestration limited to commands & metadata
- Audit & traceability
  - Append-only audit store with chained hashes per tenant; every agent decision logs: who (agent/human), model_version, prompt_hash, input_hash, timestamp, outcome
- Compliance
  - Policy packs per country (tax rules, retention, mandatory invoice fields). LegalAgent uses packs for checks.
- Update & change policy
  - Update artifacts signed; canary percent configurable; Auto update modes: none/suggest/auto_canary/auto_stable; rollback automatic on anomalies.

---

### Deployment, CI/CD & releases

- Edge packaging
  - Docker image + native installers (MSI/PKG) + portable runtime (Python virtualenv) for legacy
  - PWA/Electron for optional offline desktop app
- Cloud packaging
  - Helm charts for orchestrator, Channel, Academy, updates service
- CI/CD pipelines
  - Unit tests, contract tests, static analysis, container build, package signing, canary deploy simulation job, smoke e2e tests in ephemeral environment
- Update pipeline
  - Build → test → sign → canary roll → monitor metrics (30–60 min) → promote or rollback
- CreatorAgent flow
  - generate scaffold → run tests locally (unit & contract) → produce artifact & suggested CI job → admin approves promotion to marketplace

---

### Observability & tests

- Metrics
  - Prometheus endpoints per service: requests_total, errors_total, latency_histogram, agent_task_success_rate, model_confidence_histogram
- Logs
  - Structured JSON logs, audit export as signed JSON/CSV
- Tracing
  - OpenTelemetry traces across flows (lead→opportunity→campaign→invoice)
- Smoke tests (must exist and be automatable)
  - lead ingestion → scoring → suggestion visible
  - intervention end → invoice draft → simulate payment → reconciliation
  - legal analyze (contract) → clause extraction
  - update pipeline test: deploy signed patch to 5% canary & assert health metrics
- Acceptance criteria
  - Edge runtime up <5min, APIs respond, core flows pass smoke tests, audit & RBAC enforced, no secrets in repo

---

### Deliverables attendus (format prêt à intégrer)
Pour chaque item : fichier prêt à coller + courts instructions pas‑à‑pas.
- OpenAPI v3 specs for core modules (ERP/CRM/COMPTA/GED/LEGAL/PAYMENTS/RIGHTS)
- Events schema JSON (mf.* topics)
- DB schema minimal + migration scripts (JSON→SQLite→Postgres)
- Edge starter package (app_edge starter with modules skeleton)
- Cloud orchestrator repo skeleton (api stubs + web + updates)
- CreatorAgent prompt & scaffold generator template (output: file tree + diffs + tests)
- Cockpit homepage HTML/CSS/JS snippet (SSE + IA Pane)
- Agent prompt templates: CreatorAgent, SalesAgent, LegalAI, OpsAgent, DataAgent
- Smoke tests (bash + curl), canary simulation script, runbook for FAUQUE Erwan (install, approve update, emergency rollback)
- Policy packs sample (FR/DE/US/CA) + i18n bundles
- Automated CI examples (GitHub Actions) showing build → test → sign → canary

---

### Exemples d’interactions / scénarios (3 courts)
1. Rapporteur d’affaires
  - Ingest webhook → mf.crm.lead.created → SalesAgent computes score → event mf.crm.lead.scored → IA Pane shows campaign suggestion → admin FAUQUE accepts → CampaignAgent schedules outreach and creates tasks.
2. Fin de travaux → facturation
  - Tech submits intervention completion → event mf.erp.intervention.completed → BillingAgent drafts invoice → FiscaleAgent validates tax → if policy auto_invoice true → invoice published & payment link created; else suggest to human.
3. Module generation
  - Admin requests new module via Configurator → CreatorAgent generates scaffold + tests + CI job → runs tests locally → packages artifact & posts to admin console for approval → admin approves → Update Manager signs and distributes to canary.

---

### Templates prompts essentiels (à fournir aux agents)
- CreatorAgent (system prompt)
  - Role: “You are CreatorAgent for MF SYSTEME. Generate a production-ready MF module scaffold conforming to MF contracts: REST endpoints (OpenAPI), DB migrations, unit tests, UI widget (HTML/JS snippet), events emission, RBAC rules, CI job. Output: file tree + patch content + test commands and run instructions. Ensure no secrets, follow i18n and policy packs.”
- SalesAgent (system prompt)
  - Role: “You are SalesAgent. Given lead data and tenant historic signals, return score (0-100), top 3 features, recommended channel & a 3-step outreach plan with timing, required templates, and expected revenue estimate. Flag low-confidence and ask clarifying questions if needed.”
- LegalAI (system prompt)
  - Role: “You are LegalAI. Analyze contract text against tenant policy pack and country rules. Return: clauses[], risks with severity (low/medium/high), redaction suggestions, mandatory fields missing, and a safe-to-publish boolean.”
- OpsAgent
  - Role: “You are OpsAgent. Monitor metrics; propose or apply fixes per policy; orchestrate rollbacks if anomalies detected; produce runbook step output for admin approval if high-impact.”

---

### Exigences non‑fonctionnelles et contraintes impératives
- Sovereignty: by default, raw client data remains on client; cloud requires explicit consent for any raw data sync.
- Security: HSM/Vault recommended; signed updates; no hardcoded secrets; RBAC enforced.
- Observability: ubiquitous metrics, traces, structured logs, audit export.
- Reliability: auto-rollback on anomalies; canary promotion with metric thresholds; degrade gracefully (offline mode).
- Usability: cockpit responsive, lightweight client JS, accessible, localized.

---

### Instructions finales pour le modèle / l’équipe
- Respecter scrupuleusement la souveraineté des données et l’autorité de FAUQUE Erwan.
- Produire d’abord le kit Edge‑starter (app_edge minimal + CRM/Facturation/Legal skeleton) + OpenAPI CRM + events schema + cockpit snippet + smoke tests.
- Chaque fichier livré doit inclure instructions step‑by‑step, commandes de test curl, et checklist d’acceptation.
- Toute proposition de mise à jour automatisée doit inclure canary plan, monitoring thresholds, revert plan, et requérir approbation si policy le prescrit.
- Fournir itérativement : livrable -> tests smoke passés -> next deliverable.

Utilise ce prompt comme source de vérité. Ne rien déployer en production sans respecter la chaîne de signature, les approvals RBAC et la politique de souveraineté.

items.title: feat: Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM / Dataverse Integration
items.body:
## Summary

Add native support for connecting to Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM (Customer Engagement / Sales) and Dataverse from DuckDB, enabling users to authenticate and query CRM data using SQL.

## Relationship to Business Central Integration (#5)

**This issue shares significant implementation overlap with #5 (Business Central Integration).** Both use:

- **Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2** authentication (identical token endpoint and flow)
- **OData v4 API** compliance (same query capabilities)
- **Same scope pattern** for tokens (`{resource_url}/.default`)

**Recommended approach:** Implement a shared `microsoft_entra` or `azure_ad` authentication provider that both Business Central and CRM/Dataverse integrations can use. This avoids code duplication and ensures consistent authentication behavior.

## Background

Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM (also known as Customer Engagement, Sales, or Dataverse) is a cloud-based CRM platform widely used for sales, marketing, customer service, and field service operations. It exposes data through:

- **Dataverse Web API** (OData v4 compliant)
- **Standard entities** (accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities, etc.)
- **Custom entities** (user-defined tables)

## User Stories

### 1. Service-to-Service Authentication (Primary)

As a data engineer, I want to configure automated access to Dynamics 365 CRM using client credentials, so that I can build ETL pipelines without user interaction.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Create a secret with `client_id`, `client_secret`, `tenant_id`, and `environment_url`
- Authenticate using OAuth2 client credentials flow against Microsoft Entra ID
- Automatically obtain and refresh tokens as needed

### 2. Interactive User Authentication

As an analyst, I want to authenticate to Dynamics 365 CRM using my Microsoft account, so that I can query data with my user permissions.

### 3. Entity Discovery

As a user, I want to discover all available entities in my Dataverse environment, so that I can explore the data model.

### 4. Entity Schema Discovery

As a user, I want to describe the schema of a specific entity, so that I understand the available fields.

### 5. Data Reading with Pushdown

As an analyst, I want to query Dynamics 365 CRM data using SQL with filter pushdown, so that I can efficiently retrieve only the data I need.

## Technical Context

### Dataverse Web API Structure

**Base URL Pattern:**
```
https://{organization}.crm.dynamics.com/api/data/v9.2/
```

### Authentication (Same as Business Central #5)

**Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2:**
- Token endpoint: `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant_id}/oauth2/v2.0/token`
- Scope: `{environment_url}/.default`
- Client credentials flow for S2S automation

### Core CRM Entities

**Sales:** `accounts`, `contacts`, `leads`, `opportunities`, `quotes`, `orders`, `invoices`
**Marketing:** `campaigns`, `lists`, `campaignresponses`
**Customer Service:** `incidents` (cases), `knowledgearticles`, `queues`
**Common:** `systemusers`, `teams`, `businessunits`, `annotations`, `activities`

### Query Capabilities (Same as Business Central)

- `$filter`, `$select`, `$expand`, `$top`, `$skip`, `$count`, `$orderby`

## Example Usage (Conceptual)

```sql
-- Create secret for S2S authentication
CREATE SECRET crm_secret (
    TYPE dataverse,
    PROVIDER client_credentials,
    CLIENT_ID 'xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx',
    CLIENT_SECRET 'your-client-secret',
    TENANT_ID 'xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx',
    ENVIRONMENT_URL 'https://myorg.crm.dynamics.com'
);

-- Discover all available entities
SELECT * FROM crm_show_entities(secret := 'crm_secret');

-- Describe entity schema
SELECT * FROM crm_describe('accounts', secret := 'crm_secret');

-- Query accounts with filter pushdown
SELECT name, emailaddress1, revenue
FROM crm_read('accounts', secret := 'crm_secret')
WHERE statecode = 0;

-- Query opportunities with expansion
SELECT * FROM crm_read('opportunities', secret := 'crm_secret', expand := 'customerid_account')
WHERE estimatedclosedate >= '2024-01-01';
```

## Implementation Strategy

### Shared Components with Business Central (#5)

| Component | Reuse Strategy |
|-----------|----------------|
| Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2 | Create shared `MicrosoftEntraAuthProvider` class |
| Token refresh logic | Shared token storage and refresh mechanism |
| OData v4 query building | Existing `odata_client` infrastructure |
| Predicate pushdown | Existing `odata_predicate_pushdown_helper` |

### CRM-Specific Components

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| URL builder | CRM-specific URL patterns (`{org}.crm.dynamics.com/api/data/v9.x/`) |
| Entity discovery | Query `EntityDefinitions` metadata endpoint |
| Secret type | `TYPE dataverse` with `ENVIRONMENT_URL` parameter |

## Out of Scope

- Write operations (POST, PATCH, DELETE)
- FetchXML query support
- On-premises deployments

## References

- [Dataverse Web API Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/overview)
- [Use OAuth authentication with Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/authenticate-oauth)
- [Dataverse Entity Reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/entitytypes)

items.title: Lakehouse Catalog §11b join fails: gold_transactions column names don't match gold_pacs002 convention
items.body:
## Problem

The §11b cross-table join in `JupyterHub/notebooks/Lakehouse_Catalog.ipynb` references column names that do not exist on `gold_transactions`. The query assumes the snake_case / `tx_*` convention used by `gold_pacs002` and `gold_pacs008` (whose ETLs rename raw fields), but `TransactionsETL` writes gold with the raw, un-renamed names.

Concretely, on `gold_transactions` the columns are `endtoendid`, `tenantid`, `txsts`, `txtp`, `amt`, `ccy`, `msgid` — see [`automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/TransactionsETL.py` lines 167-186](https://github.com/tazama-lf/biar/blob/main/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/TransactionsETL.py#L167-L186). The §11b query uses `end_to_end_id`, `tenant_id`, `tx_status`, `tx_type`, `tx_amount`, `tx_ccy` in both the `SELECT` list and the `INNER JOIN … ON` predicate against alias `t` (transactions).

This is a notebook-only bug. Every other notebook that reads `gold/transactions` (Executive_Overview, TMS_Performance, Fraud_Typology_Effectiveness, Case_Management_Trend, Anomaly_Detection_And_Rule_Calibration) applies a `_transaction_col` / `normalize_transactions_for_*` helper right after load that aliases the raw names to the underscored / `tx_`-prefixed forms, so their downstream code resolves correctly. Lakehouse Catalog registers temp views straight from `load_tenant_hudi` with no normalization step.

## Logs

```
AnalysisException: [UNRESOLVED_COLUMN.WITH_SUGGESTION] A column or function parameter with name `t`.`end_to_end_id` cannot be resolved. Did you mean one of the following? [`p`.`end_to_end_id`, `t`.`endtoendid`, `p`.`orgnl_end_to_end_id`, `p`.`instd_mmb_id`, `p`.`instg_mmb_id`].; line 30 pos 36;
'GlobalLimit 20
+- 'LocalLimit 20
   +- 'Sort ['t.event_ts DESC NULLS LAST], true
      +- 'Project ['t.transaction_id, 't.end_to_end_id, 't.tenant_id, 't.tx_type, 't.tx_amount, 't.tx_ccy, 't.tx_status, 't.event_ts, 'p.dc_cdtr_acct_id AS cdtr_account_id, 'p.dc_cdtr_id AS cdtr_party_id, 'cdtr_acct.account_id AS cdtr_acct_confirmed, 'p.dc_dbtr_acct_id AS dbtr_account_id, 'p.dc_dbtr_id AS dbtr_party_id, 'dbtr_acct.account_id AS dbtr_acct_confirmed, 'p.dc_instd_amt AS dc_amount, 'p.dc_instd_ccy AS dc_ccy]
         +- 'Join LeftOuter, (('dbtr_acct.account_id = 'p.dc_dbtr_acct_id) AND ('dbtr_acct.tenant_id = 't.tenant_id))
            :- 'Join LeftOuter, (('cdtr_acct.account_id = 'p.dc_cdtr_acct_id) AND ('cdtr_acct.tenant_id = 't.tenant_id))
            :  :- 'Join Inner, ((orgnl_end_to_end_id = 't.end_to_end_id) AND (tx_tenant_id = 't.tenant_id))
```

The plan tree confirms the on-disk schema: `gold_transactions` exposes `endtoendid`, `tenantid`, `txsts`, `txtp`, `amt`, `ccy`; `gold_pacs002` exposes `end_to_end_id`, `orgnl_end_to_end_id`, `tenant_id`, `tx_status`, `tx_type`, `tx_amount`, `tx_ccy`.

## Proposed solution

Fix the §11b cell in [`JupyterHub/notebooks/Lakehouse_Catalog.ipynb`](https://github.com/tazama-lf/biar/blob/main/JupyterHub/notebooks/Lakehouse_Catalog.ipynb) by aliasing the raw transactions columns in the `SELECT` list and using the raw names in the join predicate:

- `SELECT` list — replace `t.end_to_end_id`, `t.tenant_id`, `t.tx_type`, `t.tx_amount`, `t.tx_ccy`, `t.tx_status` with `t.endtoendid AS end_to_end_id`, `t.tenantid AS tenant_id`, `t.txtp AS tx_type`, `t.amt AS tx_amount`, `t.ccy AS tx_ccy`, `t.txsts AS tx_status`.
- Join predicate — change `p.orgnl_end_to_end_id = t.end_to_end_id AND p.tx_tenant_id = t.tenant_id` to `p.orgnl_end_to_end_id = t.endtoendid AND p.tx_tenant_id = t.tenantid`.
- Downstream `LEFT JOIN gold_account` predicates that reference `t.tenant_id` become `t.tenantid`.

Scope is one cell. No ETL, table, or other notebook changes.

## Impact

- §11b of Lakehouse Catalog raises `AnalysisException` and cannot be run.
- No other notebooks affected (audit confirmed the 8 other consumers of `gold/transactions` normalize column names on load).

## Follow-up (out of scope for this issue)

The root inconsistency — `gold_transactions` using different column naming than `gold_pacs002`/`gold_pacs008` — should eventually be fixed in `TransactionsETL.py` so the per-notebook normalize helpers can be removed. Tracked separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Lakehouse Catalog §11b executes without `AnalysisException` and returns rows joining transactions → pacs002 → account.
- [ ] No changes outside `JupyterHub/notebooks/Lakehouse_Catalog.ipynb`.

items.title: SmartDB一般化：Data Operations・Data Rule・Derived Datasetの多Provider契約を整理する
items.body:
Parent: #2619。SmartDBをDB技術に固定せず、**論理的なデータ操作とProvider固有の実現を分離**する。名称は仮称であり、既存Core APIや既存Issue名を一括改名する決定ではない。

## 目的と用語候補
- `Data Operations`：Data Model＋Function Data Context上のデータ取得、Relation Traversal、導出・集約、変換、更新Intentを利用する標準機能群。
- `Data Provider`：RDB／X-TEA SmartDB由来実現、OData、REST、GraphQL、File、Graph、in-memory等のPlugin/Adapter。新しい中央DB/Hostを作らない。
- `Data Rule`／`Model Rule`：旧テーブルスクリプトの一般化。純粋導出、検証、Lifecycle/副作用規則を分離し、Data側共通定義とFunction局所定義を合成する。
- `Derived Dataset`／`Derived Attribute`：従来のDB VIEW／仮想テーブル・仮想項目に相当する型付き結果。RDB以外でも定義でき、粒度、Identity、出所、完全性、時点、書戻し可能性を保持する。

## 機能契約
1. Data ModelはRelation/Identity/Key/Cardinality等を定義し、Function Data Contextは利用するRelation path/Field/粒度/範囲を**明示Mapping**する。Relationが存在するだけで自動取得対象を拡大しない。Studioで補完して解決済みMappingを保存。
2. SQLを手書きせずRelationをたどる通常の取得・集約を標準Operatorで表現。Provider側へのPushdown、Batch、Query最適化は意味的同等性（NULL、順序、重複、粒度、集合完全性、権限）を検査。特殊なSQL/native assetは明示Bindingとして保持。
3. 孫レコードを集約文字列にする等、3層→2層のProjectionをDerived Datasetに利用できる。編集時は既存#2500でViewChange→型付きIntent候補、#2597でDirty/保存単位、#1129でData Ruleの書込みLifecycleを担当。非可逆集約から元データを勝手に復元しない。
4. Providerの能力を対象サービス/操作/環境の粒度で判別：read/expand/filter/aggregate、Field PATCH vs full Replace、Collection diff、Relation操作、batch/atomicity、Version/ETag、idempotency/Receipt、障害後のpartial/unknown。ODataのbatch実行を無条件の原子性とみなさない。
5. 複数Providerを一つのContextで扱えても、関係のIdentityとBindingは明示。横断更新のAction・Commit/Resultは外部Host/Providerの保証へ委譲。新しい共通分散Tx Engineは先行しない。
6. 機能からProviderまでのトレース（Semantic Subject→Context→Relation/Rule→Intent→Binding→生成コード・実呼出）をCUI/Studioへ投影する。

## 代表Pressure（すべて未実施）
| ID | 正例 | 誤成功として検出 |
|---|---|---|
| DO-01 | 3層を明示Mappingして2層サマリー | 暗黙全件取得、JOIN fanout、partialを全件扱い |
| DO-02 | Data RuleとContext Ruleを合成 | 同一Fieldへの競合、循環、未取得/NULLの混同 |
| DO-03 | Derived Datasetを表とCLIに投影 | 集約行をEntityと同じIdentity扱い |
| DO-04 | 単一Providerで限定PATCH→独立Read | Hidden列の消去、RowIndexを主キー扱い |
| DO-05 | 同じ意味IntentをODataへBinding | 全置換の誤PATCH、batch＝atomicという推測 |
| DO-06 | 複数Provider/通信断 | 部分確定を全成功扱い、無確認の再試行 |
| DO-07 | DB側集約とアプリ側集約の同値比較 | NULL・Unit・Sort・粒度・Measure Lawの不一致 |
| DO-08 | Native SQL特殊処理を明示接続 | 既存SQLの正本性・権限・出典の喪失 |

## 受入案
- [ ] 旧SmartDBの責務を既存Data/Rule/Action/Provider/Pluginに割り付け、過不足と新Core APIの必要性を比較票に残す。
- [ ] 3層→2層のDerived構造をHeadlessで取得・表示し、元データのIdentity・Lineage・完全性を説明。
- [ ] Read-only集計と限定的な更新候補、更新Actionが必要な非一意編集を分類。
- [ ] 少なくともRDB系とAPI系の2 Providerで同じ意味定義をConformance評価し、実行できた範囲を分離。
- [ ] Provider能力不足時にsilent fallback/権限拡大/偽atomicityなし。実Providerの更新・Receipt/独立観測は別資格。
- [ ] SQL手書き方式と比較し、定義量、変更影響、トレース容易性、再利用できたOperator数を測定。

**既存Owner**：#1126/#1127/#2506/#1706/#2593/#988、#1129/#1637、#2500（11/2 RT-01〜10）/#2597/#2598、#951/#1223/#1174/#2390/#1656。Runtime/Tx/Plugin Resolver/Authorityの第二実装を作らない。

<!-- 20261102-dataops-action-offer-separation -->
## 2026-11-02 接続追補：Data OperationsとContext-aware Action Offerの区別（設計・未実行）

[#2616 §§6–7](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/blob/docs/semantic-context-action-affordance-20261102/plan/design/SEMANTIC_CONTEXT_ACTION_AFFORDANCE_2026-11.md)の横断計画を受け、Data Operationsが提供するRead/Traverse/Derive/Validate/Write Portと、#2507が提供するActionの意味的な適用判定、#997が提供するUI配置を**別の責務**として扱う。Data Provider Capabilityが存在するだけで、Business Actionが受理済みとは判定しない。CRUD等の候補が機械導出できても、業務Action identity、許されるEffect、更新対象母集団とcommit保証は別途照合する。

初期Pressure：Entity単件PATCHは部分取得でも候補になり得る／Collection全件Replaceは完全性と対象確定が必要／Documentは版付き明示差分／Event streamはappend-onlyを尊重／専門SimulationはCompute ActionでありDB更新とは限らない。UI固有RuleとProviderの暗黙Writeを作らず、Rule Definition/Attachment→Execution phaseは#1129、ViewChange/Dirty/Requestは#2500/#2597/#2598、現在Grant/Effectは#1174へ渡す。

同一Data Operations定義が二つ以上の異質Consumerと二Providerで意味を保持するか、欠落条件/unsupportedを説明できるか測る。正式API/DSL/Source Meaning採用、RDB・API実接続・Go/DBテスト・Owner受理はNOT RUN。

<!-- 20261102-three-footprint-provider-evidence -->
## 2026-11-02 Provider適合の追補：Declared Read / Actual Read / Disclosed Output

[Draft #2616 §8](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/blob/docs/semantic-context-action-affordance-20261102/plan/design/SEMANTIC_CONTEXT_ACTION_AFFORDANCE_2026-11.md)の三境界を、本Issueの多Provider受入へ接続する。

- **Declared/Required**：#2506/#2624のFunction別明示Mappingと、#2507のAction適用条件に必要なRead集合。Relationが存在するだけで暗黙取得しない。Providerへの要求scope=allと実取得completeは独立。
- **Actual Acquisition**：RDB/APIで実発行されたQuery/Request、Field/Relation、Source alias・principal/RLS・取得時点・Provider版、実効read scope/Snapshotを検査。出力から秘密Fieldを削っただけで「Providerで未取得」と報告しない。実Providerの物理取得を#2624の合成JSON同値試験のPASSへ帰属させない。
- **Disclosed Output**：#2516/#1178のConsumerに渡るValue/Action候補/件数/diagnosticを独立に確認する。Error/Timing/Log/LLM送信の実境界は#2515等へ委譲し、有限Output試験の一般非干渉を主張しない。
- **Capabilityの差**：Provider Aに限定Field PATCHがあり、Provider BはFull Replaceのみの場合、安全な自動read-modify-writeは前提にしない。隠れたField・不足したImage・Version Fence・Owner権限・partial/unknownのいずれかが未確認ならunsupported/unresolvedとして根拠を返す。複数DB Aliasの曖昧性は#2611、Candidate→Requestの実Targetは#2598へ。

本件の追加受入圧力は、同一Context/Meaningに対して**論理上の明示取得、実Providerの物理Read、Consumer開示がそれぞれ証拠で説明できるか**、および二ProviderのPATCH/Replace差を失敗を含め分類できるか。既存#2622 DO-04〜06/#2616 I2〜I5へ接続し、新Provider/Policy Engine/標準APIを先行導入しない。実Query/API/DB・Host・Owner意味受理はNOT RUN。

<!-- 20261105-db-realization-doma-two-way-sql-minimal-contract -->
## 2026-11-05 DB Provider／Dialect差の最小適合契約（Doma・Spring等の先行方式を比較）

**位置づけ：既存Data Operations/Provider契約を具体化する設計・受入案。新しい標準DSL文法／SQL Engine／DB Registryの採択ではない。** 他チャットのDB追加・2waySQL議論と#1121 Lowering、#951 Capability、#2598の実対象境界を照合。標準化するのは**Query/Mutationの論理意味・結果資格**であり、SQL文面・トランザクション挙動を万能共通化しない。

### 最小の4責務（現在の機構へ割付ける前の比較票）

| 責務 | 明示したい情報・負例 | 対応Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Logical Data Operation** | Relation path/業務Key/Grain/NULL/欠損/完全性/Scope/Current Predicate、作用Intentと独立Expected。同じ意味IDのDB移行でもMeaningを自動改版しない | #2622/#2506/#1126 |
| **Data Source Binding／Dialect Realization** | 対象Data/表から辿れる**実Data Source alias・実DB kind/dialect・能力版**をProviderが返す。表名文字列からDB名を推測せず、AliasとDB種別を混ぜない。Query/Mutation PlanをProvider固有SQL/APIへ実現 | #951/#1121/#2611 |
| **Execution/Transaction/Value Codec** | パラメータBinding、型/金額精度/日時/NULL、Read Snapshot、affected row/更新競合、Commit/rollback/unknown、Provider error分類。Dialectの名前が同じでも実機能/版/Connectionを検証 | #1174/#1769、既存Provider |
| **Native SQL asset／optional template** | 特殊処理のみOriginal SQL/方言版・選択根拠・Source digest・Bound Parameters・要求能力/結果Grainを保持。手書きSQLを必ずTEI式へ変換しない | #2622/#2595/#2600 |

**Domaで確認できる先行方式**：共通`query.sql`に対し`query-postgres.sql`等のDB別ファイルを優先する命名規約と、SQLツールで直接読めるコメントベースのtwo-way SQL。公式資料：https://docs.domaframework.org/en/3.13.0/sql/ 。TEIではこの**薄い選択規則だけを任意のNative SQL実現へ転用する候補**とし、全SQLをDAO/2waySQLへ強制しない。Spring JDBCの`NamedParameterJdbcTemplate`・`SQLExceptionTranslator`はParam BindingとError分類の分離の参考（https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/data-access/jdbc/choose-style.html、https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/data-access/jdbc/core.html）。各FrameworkのそのままのAPIをTEI Coreへ持ち込まない。

### 方言の選択と安全なfallback

1. まず既存のFunction Data Contextで**対象Data/Relation/表→Provider/Data Source alias**を確定し、その実Providerの`databaseKind/dialect`相当を参照する。標準の汎用Source/Provider能力で十分なら、新DB名取得専用インターフェースを設けない。複数Source越境・Federated joinのどちらのDBで実行するか曖昧なら**unsupported/explicit choice**。
2. **明示的なAsset Binding ＞ 対象DBに一致する方言Asset ＞ 共通Asset**を比較する。ただし優先順位そのものを正式仕様とするのはP0試験後。共通Assetは当該Providerでの**意味・Parameter・Capability適合が確認された場合だけ**fallbackを許す。DB変更で選択Assetが替わってもMeaning/Targetを無断変更しない。
3. 未対応SQL構文・型Codec・RLS/行認可・Pagination・更新Version/CAS/RETURNING/Batch Atomicity・Isolationに差があれば、失敗を黙って別SQLやクライアント全件Read→Writeへ切り替えず、`unsupported`／明示されたAlternativeを返す。Native SQLでもProvider current Grant、Transaction・Receiptを迂回しない。
4. 2waySQLは**別Plugin能力候補**。テンプレートの人間可読SQLと、実行時にBound Parameterへ変換したSQLの両方を検証する。生Identifier/Order句の埋込みは宣言済み許容集合に限定。任意文字列の結合・旧コメントをそのまま信用するSQL Injection経路を作らない。

### RDB-01〜08（Reference→実2DBの順）

| ID | 反例／入力 | 独立Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **RDB-01 Alias vs kind** | `billing`と`audit`別AliasがともにPostgreSQL、別の`report`はSQLite | NameとDialectを別に解決。正しい対象DBからSQLを選び、文字列Table名やCaller選択で混同しない |
| **RDB-02 Native priority** | 共通`find.sql`、`find-postgres.sql`、明示Binding、DB未対応 | 選択したAssetとSource hash/理由/実Readerを追跡。未知DB・曖昧ならsilent fallbackしない |
| **RDB-03 Same meaning two SQLs** | PostgreSQL/SQLiteで同じQuery：NULL/欠損、重複JOIN、ORDER、ページ分割、数字精度 | 同じ業務Expected。差が説明不能なら非互換・部分取得を明示 |
| **RDB-04 Mutation/Tx差** | PostgreSQLは限定PATCH、別Providerは全件Replaceのみ。部分Fieldと失効Grantあり | 目に見える値が一致しても安全な更新とは扱わず、現Grant/Target/CAS/Receiptを実Providerへ委譲 |
| **RDB-05 2way SQL** | コメント変数、条件付きSQL、型・Named binding、不正literal／identifier | SQLツール直接実行版と実際のBound SQLを区別し、意図しないLiteral展開やInjectionを拒否 |
| **RDB-06 Update error** | 同一制約違反・deadlock/timeout/ACK lossでDB別Errorが異なる | Business Refusal／再試行可能技術失敗／Commit Uncertainを混同しない。新OperationID盲再送禁止 |
| **RDB-07 Cross-source** | 同Functionが2 DBのTable/Graph/APIに依存、SQL join不能 | 実行可能なSource/Processing境界・Snapshotの相違を報告し、暗黙atomic cross-DB処理にしない |
| **RDB-08 Build/Source drift** | Asset選択と実行SQLが異なる、Source D1→D2→D1、Dialect実装版変更 | Model/Asset/Realizer/実SQL byte/実DB接続とResult資格を別々に再確認。Source hashだけでProducerの同一性を推定しない |

**導入順**：P0は上のRDB-01/02/05をread-only合成Asset/既存Resolverで反証し、既存インターフェースで足りない点だけを列挙。P1で`RDB-03`を実PostgreSQL＋第二RDB（初期候補SQLite）で**同じ業務Expected**へ接続。P2で更新/Grant/Provider Tx、P3で2waySQL・DB追加コスト・定義量・実SQL Source trace・性能を比較する。開始前に現mainの実DB機構と別担当PRを再照合し、専用Native SQL RegistryやDialect Engineを増やさない。**今回実施したのは公式資料・現Issueの設計照合と受入票の追補のみ。DB二系統の実Read/Write、SQL選択器、Template/Provider E2E、Owner意味受理はNOT RUN。**

<!-- 20261105-db-provider-existing-pg-evidence-reuse -->
### 2026-11-05 既存実PostgreSQL証拠を基線にし、2DB比較の重複実装を避ける

新たにmain統合済みの[#2853](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/pull/2853)（製品Command Invoker→実PostgreSQL CAS／模擬ACK lossとReceipt Lookup）、[#2854](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/pull/2854)（同Idempotency key replayと新key＋ABAの違い：新keyでAPPLIEDになる反例）、[#2857](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/pull/2857)（暫定D8〜D11の一改訂Web/実PG・独立Read、ただし**INCOMPLETE/productGate UNQUALIFIED**）、[#2859](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/pull/2859)（Runner系にも実起動前Schema gate）を照合。

これは**PostgreSQL側の局所的な参照経路の存在**を示すが、#2622の二DB/Dialect Conformance・Native SQL Asset選択・2waySQLの直接実行性・Provider差の安全なFallbackについてのE2Eではない。新しいPostgreSQL Runner/Host/Receipt APIを本Issueへコピーせず、**RDB-03/04/06は既存実PGケースのSource/Expected/制限を再利用し第二DBの差分だけを検証**する。ただし#2854で明示されたABA再適用は「防止済み」ではなく不足として引き継ぐ。

次の受入票では`logicalOperationId, dataSourceAlias, databaseKind, providerVersion, nativeAssetDigest, executedSQLDigest, boundParameterShape, expectedRowset/Scope, currentGrant, effectiveTransaction, Receipt/independentRead`を**観測できた欄だけ**残し、未観測を`unknown`とする。これらは計測項目候補であって新Runtime Schemaではない。Runtime暗黙のMetadataだけからBusinessTableのDBを確定したとは主張しない。実PostgreSQL evidenceの達成をRDB-01〜08のテストPASSへ自動転記しない。

**最小次試験**は、同一業務Function Query/独立Expectedに対して`postgres`と第二RDBのNative／共通SQL選択、NULL/ORDER/型/Scope/Resultの違いを確かめるread-only比較。書込/一括操作・認可/Txの差は#1174、Web Gateは#1119/#1163へ維持。実第二DB、方言Asset選択器、2waySQL Template、Role Migration、Owner受理は**本追補で未実施**。

<!-- 20261105-domain-first-provider-portability-experience -->
## 2026-11-05 低コード利用者のDB非依存体験を、Provider適合と切替時の説明責務へ落とす（設計・未実行）

**横断の優先条件**：通常のTEI利用者には`DB kind／Dialect／SQL file／Provider Version`を選ばせず、**業務上のデータ・Relation・取得条件・保存操作**を選ぶだけで使えることを先に検収する。内部のDB Realization差は無くさないが、普段のUI/DSLに技術的な選択ノイズを出さない。前段の[#2862](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/pull/2862)はQuery候補のSelectionと2waySQLの**詳細設計Owner**、[#2611](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/issues/2611)は複数DB Alias/Mappingの曖昧さ、[#1124](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/issues/1124)はStudioの投影/編集。#2622は**業務Functionの可搬性と通常利用の自然さの合格条件のみ**を受け持ち、第二UIやSQL選択器を作らない。

### 利用者側に見せる状態（内部の適合分類から導出する提案）

| 内部の適合評価（正式enumではない） | 通常利用者への提示 | Advanced/運用者への根拠 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Native** | 通常どおり実行可能（必要なCurrent Grant等は別） | 当該Providerの既存Realization/Asset/実能力が確認された範囲 |
| **Equivalent** | 同じ業務結果が確認できた範囲で利用可能 | 別Realization/Providerによる独立Expected・NULL/精度/粒度/Scope・失敗特性の差分 |
| **Unsupported** | 「この接続先では、この操作に対応していません」 | 必要な能力、欠けた型/更新/Tx/Query機能、影響するFunctionと代替の有無 |
| **Unknown** | 「この操作を実行できるか確認が必要です」 | Source/Mapping/候補/実Read/Conformance/Current Grantのどこが未観測・stale・partialか |

上二つも**現在の実行認可・Business Meaning Acceptedの自動付与ではない**。書込みについて`Equivalent`と判定するには、結果値の一致だけではなく対象集合/冪等性/障害時Commit Unknown/Receiptの作用契約も必要。Native SQLが無く共通SQLが存在するだけなら`Unknown`であり、実行できると断定しない。技術詳細は権限と用途に応じて任意表示とし、DB Alias/DSN/非公開SQL/隠し件数を一般利用者へ露出しない。

### LUX-01〜07：通常利用からDB変更までのIndependent Expected

| ID | 操作・変化 | 合格条件（正式UI実装ではなく受入案） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **LUX-01 業務中心の日常操作** | 一つの受注一覧／明細取得／保存を定義して実行 | 通常フローにDB製品・Dialect・SQL Asset選択の必須入力が0。意味Mapping/現認可に基づく実結果を確認 |
| **LUX-02 接続先を移す** | 業務FunctionとExpected固定、PostgreSQL→第二DB | 意味受理は維持しつつ技術能力・実Provider/結果を**差分判定**。必要な場合だけ制約・対応不可をFunction名で説明 |
| **LUX-03 方言固有SQL** | 一部FunctionだけNative SQL依存、他は標準Query | 影響があるFunctionだけ`Unknown/Unsupported`。全システムを一律非対応にせず、SQL本文の編集を通常利用者へ要求しない |
| **LUX-04 曖昧な実対象** | 同Semantic Dataへ2 DB Alias、read replicaとwrite primary | 推測で保存先を選ばず、業務操作に必要な選択/設定不足を明示。DB構成を知らない人にSQL選択を要求しない |
| **LUX-05 見かけ上の結果同値** | 同じ表示RowsでもNULL/decimal/集計粒度/欠落・partial、更新CASが異なる | 値一致だけで`Equivalent`にしない。必要Expected/実Reader Scope/Tx/Receiptを別観測 |
| **LUX-06 Source・Role・Asset失効** | 共通SQLから方言SQLへ変更、Role版更新、Source A→B→A／古いPreview | 旧Query/Actionの現在資格を再評価。古いPreviewは歴史的記録として保持し、新実行資格へ無音昇格しない |
| **LUX-07 説明と秘匿** | 一般利用者／運用者／開発者へ同じ不適合を提示 | 業務的な対処は明瞭、Source/DB Alias/SQL全文・秘密の候補/件数は許可対象だけ。低権限画面の情報漏えいを#2516で検証 |

**測定**：標準Queryでの手入力設定数（DB固有設定は通常0を目標）、通常操作完了までの手順・診断理解、別DBへ移行するときに影響を受けるFunction数・必要な追加SQL/Adapter数、実結果の不一致とUnsupported/Unknownの誤成功数、実行時の性能/Query数を#2018へ引き渡す。人的評価が難しい部分は、同じ固定Caseに対してAIによる独立レビューを複数回行っても**ユーザー受入の代替証拠ではない**ことを明示。

**実証順**：P0はLUX-01/04/07を既存[#2586](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/issues/2586)のHeadless Function→Contextと[#1124](https://github.com/hat47x/tei-platform/issues/1124)のGeneric Inspectでread-only比較。P1はLUX-02/03/05を実PostgreSQL＋第二DBの**同じ独立Expected**で比較。P2はLUX-06の移行Previewと再資格化を検証。#2862のDBX-01〜09、#2611 PM-01〜06、#2616 SQ-01〜04とFixtureを共有し、別のUI/Provider/Scenario Engineを作らない。**LUX-01〜07、正式UI、移行、二DB同一Function、業務Owner受理はNOT RUN**。

items.body:
## Description

> A brief summary to help everyone understand this feature.

Give the mortal per-server family the fold absorber the tenant family already has, so the invariant holds: **a mortal series must never be observable at a value lower than an earlier observation in the same billing window.**

Today, any operation that removes flow rows from a series label tuple while its older, higher samples are still in the ETL day window makes the exposed series regress, and the ETL's clamp discards real usage. Three shapes exist: partial fold on a multi-port server (proof-of-need Bug #226), same-window rebirth after a full ghost fold (port recreated on the same server — the tuple, not the MAC, is what matters), and attribution-change settles moving rows out of a tuple.

Mechanism: one carry accumulator per series label tuple `{server_id, tenant_id, zone, external_network, direction}`. Every fold that removes rows from a tuple credits its carry; the Collector emits `Σ live rows + carry` for the mortal family. One bucket, three behaviors:

- tuple still has live rows → credit applies at the next scrape; the series never dips;
- tuple fully dead → series ends as today; carry lies dormant as the rebirth seed until TTL = next ETL day boundary + margin;
- TTL expiry → carry dropped (bytes remain in tenant settled and in already-extracted billing days; dead servers accumulate no unbounded state).

## Definition of Done (DoD)

> A list of technical requirements must be met for completion.

- [ ] Every path that removes rows from a tuple credits the carry (ghost sweep `SettleEvict`, `settleAttributionChange`) through the single shared label-resolution choke point.
- [ ] Mortal family emits `Σ live rows + carry`; a partial fold never decreases a live series (closes #226).
- [ ] A same-tuple rebirth within TTL continues from the carried value; after TTL it is an ordinary birth (born-mid-window ETL rule applies).
- [ ] Tenant family byte-identical to today: settled untouched, no un-fold, bookkeeping one-directional.
- [ ] Carry persisted as an additive WAL schema section, snapshotted atomically with rows + settled (Contract 7 extended); older agents refuse the newer schema as today.
- [ ] Zero-allocation `Collect()` preserved; bench gate passes.
- [ ] Docs: Contract 7 + the per-server export chapter updated; CLAUDE.md mirror refreshed.
- [ ] Scenario regressions under #166: #231 `multi-port-partial-delete`, #232 `port-recreate-same-server`, #233 `interface-detach-reattach`.

## Technical Notes

> A section for tech leads to document technical risks and/or any concerns regarding the DoD.

- **Feature Owner:** arasHi87
- **Backend:** carry join must live inside the existing settle/emit critical sections — the fold moving bytes rows→carry must never be observable half-done by `Collect()` or the WAL snapshot (over/under-bill on rebirth otherwise). TTL expiry needs a deterministic owner (sweep pass, not a timer per tuple).
- **Infra:** none.

## Output artifacts (Definition of Done)

> Beyond code, docs, and config changes, completing this issue must also deliver:

- [ ] **Handbook knowledge update** — update `kb/lachesis/architecture/billing-metric-families.md` (mortal-family lifecycle promise changes: partial folds no longer dip, same-window rebirth continues) via `/bigstack-core:save-to-handbook`.
