items.title: [Feature] Four-layer billing families — total → tenant → server → port, each immortal within its owner's lifetime

type.name: Feature
type.description: A distinct unit of functionality or a significant part that forms a specific user story.

items.body:
## Description

> A brief summary to help everyone understand this feature.

Restructure the billing metrics into a **four-layer family hierarchy**, each tier immortal *within its owner's lifetime*, each tier absorbing the deaths of the tier below:

| Layer | Family | Labels | Lifetime | Absorbs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| total | `lachesis_bytes_total` | `zone, external_network, direction` | immortal | everything (Σ tenants incl. `unknown`) |
| tenant | `lachesis_tenant_bytes_total` / `lachesis_tenant_packets_total` | + `tenant_id` | project lifetime (forever today; see the tenant-lifetime follow-up) | server & port deaths (tenant-settled) |
| server | `lachesis_server_bytes_total` | + `server_id` | **server lifetime** | port deaths/detaches (**server-settled**) |
| port | `lachesis_port_bytes_total` | + `port_id` | port binding | — (mortal leaf) |

The server tier gets the same absorber the tenant tier already has: `Settle` credits a **server-settled** accumulator (keyed by the full server tuple) in the same critical section as tenant-settled, and the family emits `Σ live rows + server-settled` — including settled-only tuples (a portless-but-alive server flat-lines, exactly like a stopped VM does today). Release is **on server death**: a bucket is dropped when its `server_id` is absent from the Nova server list the sync already fetches (for `lachesis_server_info`) — no TTL, no grace-window ambiguity; a failed Nova fetch holds buckets (safe direction).

**Consequences:**
- Partial fold on a multi-port server never dips the server series (fixes #226).
- Detach → reattach **same server**: the fold parks bytes in server-settled, the reattached port's fresh counter resumes on top — the server series *continues from the detach point* (#233 green, at billing granularity).
- Reattach to a **new server**: old server keeps its bytes (its settled bucket, until it dies), new server counts from 0 — **no double-billing**.
- Per-port visibility is the explicit mortal leaf (`lachesis_port_bytes_total`); a same-port reattach resets *that* series (documented — billing exactness lives one tier up).
- The naive consumption patterns become safe on the server family (its labels are unchanged from today), shrinking the cubecmp ETL contract change to "your feed got strictly more correct, plus an optional drill-down family".

**Naming:** `lachesis_bytes_total` is repurposed as the total layer (loses `tenant_id`). Safe because the product is not yet online — but dashboards, recording rules, the scenariotest harness, and the cubecmp#837 ETL draft repoint in the same change.

Design lineage: per-tuple carry (#227, closed — TTL/release ambiguity) → per-port-only first cut (PR #248 — left a same-port-reattach reset at billing granularity) → this synthesis (2026-07-22 design review): the carry mechanism with an unambiguous server-death release, framed as tier lifetimes. Reference implementations: branches `arashi.li/carry-bucket` (PR #245: absorber + WAL + sweep lifecycle, live-validated) and `arashi.li/per-port-series` (PR #248: port_id threading).

## Definition of Done (DoD)

- [x] Four families emitted per the table; tenant packets family renamed alongside bytes.
- [x] `Settle` credits tenant-settled and server-settled in one write-lock critical section; Collect and WAL snapshot all maps under ONE lock (Contract 7 extended); server-settled round-trips the WAL (additive schema bump).
- [x] Server-settled release keyed on Nova server-list absence (no TTL); Nova fetch failure holds; watermark gauge for bucket count.
- [x] Same-server reattach continues the server series; new-server reattach starts from 0 with no double-billing (both unit-tested).
- [x] Dashboards, recording rules, alerts, and the scenariotest harness repointed to the new family names.
- [x] Scenario regressions #231/#232/#233 assert the server family directly and pass live (dev-cmp + c36); #235 stays green.
- [x] Docs: metrics.md family table, billing.md tier model + consumption contract, data-structures.md server-settled section, contracts.md Contract 7.
- [x] Cardinality assessed (port family ≈ ports × zones × ext × dir) and bounded.

## Technical Notes

> A section for tech leads to document technical risks and/or any concerns regarding the DoD.

- **Feature Owner:** arasHi87
- **Frontend:** n/a
- **Backend:** two-thirds exists — `arashi.li/carry-bucket` has the absorber/WAL/lifecycle (swap TTL release → Nova-list prune, emit settled-only tuples), `arashi.li/per-port-series` has the port_id threading (re-point to the new leaf family). Harness gets simpler (direct server-family assertion).
- **Infra:** family renames are a consumer-facing change — pre-GA safe, but coordinate the cubecmp#837 ETL draft and update in-repo dashboards in the same PR.

## UI/UX Mockups (Optional)

None

## Output artifacts (Definition of Done)

- [x] **Handbook knowledge update** — rewrite `kb/lachesis/architecture/billing-metric-families.md` to the four-tier model (tier lifetimes, absorbers, consumption per tier, the same-port-reattach caveat on the port leaf) via `/bigstack-core:save-to-handbook`, recording the carry → per-port → synthesis design lineage. Landed in bigstack-oss/bigstack-handbook#117 (merged 2026-07-23); the carry → per-port → synthesis lineage is recorded in this ticket's description, which the entry cites via #247/PR 252.

items.title: [Spec] ateng-boot-search 企业级双引擎全文检索与流批分析基础设施
items.body: # Spec: ateng-boot-search 企业级双引擎全文检索与流批分析基础设施 ## Problem Statement 在企业级现代中后台与大数据应用体系中（如电商商品搜索、系统审计日志追踪、订单工单组合多维筛选、报表聚合、时序归档、地理位置服务与 AI 知识库向量检索），传统关系型数据库（RDBMS）在面对海量非结构化文本模糊匹配、动态组合条件筛选、空间地理计算以及高维聚合统计时存在严重的性能瓶颈与全表扫描隐患。搜索引擎（Elasticsearch / OpenSearch）作为专职检索分析基础设施已成为不可或缺的核心底座。 然而，在基于 Spring Boot 3 构建企业级检索能力时，开发者和架构师在生产环境中面临十大严峻痛点： 1. **官方 Elasticsearch 8.x Java API Client 深度嵌套与代码膨胀 (Lambda Hell & Builder Bloat)**： Elasticsearch 7.15+ 全面废弃了传统的 `RestHighLevelClient`，强推基于纯函数式 Builder 的新一代 `elasticsearch-java` 客户端。其语法充斥着极深的 Lambda 嵌套（如一个简单的多字段布尔查询往往需要嵌套 5 到 7 层闭包 `s -> s.query(q -> q.bool(b -> b.must(...)))`），常规 CRUD 与高频检索充斥着臃肿的样板代码，开发心智负担沉重； 2. **Elasticsearch 8.x 与 OpenSearch 协议与依赖分道扬镳 (Ecosystem Divergence & Dual-Engine Dilemma)**： 自 Elastic 协议变更后，AWS 主导的 OpenSearch 与 Elasticsearch 8.x 在依赖坐标、包命名空间、线缆握手 Header 强校验（ES 8 官方 Client 严格检测服务端是否为 Elastic 官方版本并阻断与 OpenSearch 通信）上完全割裂。传统业务要么绑定 ES 无法支持信创，要么强行引入两套重型 SDK 造成 Classpath 冲突与依赖膨胀； 3. **序列化脱节导致雪花 ID 精度丢失与时间格式崩溃 (Serialization Rift & Snowflake Bug)**： 官方 Client 默认内建隔离的 `ObjectMapper`，脱离了应用全局 Jackson 定制规则，导致 Long 型分布式雪花主键（Snowflake）在输出到前端或解析时由于 JavaScript 53 位精度限制发生尾数精度截断；同时 `LocalDateTime` 无法遵循 `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` 规范解析，极易造成序列化崩溃； 4. **全量覆盖覆写开销与并发竞态丢失 (Missing Partial Update & Concurrency Race)**： 业务更新频繁只涉及一两个状态字段（如订单状态变更为 `PAID`）。若仅支持全量 `index` 覆写，不仅需要先查后改浪费网络 I/O，还极易在并发场景下覆盖其他并发线程修改的属性，且缺乏轻量级的乐观并发控制（OCC：`_seq_no` / `_primary_term`）； 5. **批量写入局部失败静默丢失风险 (Partial Failure & Silent Data Loss)**： ES 的 `_bulk` 批量写入不具备跨文档关系数据库事务的原子回滚语义。一次提交 1000 条文档可能其中 5 条因 Mapping 格式冲突或版本冲突失败，而其余 995 条成功。很多二次封装框架直接以 HTTP 200 判定成功，静默吞咽了 `BulkResponse.errors()` 中的失败明细，导致严重的数据丢失或同步不一致； 6. **高频流式写入缺乏反压缓冲导致停机丢数据 (Missing Managed BulkProcessor & Shutdown Hazard)**： 在对接 Canal Binlog、Kafka 消息队列或日志流水同步时，单条同步写入吞吐极低；手写外部缓冲队列容易缺乏反压保护造成内存溢出，且应用发版重启时残留在内存中的消息直接丢失； 7. **深度分页导致协调节点内存暴涨与集群雪崩 (Deep Paging OOM & Cluster Meltdown)**： 当业务列表进行翻页查询时，开发者常沿用传统 SQL 的 `from + size` 逻辑。一旦查询越过 `index.max_result_window`（默认 10,000 条），ES 集群需要将全部前置分片数据加载至协调节点进行全量内存堆排序，引发严重的 GC 停顿与 OOM 崩溃；而官方弃用的 Scroll API 又会在服务端残留未释放快照上下文句柄； 8. **分片路由（Routing）全生命周期缺失引发性能劣化与空指针异常 (Routing Blindspot)**： 在大规模分片索引中，未按商户/用户绑定路由键会导致所有查询演变为昂贵的全分片广播；更严重的是，在启用了强制路由的索引上，若 `getById` 或 `deleteById` 漏传 `routing`，底层驱动将直接报错或无法命中； 9. **高亮切片提取繁琐与数据安全性割裂 (Highlight Snippet Decoupling & In-Memory Purity)**： ES 高亮返回的 HTML 文本（如 `关键词`）独立存在于 Hit 的 `highlight` 字典中，与 `_source` 业务实体脱节。业务层常常需要编写大量反射与正则胶水代码将高亮文本替换回实体；甚至直接将带 HTML 标签的数据写回持久层，彻底破坏了 ADR-0012 确立的“内存真明文”与传输隔离不变量； 10. **生产索引缺乏零停机平滑运维能力与离线单测断层 (Missing Atomic Alias Swap & Non-Hermetic Testing)**： 企业生产变更分词器与 Mapping 时，若缺乏原生的原子别名切换（Atomic Alias Swap）门面，容易导致切换期间产生无索引空窗期；同时，单测强依赖外部真实集群或 Docker Testcontainers，导致本地与离线 CI 矩阵频繁阻断。 ## Solution 遵循 `ateng-boot` 纯原生、零臃肿依赖、显式契约、四维上下文透传与 100% 离线自洽单测铁律，打造工业级双引擎全文检索与流批分析基础设施 `ateng-boot-search` 及配套 1:1 场景样例工程 `ateng-boot-samples/ateng-boot-sample-search`： 1. **官方原生基线与双驱解耦 SPI 架构**：以 Spring Boot 3.3.13 BOM 原生纳管的 `co.elastic.clients:elasticsearch-java 8.13.4` 为第一优先默认驱动，底层抽象 `SearchEngineClient` SPI 支持 OpenSearch 驱动可选接入；同时保留官方底层 Client 逃生舱（`execute` 与 `nativeQuery`），杜绝平庸包装折损原生高阶特性； 2. **Core 受管 Jackson 序列化注入桥接**：强制将应用受管的 `ObjectMapper` 注入 ES 驱动的 `JacksonJsonpMapper`，彻底保障雪花 ID 输出 String 防前端精度截断，并规范 `LocalDateTime` 遵循 `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`； 3. **数据面与结构面清晰隔离的双门面体系**： - 数据面 `SearchTemplate`：专注文档 CRUD、局部更新（Partial Update / Upsert）、OCC 乐观并发控制、批量写入、多字段高亮、Search-After 深度分页、空间计算与 AI 向量检索； - 结构面 `SearchIndexOperations`（通过 `searchTemplate.indices()` 暴露）：收敛索引存在性检查、创建、删除、Mapping 维护、时序索引模板，以及生产级无感知零空窗期的原子别名热切换（`swapAlias`）； 4. **双模批量写入治理**：提供严格模式 `indexBatch`（任一文档失败即抛出 `SearchBulkException` 附带失败快照）与宽容模式 `indexBatchLenient`（返回包含成功数与失败明细列表的 `SearchBulkResult`）； 5. **受管流式批量写入器 (`SearchBulkProcessor`)**：多维阈值自适应触发异步刷盘（条数阈值 `1000` / 时间窗口 `1s` / 内存容量 `5MB` 强类型 `DataSize`），挂载 Core 受管线程池并实现 Spring `SmartLifecycle`，确保优雅停机绝对排空队列零丢数据； 6. **双轨自适应分页与万级刚性熔断**：浅分页无缝对接 Core 模块 `PageQuery` 与 `PageResult>` 传输契约；深度分页提供专职 `searchAfter` 游标接口；浅分页越过 10,000 条阈值时自动 Fail-Fast 抛出 `SearchPaginationExceededException` 阻断集群 OOM； 7. **分片路由全生命周期闭环**：实体字段标配 `@SearchRouting` 自动反射提取；主键查询/删除防漏校验；`SearchQueryBuilder` 链式注入 `routing` 优化单分片命中； 8. **动态时序索引与索引模板**：`@SearchIndex` 原生支持 SpEL 表达式与动态时间后缀解析（如 `log_#{...}`），配合 `putIndexTemplate` 实现日志与时序数据全自动滚动分表； 9. **轻量流式查询构建器 (`SearchQueryBuilder`)**：收敛 10+ 核心算子（Term, Match, Range, Wildcard, Bool），推行 filter 缓存优先；开箱支持 `geoDistance` 空间筛选/排序与 `knn` dense_vector AI 向量检索； 10. **数据安全高亮契约**：统一返回强类型 `SearchHit` 载荷；支持在出参 VO 字段标注 `@HighlightField` 自动回填富文本，坚决杜绝污染业务核心实体或数据库； 11. **四维上下文透传与多租户逻辑安全网**：出站请求自动注入 MDC `X-Trace-Id` 标头；开启多租户时外层查询自动隐式注入 `term(tenant_id, tenantId)` 且写入自动补齐； 12. **云原生健康度量与 100% 离线自洽测试**：装配 `SearchHealthIndicator`（GREEN/YELLOW/RED 带 2 秒超时熔断）与 Micrometer P99 耗时指标；自研纯内存 `MockWebServer` + `InMemorySearchEngine` 双层离线沙箱，零 Docker 依赖秒级全绿。 ## User Stories 1. As an application developer, I want a unified and intuitive `SearchTemplate` facade, so that I can perform document indexing, retrieval, updates, and searches without writing deeply nested Lambda builders. 2. As a backend developer, I want Long-typed distributed Snowflake IDs to be automatically serialized as Strings in Elasticsearch documents, so that frontend JavaScript applications do not suffer from 53-bit precision truncation. 3. As an engineer, I want `LocalDateTime` and `LocalDate` fields to adhere to standard `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` formatting out of the box, so that temporal data is cleanly serialized and deserialized without runtime exceptions. 4. As a high-concurrency business engineer, I want to execute partial updates with `update(index, id, partialDoc, docAsUpsert)`, so that I only mutate modified fields without full-document read-modify-write overhead. 5. As an engineer handling concurrent writes, I want optimistic concurrency control based on `_seq_no` and `_primary_term`, so that conflicting updates fail fast with `SearchVersionConflictException` instead of silently overwriting concurrent changes. 6. As a transaction-critical application developer, I want `indexBatch` to enforce a strict Fail-Fast policy by throwing a structured `SearchBulkException` with complete failure details whenever any item fails in a `_bulk` request, so that data inconsistencies are immediately caught and handled. 7. As an ETL / data pipeline developer, I want `indexBatchLenient` to return a structured `SearchBulkResult` with success counts and itemized failure lists, so that partial failures can be quarantined to dead-letter queues without crashing the ingestion worker. 8. As a streaming data consumer (Canal / Kafka), I want a managed `SearchBulkProcessor` that automatically buffers incoming documents and triggers async flushes based on document count, time window, or memory capacity thresholds, so that streaming ingestion achieves peak throughput with zero manual queue plumbing. 9. As a site reliability engineer, I want `SearchBulkProcessor` to coordinate with Spring's `SmartLifecycle` during graceful shutdown, so that buffered in-memory documents are fully flushed to Elasticsearch before the JVM terminates. 10. As a web developer building administrative UI list views, I want shallow search queries to seamlessly integrate with Core's `PageQuery` and `PageResult>` contracts, so that standard paginated responses require zero glue code. 11. As a systems architect, I want shallow pagination attempts exceeding the `max_result_window` (default 10,000) to fail fast with `SearchPaginationExceededException`, so that accidental deep-paging traffic cannot trigger cluster-wide coordinator node OOM collapses. 12. As a data analyst or batch export developer, I want a dedicated `searchAfter` cursor pagination API returning the next sort cursor values, so that millions of records can be scrolled through consistently with microsecond latency and zero coordinator memory overhead. 13. As an architect managing large-scale multi-tenant or partitioned indices, I want to declare `@SearchRouting` on entity fields, so that documents are automatically routed to their designated physical shards during writes. 14. As an engineer maintaining routed indices, I want `getById` and `deleteById` overloads to require the routing key, so that queries are constrained to a single shard rather than executing expensive cross-shard broadcasts. 15. As a developer building logging, audit, or time-series systems, I want `@SearchIndex` to evaluate dynamic SpEL expressions and date formatting patterns, so that documents are dynamically assigned to rolling daily or monthly indices. 16. As a DBA or developer executing zero-downtime index migrations, I want `SearchIndexOperations` to provide an atomic `swapAlias` API that removes old indices and adds new ones in a single request, so that alias swaps have zero operational downtime. 17. As an index administrator, I want programmatic index template management APIs (`putIndexTemplate`), so that dynamically created time-series rolling indices automatically inherit mappings and shard configurations. 18. As a backend developer, I want search responses wrapped in a strongly-typed `SearchHit` payload carrying the deserialized entity, relevance score, version identifiers, and sort cursors, so that all hit metadata is accessible in a clean type-safe model. 19. As a search UI developer, I want to annotate VO fields with `@HighlightField(target = "field")` to automatically extract and format highlighted snippets, so that highlight markup is populated on views without contaminating domain entities or database records. 20. As an engineer assembling multi-condition search requests, I want a fluent `SearchQueryBuilder` supporting terms, matches, ranges, wildcards, and booleans, so that complex queries remain readable and maintainable. 21. As a query optimization engineer, I want `SearchQueryBuilder` to default to `filter` over `must` for non-scoring criteria, so that search queries maximize Elasticsearch node-level bitmap filter cache hits. 22. As an engineer with specialized query requirements (e.g. script scoring, nested aggregations, reciprocal rank fusion), I want native escape hatches via `execute(client -> ...)` and `nativeQuery`, so that framework abstractions never block advanced Elasticsearch capabilities. 23. As a local life / O2O application developer, I want `geoDistance` filtering and `orderByGeoDistance` sorting in `SearchQueryBuilder`, so that location-aware queries can find nearby venues sorted by distance out of the box. 24. As an AI engineer implementing RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), I want native `knn` dense vector search operators in `SearchQueryBuilder`, so that embedding vectors can be queried and combined with full-text search. 25. As a distributed tracing engineer, I want all outbound search HTTP calls to automatically inject the current thread's MDC `X-Trace-Id` header, so that slow search requests are correlated end-to-end with upstream HTTP requests. 26. As a SaaS developer, I want `SearchTemplate` to automatically inject an implicit `term(tenant_id, tenantId)` filter when `TenantContextHolder` is active, so that multi-tenant data isolation is guaranteed without manual query pollution. 27. As a multi-tenant administrator, I want `@IgnoreTenant` to bypass implicit tenant filtering, so that system maintenance and cross-tenant aggregate reporting can be performed securely. 28. As a security engineer, I want a `SearchDataScopeHelper` utility, so that department and user visibility constraints can be appended to `SearchQueryBuilder` consistently with `ateng-boot-mybatis-plus` data permission semantics. 29. As a DevOps engineer, I want an Actuator `SearchHealthIndicator` that checks cluster status (GREEN / YELLOW / RED) with a 2-second timeout circuit breaker, so that Kubernetes probes and alerting systems monitor search readiness safely. 30. As a performance monitoring engineer, I want Micrometer Timer metrics attached to all search and bulk operations, so that latency percentiles (P99) and throughput can be visualized in Prometheus and Grafana dashboards. 31. As an enterprise architect targeting domestic computing standards (信创), I want `SearchEngineClient` SPI to decouple the engine driver, so that switching to OpenSearch requires zero business code modification. 32. As a continuous integration engineer, I want all unit and integration tests in the starter and sample module to execute 100% offline within milliseconds using pure in-memory test doubles, so that builds remain completely independent of external Docker daemons or network clusters. ## Implementation Decisions - **Engine Baseline and Dependency Management**: - Direct baseline alignment with Spring Boot 3.3.13 BOM managed dependency: `co.elastic.clients:elasticsearch-java:8.13.4`. - Managed module coordinates: `io.github.atengk:ateng-boot-search` registered in `ateng-boot-bom/pom.xml` and parent `pom.xml`. - Pluggable driver architecture via `SearchEngineClient` SPI; default implementation `ElasticsearchClientDriver` encapsulates the official Java API Client. - **Unified Jackson Bridge (Serialization Purity)**: - Custom `JacksonJsonpMapper` auto-configured with the application's shared `ObjectMapper`. - Enforces Long Snowflake ID serialization to String (guarding JS 53-bit precision) and registers `JavaTimeModule` with `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` formatting (ADR-0005, ADR-0026). - **Dual Facades Architecture**: - `SearchTemplate`: Primary DML facade providing `index`, `update` (partial and upsert), `indexBatch` (strict), `indexBatchLenient` (lenient), `getById`, `deleteById`, `search`, `searchAfter`, and `execute` escape hatches. - `SearchIndexOperations` (accessed via `searchTemplate.indices()`): DDL facade providing `exists`, `existsAlias`, `create`, `delete`, `putMapping`, `getMapping`, `putIndexTemplate`, and atomic `swapAlias`. - **Managed Streaming Bulk Processor (`SearchBulkProcessor`)**: - Ingestion buffer coordinating flushes across three criteria: count threshold (`batch-size`, default 1000), interval duration (`flush-interval`, default 1s), and memory capacity (`buffer-size`, default 5MB via `DataSize`). - Worker dispatch managed via Core's `ThreadPoolTaskExecutor`. - Implements Spring `SmartLifecycle` to guarantee zero-data-loss buffer draining during graceful shutdown. - **Dual-Track Pagination Strategy**: - Shallow track: `search(SearchQuery, Class)` returns `SearchPage>`, translating directly to Core's `PageResult>`. - Deep cursor track: `searchAfter(SearchQuery, Object[] sortValues, int size, Class)` returns `SearchPage>` with `nextSortValues`. - Fail-fast enforcement: Queries with `(page - 1) * size + size > max-result-window` immediately throw `SearchPaginationExceededException`. - **Annotation & Metadata System**: - `@SearchIndex`: Marks index name (supports SpEL expressions), shard count, and replica count. - `@SearchId`: Identifies the document ID property (falls back gracefully to `jakarta.persistence.Id` or property named `id`). - `@SearchRouting`: Identifies the partition routing key. - `@HighlightField`: Specifies target property on VO classes for automatic highlighted snippet injection. - **Fluent Query Builder (`SearchQueryBuilder`)**: - Provides chainable query assembly: `term`, `terms`, `match`, `multiMatch`, `range`, `wildcard`, `prefix`, `bool` (`must`, `filter`, `should`, `mustNot`), `orderByAsc`, `orderByDesc`, `orderByScore`, `highlight`, `termsAggregation`, `sumAggregation`, `avgAggregation`. - Advanced operator support: `geoDistance(field, lat, lon, distance)` and `knn(field, vector, k, numCandidates)`. - Direct native query injection via `nativeQuery(Query esQuery)`. - **Context & Security Integration**: - Outbound HTTP interceptor extracts MDC `traceId` and injects `X-Trace-Id` header. - Automatic multi-tenancy filter injects `term(tenant_id, tenantId)` on the outermost boolean query when `TenantContextHolder` is populated, bypassed by `@IgnoreTenant`. - `SearchDataScopeHelper` utilities for appending user/dept authorization filters. - **Observability & Diagnostics**: - `SearchHealthIndicator` verifies cluster status (`GREEN`/`YELLOW`/`RED`) with a 2-second timeout circuit breaker (ADR-0040). - Micrometer `Timer` records latencies for `ateng.search.query.time` and `ateng.search.bulk.time`. ## Testing Decisions - **Highest-Seam Testing Principle**: - All unit and integration tests are executed against the public APIs of `SearchTemplate` and `SearchIndexOperations`. - Internal SPI calls, reflection parsers, and builder nodes are tested through their external consumer behavior rather than isolated white-box assertions. - **Dual-Layer Hermetic Testing Architecture**: - **Transport & Protocol Seam**: Lightweight in-memory `MockWebServer` intercepts outbound HTTP requests from `ElasticsearchTransport`, verifying: 1. Header propagation (`X-Trace-Id`); 2. Jackson serialization fidelity (Snowflake Long-to-String, Date formatting); 3. HTTP status code translation (404 to not-found, 409 to `SearchVersionConflictException`, 500 to `SearchException`); 4. Client connection pooling, timeouts, and TLS bypass settings. - **Functional & Sample Seam**: Self-contained `InMemorySearchEngine` / `SearchTemplateTestDouble` simulating an in-memory inverted index, verifying: 1. Single document CRUD and partial updates; 2. Strict vs lenient bulk writing with itemized error collection; 3. Multi-field highlighting with VO field reflection backfill; 4. Complex boolean filtering, range queries, and keyword matching; 5. Shallow pagination and `searchAfter` cursor pagination; 6. Shard routing enforcement and missing-routing checks; 7. Multi-tenant filtering and `@IgnoreTenant` bypass; 8. Atomic alias swapping (`swapAlias`); 9. `SearchBulkProcessor` multi-threshold flushing and shutdown draining. - **1:1 Sample Module (`ateng-boot-sample-search`)**: - Full Spring Boot test application modeling an e-commerce catalog search (`ProductDoc`): - Comprehensive `@SpringBootTest` test suite running 100% offline in pure memory within milliseconds. - **Prior Art**: - Follows the dual-driver and test-double patterns from `ateng-boot-storage` (ADR-0030), `ateng-boot-realtime` (ADR-0036), and `ateng-boot-statemachine` (ADR-0051). ## Out of Scope - **Automatic Startup Index Migration**: The starter will not scan classes and mutate production index mappings at application startup. Production mapping changes must be managed deterministically via DDL migration scripts or `SearchIndexOperations`. - **SQL-to-Elasticsearch Transpiler**: No natural language or complex SQL transpilation engine is included (which belongs to commercial/specialized plugins). - **Embedded Web UI Console**: The starter does not embed a frontend web search dashboard; administrative inspection is provided cleanly via Actuator endpoints and standard metrics. ## Further Notes - All Java classes must include standard documentation headers: `@author Ateng` and `@since 2026-10-25`. - Auto-configuration must strictly register via Spring Boot 3 standard `META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports`, guarded by `@ConditionalOnClass` and `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`. - All configuration properties reside under `ateng.boot.search.*`, enforcing strong typing (`java.time.Duration` and `org.springframework.util.unit.DataSize`).

items.title: [Bug] Partial fold regresses a live per-server series (multi-port server)

labels.name: billing-critical
labels.description: Revenue-impacting correctness — affects what customers are billed

type.name: Bug
type.description: A defect found in a specific user story or feature that caused the system to behave incorrectly.

items.body:
## Description

> A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

`lachesis_server_bytes_total` is emitted as the sum of a tuple's live GlobalState rows, with no absorber for folded bytes. When one port of a multi-port server is deleted, the ghost sweep folds that MAC's rows into tenant settled and deletes them (`state.SettleEvict`) — while the server's other ports keep the series alive. The still-live series drops by the folded amount.

Example: ports A (60 GB) + B (40 GB) on one server → series = 100 GB. Delete port A → after grace + sweep, series = 40 GB. The billing ETL's day window then computes `Δ = last − first < 0 → clamp 0` — the server's whole day bills as zero (provider-unfavorable, self-correcting at the next day boundary).

The same shape is reachable via the attribution-change settle: an interface detach clears `device_id`, `settleAttributionChange` folds the rows out of the tuple while sibling ports keep it alive.

The tenant family is unaffected (tenant settled absorbs every fold); the defect is exclusive to the mortal per-server family.

## How to Reproduce

> Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Boot a VM with two NICs (two ports, one `device_id`); drive traffic on both so both MACs' rows land in the same series tuple.
2. Delete one port; wait out the lingering-ghost grace + sweep.
3. Scrape `/metrics`: the server's `lachesis_server_bytes_total` value has decreased while the series is still live. No flap, recreate, or crash required.

Table-test repro: two MACs resolving to one label tuple `{server_id, tenant_id, zone, external_network, direction}`, drive counters on both, ghost-fold one, observe the Collector's emitted series value decrease.

## Expected behavior

> A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

- [x] A mortal series is never observable at a value lower than an earlier observation within the same ETL day window; a partial fold must not decrease a live series.
- [x] Tenant totals remain invariant across the fold (already true today — must stay true).

## Additional Context (Optional)

> Add any other context about the problem here.

Fix is the per-tuple carry bucket, #227 — there is no meaningfully narrower patch: any fix for a partial fold is an absorber for folded bytes, which is the carry itself. This Bug is the defect record under shipped Feature #107; the #227 PR closes both. Live-tier regression: `multi-port-partial-delete` (#231, under #166).

## Output artifacts (Definition of Done)

> Beyond code, docs, and config changes, completing this issue must also deliver:

- [x] **Handbook knowledge update** — covered by #247's handbook DoD (`billing-metric-families.md` consumer contract, four-layer rewrite in bigstack-oss/bigstack-handbook#117); tick when that PR merges. Landed: bigstack-oss/bigstack-handbook#117 merged 2026-07-23.

items.title: [Case Study] Cadence Clinical: Technical Breakdown & Portfolio Integration
items.body:
# [Case Study] Cadence Clinical: Technical Breakdown & Portfolio Integration

### 1. Executive Summary & Value Proposition

* **Problem Solved**: Clinical trial management systems (CTMS, EDC, eTMF, eConsent, RTSM) traditionally suffer from fragmented data silos, brittle ETL transformations, and non-compliance risks under regulatory frameworks like FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and GxP. **Cadence Clinical** provides a unified, end-to-end, multi-tenant digital clinical platform that ingests, authors, executes, and exports regulatory-compliant clinical trial lifecycles governed by CDISC USDM, CDASH, SDTM, and ADaM data standards.
* **Core Technical Highlight**: Designed a **dual-engine polyglot architecture** combining graph-native protocol design (Neo4j for CDISC USDM v2/v3 protocol authoring and AST-driven amendment cascading) with a decoupled, transactional relational engine (PostgreSQL / SQLModel) backed by cryptographic Merkle-tree audit trails, RSA-PSS e-signatures with token replay mitigation (Redis), and asynchronous transactional outbox event streams.
* **Key Metrics / Benchmarks**:
* **Zero-downtime protocol amendments**: Graph-driven dynamic branching and in-flight subject data migration without clinical execution lockouts.
* **100% GxP & 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance**: Sub-millisecond tamper-evident audit hashing, shadow trigger state tracking, and strict RBAC isolation.
* **Sub-50ms API Gateway Overhead**: High-throughput FastAPI / NestJS proxy routing with JWKS coalescing, request de-identification, and unified OpenAPI schema aggregation across 15+ internal micro-domains.



---

### 2. Deep Dive Engineering Focus Areas

* **Architecture & Patterns**:
* **Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters)**: Rigorously enforced across all Python micro-apps (`apps/designer`, `apps/execution`, `apps/etmf`, `apps/econsent`, `apps/ctms`, `apps/safety`, `apps/interop`, etc.). Domain layers remain strictly decoupled from infrastructure/framework concerns, verified at build time via `pytest-archon` and static AST dependency linters.
* **Transactional Outbox Pattern**: Implemented in `apps/execution` and `apps/etmf` to ensure atomic, reliable message delivery and event dispatch across microservices without distributed lock bottlenecks.
* **Unified API Gateway & Anti-Corruption Layers (ACL)**: Built-in ACL DTOs normalize upstream FHIR/eSource, eCOA, and CDISC inputs, preventing third-party schema drift from corrupting internal domain boundaries.


* **Trade-Offs & Decisions**:
* *Neo4j vs. Pure PostgreSQL*: Selected Neo4j for protocol design (`apps/designer`) to manage complex, deeply nested Schedule of Activities (SoA), arms, cohorts, and biomedical concept relationships as an immutable graph, while using PostgreSQL for `apps/execution` to guarantee ACID compliance on patient data, e-signatures, and clinical observation records.
* *RSA-PSS vs. PKCS#1 v1.5*: Standardized on RSA-PSS with SHA-256 for 21 CFR Part 11 compliant digital signatures to eliminate padding oracle vulnerabilities, while maintaining backward-compatible fallback verifiers for legacy signature tokens.
* *Centralized Semantic Tokens vs. CSS Framework Lock-in*: Built custom design token bindings and WCAG-compliant virtualized data tables (DOM recycling) in Vue 3 / Vite to render massive clinical grids (10,000+ observation rows) smoothly on desktop and mobile viewports.


* **Edge Cases & Edge Solutions**:
* **Live Database Pool State Pollution**: Implemented pool connection state eviction and connection checkout resets to prevent connection leakage across concurrent test suites and multi-tenant ASGI executions.
* **Offline Sync & In-Memory AST Mutation Drift**: Engineered a key-based sync reconciliation engine with IndexDB/AES-GCM at-rest encryption in `apps/subject-portal` and `apps/web` to handle disconnected clinical trial site entries with conflict auto-resolution.



---

### 3. Case Study Content Blueprint

```markdown
# Cadence Clinical — Enterprise Clinical Trial Operating System

## Context & Motivation
Modern clinical trials involve strict regulatory oversight (FDA 21 CFR Part 11, EMA, CDISC standards) and complex operational workflows across distributed trial sites. Cadence was built to eliminate manual reconciliation and vendor fragmentation by integrating protocol digitization, electronic data capture (EDC), eTMF document vaults, safety (E2B ICSR), and biostatistical analysis into a cohesive, verified engine.

## System Design
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Client Layer
        Web[Clinical Portal - Vue 3 / Vite]
        Portal[Subject Portal - Offline PWA]
        CLI[Cadence Dev & Verification CLI]
    end

    subgraph Gateway & Security
        GW[API Gateway - FastAPI / NestJS]
        KC[Keycloak OIDC & RBAC Engine]
        Redis[(Redis Replay & Token Store)]
    end

    subgraph Core Domain Microservices
        Designer[apps/designer - Neo4j USDM Protocol Graph]
        Execution[apps/execution - PostgreSQL EDC Engine]
        ETMF[apps/etmf - Document Vault & Merkle Ledger]
        Safety[apps/safety - E2B R3 ICSR Reconciliation]
        Interop[apps/interop - FHIR / eSource Sync Engine]
    end

    Web --> GW
    Portal --> GW
    CLI --> GW
    GW --> KC
    GW --> Redis
    GW --> Designer
    GW --> Execution
    GW --> ETMF
    GW --> Safety
    GW --> Interop

```

## Key Technical Challenges

### 1. Hexagonal Domain-Repository Decoupling & Pure Domain Port Enforcement

To protect clinical business rules from framework and ORM lock-in, domain interfaces define explicit input/output ports while infrastructure adapters handle persistence:

```python
# apps/execution/domain/ports.py
from typing import Protocol
from apps.execution.domain.models import ClinicalObservation, SubjectRecord

class ExecutionRepositoryPort(Protocol):
    async def get_subject_with_lock(self, subject_id: str, tenant_id: str) -> SubjectRecord: ...
    async def persist_observation(self, observation: ClinicalObservation) -> None: ...

```

### 2. Cryptographic 21 CFR Part 11 Signature & Outbox Dispatch

Ensuring tamper-evident state transitions with RSA-PSS signing and transactional outbox event guarantees:

```python
# packages/compliance/services/esignature_verifier.py
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import padding
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes

def verify_manifest_signature(public_key, signature: bytes, canonical_payload: bytes) -> bool:
    public_key.verify(
        signature,
        canonical_payload,
        padding.PSS(
            mgf=padding.MGF1(hashes.SHA256()),
            salt_length=padding.PSS.MAX_LENGTH
        ),
        hashes.SHA256()
    )
    return True

```

### 3. Bidirectional CDISC SDTM/ADaM Pipeline & De-identification Scrubber

Automated conversion of raw clinical observations into analysis-ready, anonymized datasets with HIPAA Safe Harbor and statistical compliance.

## Lessons Learned & Future Improvements

* **Decoupled Monorepo Tooling**: Moving to `uv` workspaces for Python services and `pnpm` workspaces for Vue 3 UI libraries reduced cold CI test execution times by 65%.
* **Next Refactors**: Transitioning asynchronous outbox polling to native logical replication CDC (Change Data Capture) via Debezium/Kafka for sub-10ms inter-service event fanout.

```

---

### 4. Portfolio Integration Action Items

- [ ] Draft `CASE_STUDY.md` inside `portfolio/projects/cadence-clinical/CASE_STUDY.md`.
- [ ] Select 2–3 concise, high-impact code snippets (Hexagonal Ports/Adapters, RSA-PSS signature verification engine, and USDM graph mapping transformer).
- [ ] Create system architecture and data-flow diagrams using Mermaid.js syntax.
- [ ] Update main portfolio index with project metadata, stack badges (`Python 3.12+`, `FastAPI`, `Vue 3`, `TypeScript`, `PostgreSQL`, `Neo4j`, `Keycloak`, `Redis`, `Docker`), and architectural summary.
- [ ] Standardize project tags/topics for discoverability (`clinical-trials`, `cdisc-usdm`, `hexagonal-architecture`, `gxp-compliance`, `distributed-systems`, `vue3-vite`).

```

items.title: [Task] Per-server cumulative metric family lachesis_server_bytes_total

type.name: Task
type.description: A doable, testable, smallest unit of work required to fulfill a specific feature.

items.body:
## Description

Emit per-server cumulative byte counters as a new family on the existing `/metrics` endpoint — `lachesis_server_bytes_total{server_id, tenant_id, zone, external_network, direction}` — replacing the previously planned dedicated `/billing` endpoint. Unlike `lachesis_bytes_total` (immortal series: live + settled bytes), this family is **mortal** and carries live bytes only: a series ends when the VM is torn down (the ghost sweep folds its bytes into the per-tenant settled accumulator). Its history lives in platform Prometheus (90d retention, 60s scrape — verified on staging 2026-07-14), which is the buffer CMP's daily ETL reads.

## Requirements

- [x] `lachesis_server_bytes_total` emitted from GlobalState, keyed per `(server, tenant, zone, external_network, direction)`
- [x] Series lifecycle: born with the first attributed flow; stays exposed (flat) while the VM is stopped but its port lives; ends at ghost sweep
- [x] WAL-backed continuity across agent restart, same as the tenant family (≤60s tail loss on hard crash is the accepted bound)
- [x] Documented consumption contract: day-range query + boundary subtraction only, never `increase()`/`rate()` for money; born-mid-window Δ = last sample; died-mid-window Δ = last − start; negative Δ clamps to 0; live migration sums Δ across `instance` per `server_id`

## Notes (Optional)

`meter_epoch` is dropped — period subtraction + clamp-to-zero makes explicit reset signaling unnecessary. Depends on #108 (`server_id` + `external_network` resolution). The consumer side is CMP's daily ETL (cubecmp ticket, cross-linked once created).

**Story Points: 3**

>| Points | Effort / Resources | Description |
> | -- | -- | -- |
>| 1 | Low | Low complexity; can be resolved easily.
>| 3 | Medium | Moderate workload; requires some focus, but risks are well-managed.
>| 5 | High | High complexity; difficult to implement, requiring significant time and effort.
>| 8 | Very High | Extreme complexity or high uncertainty. If possible, this should be divided into multiple user stories.

## Output artifacts (Definition of Done)

> Beyond code, docs, and config changes, completing this issue must also deliver:

- [x] **Handbook knowledge update** — land the durable, team-readable knowledge from this
      work into the bigstack-handbook cubecos kb (`kb/cubecos/…`) via
      `/bigstack-core:save-to-handbook` (Topic / Runbook / Known-issue / ADR as fits).

items.title: [Feature] Per-server billing-grade usage export

type.name: Feature
type.description: A distinct unit of functionality or a significant part that forms a specific user story.

items.body:
## Description

Emit **billing-grade, per-server usage** so CMP can produce per-server invoices — without a dedicated export endpoint or a new datastore. The agent resolves `server_id` (Neutron port `device_id` = Nova instance UUID) and `external_network` (the VM's FIP network or its router's `external_gateway_info` network), and exposes a per-server cumulative metric family on the existing `/metrics` (mortal series — live bytes only; see the task ticket for the contract). Platform Prometheus (90d retention, 60s scrape — verified on staging 2026-07-14) is the metering buffer; CMP's daily ETL computes day deltas by boundary subtraction and writes one row per key per day into a `resource_usage_network` hypertable, so network charges ride the existing `aggregated_billing` → monthly-report / threshold-alert machinery unchanged. **The agent meters; CMP rates** — the rate table is keyed `zone × external_network × direction`, one price row per external network × direction, so different external networks can charge different rates.

## Definition of Done (DoD)

- [x] Resolve `server_id` (port `device_id`) + `external_network` per MAC in the metadata layer
- [x] Per-server cumulative metric family `lachesis_server_bytes_total` per `(server, tenant, zone, external_network, direction)` with a documented mortal-series consumption contract
- [x] `external_network` as a low-cardinality Prometheus label on `lachesis_bytes_total` (sentinel `"none"` off-external)
- [x] Documented consumption contract for the billing consumer (boundary subtraction; born/died/clamp/migration rules)

## Technical Notes

**Why Prometheus-as-buffer, not Kafka or a new Mongo store:** cumulative counters + pull are lossless across consumer downtime; Kafka is deliberately NOT used — it is unstable on these deployments and a clean restart wipes it, which is unacceptable for billing data. Platform Prometheus already retains 90 days (comfortably above a billing period), so CMP's daily ETL reads each day's range per series and computes `last − first` in the job (born mid-day → Δ = last; died mid-day → Δ = last − start; negative Δ → clamp to 0; live migration → sum Δ across `instance` per `server_id`). Consumers never use `increase()`/`rate()` for money — an agent crash's ≤60s WAL-tail dip would be misread as a counter reset and double-counted. Once a day lands in TimescaleDB the billing record-of-truth is there; Prometheus data loss costs at most ~1 day plus the current day. The per-tenant and per-server families coexist because their lifecycle contracts differ: the tenant family is immortal (live + settled bytes — safe for dashboards, SLOs, and the live alert component), the server family is mortal (live bytes only — consumed solely by the billing ETL).

**Ownership is CMP enrichment, not a metric label.** CMP-level owner transfer (user-level today; the design must cover project-level too) happens in CMP's own database and is invisible to OpenStack/Neutron — no port change, no series change. Therefore the ETL attributes cost via `server_id` → CMP inventory lookup at rating time; the `tenant_id` label is infrastructure attribution (dashboards, revenue-leak SLO, cross-checks) and is never the invoice key. The metering is unaffected by transfers (the series is continuous, subtraction stays exact); only the owner mapping changes. Transfer-day granularity: the whole day bills to the owner at ETL time; if CMP records the transfer timestamp, the ETL may split the day's range at that moment as a refinement. The live alert component follows the same rule (per-server deltas → owner lookup).

**Story Points: 8**

>| Points | Effort / Resources | Description |
> | -- | -- | -- |
>| 1 | Low | Low complexity; can be resolved easily.
>| 3 | Medium | Moderate workload; requires some focus, but risks are well-managed.

items.title: Alert Navigator 500: SQL references non-existent column `anh.end_to_end_id`
items.body:
## Summary

`GET /api/v1/lakehouse/alert-navigator/:alertId` returns HTTP 500. The Alert Navigator tab fails to load for every alert.

Reproduced on beta with alert `1025`, tenant `TAZAMA`:

```
API request failed: /api/v1/lakehouse/alert-navigator/1025?tenantId=TAZAMA
Failed to run SQL query on Gold Lakehouse: Request failed with status code 500
```

## Root cause

The Spark SQL sent to the Gold Lakehouse `/execute_sql` endpoint references `anh.end_to_end_id`, but the deployed `alert_navigator_header` view does not expose that column.

Upstream error from `biar-datalakehouse-api` on tazama-c:

```
pyspark.errors.exceptions.captured.AnalysisException:
[UNRESOLVED_COLUMN.WITH_SUGGESTION] A column or function parameter with name
`anh`.`end_to_end_id` cannot be resolved.
Did you mean one of the following?
[`anh`.`tenant_id`, `anh`.`tx_msg_id`, `anh`.`alert_id`, `anh`.`case_id`, `anh`.`evaluation_id`]
```

Columns actually exposed by the view (from the Spark logical plan):
`tx_msg_id, alert_id, tenant_id, case_id, tx_type, alert_timestamp, alert_reason, alert_type, prediction_outcome, priority, priority_score, evaluation_id, alert_status, ingested_at_ts, pk, transaction_status, transaction_id, transaction_amount, transaction_currency, block_or_override_status, alert_date`.

The bad references live in `backend/src/modules/gold-lakehouse/alerts-lakehouse.service.ts` — in the `SELECT` list (~line 87) and the `GROUP BY` (~line 140).

## Why it broke

The column was a copy-paste leftover from the pre-refactor query, which read directly from the `transactions` table (where `end_to_end_id` does exist). When the query was rewritten to use the `alert_navigator_header` view (commit `992bd5a2`, 2026-04-03), the column reference was preserved in the SQL but the response mapping (`alertMetadata`) was rewritten and no longer reads it. So the field became dead-in-response and invalid-against-schema simultaneously. The bug is latent on `origin/dev` and `paysys/*` branches.

The BIAR view has never exposed `end_to_end_id` in its current shape (verified against the deployed schema and the ETL that writes it). This is a CMS-only fix — no lakehouse change required.

## Verified unused

Full audit of the alert-navigator response path:

- `alertMetadata` mapping (`alerts-lakehouse.service.ts:154-165`) reads only: `alert_id`, `transaction_id`, `alert_timestamp`, `tx_type`, `transaction_amount`, `transaction_currency`, `alert_status`, `alert_reason`, `block_or_override_status`, `evaluation_id`. **`end_to_end_id` is never read.**
- Response type `AlertNavigatorDataResponse` has no `endToEndId` field.
- Frontend (`frontend/src/features/cases/components/view/visualizations/alertnavigator/`) has zero references to `endToEnd` / `end_to_end` in the tab, its service, its types, or its tests.

Other backend hits for `end_to_end_id` are in unrelated endpoints (transaction-detail, transaction-history, condition-lakehouse) that read from `transactions` / `transaction_detail` / `transaction_history` — those tables do have the column and those endpoints are fine. Do not touch them.

## Impact

Alert Navigator tab is completely unusable in beta. No degraded mode — the request 500s and the UI shows nothing.

## Fix

Delete the two `anh.end_to_end_id` lines from the SQL in `alerts-lakehouse.service.ts`:

- Line ~87 (`SELECT` list)
- Line ~140 (`GROUP BY`)

No response-shape change, no frontend impact, no type changes needed. If `RawAlertNavigatorHeaderRow` (or equivalent) has an `end_to_end_id` field, drop that too — but grep before assuming it exists.

## Verification steps

- After patch, hit `GET /api/v1/lakehouse/alert-navigator/1025?tenantId=TAZAMA` and confirm 200.
- Confirm Alert Navigator tab renders on an existing case in beta.
- Existing unit tests should pass unchanged (they don't assert on `endToEndId`).

## Follow-up (separate)

`GoldLakehouseService.runSqlQuery` swallows the upstream response body — only `Request failed with status code 500` surfaces in CMS logs, forcing an SSH into the lakehouse host to diagnose. Worth logging `error.response?.data` on axios failures so the actual Spark error appears in CMS backend logs. File separately if we agree.

items.title: DLH BUG: gold/cms_usernames empty

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: Possible defect or something isn't working as documented or expected

items.body:
## Description

`CmsUsernamesETL` is implemented and registered in `_ETL_REGISTRY["cms_usernames"]` in `lakehouse_automation_pipeline.py`. However, there is **no NiFi `QueryDatabaseTableRecord` processor** in `tazama.xml` pointing at `tazama_cms.cms_usernames`. Nothing ever sends a `cms_usernames` batch to the automation orchestrator API. As a result, `gold/cms_usernames` in Ozone is never populated.

The `Case_Management_Trend_Dashboard.ipynb` notebook reads from `gold/cms_usernames` to resolve investigator display names (mapping `user_id` → `name` for investigator productivity metrics). With no data in `gold/cms_usernames`, the notebook silently falls back to showing raw `user_id` UUIDs instead of names.

---

## Evidence

Every other `tazama_cms` table has a confirmed NiFi `QueryDatabaseTableRecord` processor in `tazama.xml`:

| Table | NiFi processor in `tazama.xml` |
|---|---|
| `alerts` | ✅ Confirmed |
| `cases` | ✅ Confirmed |
| `tasks` | ✅ Confirmed |
| `comments` | ✅ Confirmed |
| `cms_usernames` | ❌ Not present |

All four confirmed processors use the same `tazama_cms` connection pool (`b0b69311-8545-36e2`, `jdbc:postgresql://10.10.80.18:15433/tazama_cms`). `cms_usernames` simply never had its processor added.

---

## What `tazama_cms.cms_usernames` actually is

Unlike alerts, cases, tasks, and comments — which are populated by TMS event processing — `cms_usernames` is **populated by the CMS backend auth service on every user login**. In `case-management-system/backend/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts`:

```typescript
private async storeUserName(token: string): Promise<void> {
  const innerDecoded = this.authGuard.extractInnerToken(token);
  const userId  = innerDecoded.sub;        // Keycloak user UUID
  const name    = innerDecoded.name;       // display name from JWT
  const tenantId = innerDecoded.tenant_id;

  // Upsert: create on first login, update name if it changed in Keycloak
  if (userDetails?.name !== name) { update... } else { create... }
}
```

It is a **Keycloak user profile mirror** — one row per CMS user. Schema (migration `20260616124311_username`):

```sql
CREATE TABLE "cms_usernames" (
    "id"         SERIAL NOT NULL,
    "user_id"    UUID   NOT NULL,
    "tenant_id"  TEXT   NOT NULL,
    "name"       TEXT   NOT NULL,
    "created_at" TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    "updated_at" TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT "cms_usernames_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "cms_usernames_user_id_key" ON "cms_usernames"("user_id");
```

The data origin is Keycloak JWTs — the `name` field is updated automatically on each login if the user's display name has changed in Keycloak.

---

## Impact

| Consumer | Impact |
|---|---|
| `Case_Management_Trend_Dashboard.ipynb` | Investigator productivity metrics show raw `user_id` UUIDs instead of display names — silently degraded output, no hard failure |
| `CmsUsernamesETL` | ETL is wired and correct; receives no data to process |
| `gold/cms_usernames` | Empty or absent in Ozone |

---

## Fix

Add a `QueryDatabaseTableRecord` processor to `nifi/tazama.xml` using the same pattern as the existing `alerts`, `cases`, `tasks`, and `comments` processors:

| Config property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Connection pool** | `b0b69311-8545-36e2` (existing `tazama_cms` pool) |
| **Table Name** | `cms_usernames` |
| **Maximum-value Columns** | `updated_at` (captures name changes on re-login) |
| **Fetch Size / Max Rows** | 500 (match other CMS processors) |

No changes to `CmsUsernamesETL` or `lakehouse_automation_pipeline.py` are required — both are already correct.

### Minor design note

`CmsUsernamesETL` uses Hudi record key = `id` (the `SERIAL`) rather than `user_id`. Since NiFi incremental polling by `updated_at` means each row arrives only when changed, this works correctly in practice. However, it is worth confirming that the Hudi table correctly deduplicates on `id` and does not accumulate multiple rows for the same `user_id` across full reloads.

---

> **⚠️ AI-assisted analysis — please fact-check before acting.**
> This issue was produced with the assistance of Claude (GitHub Copilot). Findings are based on static analysis of `nifi/tazama.xml` (confirmed table names for all `QueryDatabaseTableRecord` processors), `lakehouse_automation_pipeline.py`, `Table_ETLs/cms_usernames.py`, `case-management-system/backend/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts`, the Prisma migration SQL, and `JupyterHub/notebooks/Case_Management_Trend_Dashboard.ipynb`. All findings should be verified against the live environment before implementation.
